sections.label: Constitutional commission on Elected President
sections.summary: A 2016 constitutional commission chaired by the Chief Justice recommended ways to ensure multiracial representation in the Elected President office, noting a race-blind community as the ultimate destination.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Four years ago, in 2016, a constitutional commission chaired by the Chief Justice was set up to make recommendations on how to ensure multiracial representation in the office of the Elected President.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In its report, the commission noted as follows and I quote, "The ultimate destination for our society should be a race-blind community where no safeguards are required to ensure that candidates from different ethnic groups and periodically elected into presidential office.

sections.label: Race-blind state destination
sections.summary: The commission said it is uncertain how long the journey will take, and the speaker says there is no real quarrel about wanting a race-blind state.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The commission is of the view that it would be, especially since it is uncertain how long the journey will take." It seems to me that there is no real quarrel that we want to arrive at the destination of being a race-blind state.

sections.label: CMIO population classification
sections.summary: The Government continues classifying the population by CMIO, first used in colonial Singapore in 1824, and in 2011 enabled double-barrelled ethnicity for children of mixed marriages.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The Government continues to classify the population based on the CMIO or Chinese, Malay, Indian and Others, first used in colonial Singapore in 1824, nearly 200 years ago.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: To the Government's credit, it has recognised the increasingly numbers of mixed marriages and in 2011, enabled children of mixed marriages to be registered with double-barrelled ethnicity.

sections.label: GRC and presidential ethnic requirements
sections.summary: Since 1988 GRC teams must field candidates from designated minority communities, and recent constitutional amendments introduced an ethnic requirement for presidential elections via a hiatus-triggered mechanism.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Since 1988, the Government decided to run parliamentary elections with requirements for GRC teams to field candidates from designated minority communities.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Constitutional amendments in the last term of Parliament have introduced an ethnic requirement for presidential elections, based on a hiatus-triggered mechanism.

sections.label: EIP in HDB estates
sections.summary: The EIP was introduced in 1989 to ensure a balanced mix of ethnic groups in HDB estates and prevent racial enclaves.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The EIP was introduced in 1989, "to ensure a balanced mix of ethnic groups in HDB estates and to prevent the formation of racial enclaves".

sections.label: Effects on sellers
sections.summary: For sellers, this can significantly reduce the numbers of offers available and can affect the transaction price by as much as $100,000 in one case.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: For sellers, this can significantly reduce the numbers of offers available.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: It can also affect the transaction price by as much as $100,000 in one case I came across.

sections.label: National conversation on race issues
sections.summary: The speaker suggests a wide national conversation on race, noting the 1967 constitutional commission on minority rights and proposing a national exercise on multiracialism.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: To this end, I suggest we take the time to have a wide national conversation about how we can move forward on race issues.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Way back in 1967, the then-Chief Justice Wee Chong Jin chaired a constitutional commission on minority rights.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The time is ripe for us to have a national exercise to study what progress has been made by society since then towards multiracialism and what further steps may be taken to move towards being a more race-blind society.

sections.label: Scope of race review
sections.summary: The speaker lists six areas for a review, including CMIO classifications, race-based data disclosure, self-help groups, multiracialism in elections and HDB's Ethnic Integration Policy.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: As for the scope of such a review, I can suggest that the following be considered: one, the relevance of existing ethnic classifications such as CMIO; two, the scope for more public disclosure of race-based data; three, how not to reinforce tribal instincts in public policies and surveys; four, whether the current self-help groups should be amalgamated within a unifying national body to pool national resources on a race-blind basis; five, whether multiracialism in elections should be preserved under the current framework or can less intrusive methods be used; and six, whether HDB’s Ethnic Integration Policy should be retained and if so, how it can be modified for fairness.

sections.label: Non-Chinese Prime Minister readiness
sections.summary: The speaker asks when Singaporeans will be ready for a non-Chinese Prime Minister, saying they have risen above tribal instincts and can go further.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: When will Singaporeans be ready for a non-Chinese Prime Minister?

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Singaporeans have already risen above tribal instincts on many occasions.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: We can go further, with the right policies and signalling at the official level.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: The graduating classes of 2019, 2020 and 2021 have it tough.

sections.label: Recession impact on graduate wages
sections.summary: Overseas studies show recession-year graduates face negative wage impact for three to eight years, while an MTI 2011 study found it can be as short as three years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: According to overseas studies on previous recessions, graduates entering the job market in a recession year, experience negative impact on wages for three to eight years compared to their peers who entered in a normal year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: According to a MTI study in 2011, the negative impact can be as short as three years if job mobility is high.

sections.label: Student loan repayment relief
sections.summary: The Resilience Budget's student loan repayment relief is described as a huge relief for students.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: The Resilience Budget’s student loan repayment relief is a huge relief for our students.

sections.label: Self-employed income relief scheme
sections.summary: The Self-employed Persons Income Relief Scheme proved important in helping self-employed persons tide over this period.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: The Self-employed Persons Income Relief Scheme (SIRS) proved important to help them tide over this period.

sections.label: Unfair contract terms for freelancers
sections.summary: The passage says contract fairness is handled by the Small Claims Tribunal or civil courts, and suggests legislation on unfair contract terms and interim tripartite standards.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: The current mechanism to manage the fairness of contract terms is via the Small Claims Tribunal or a civil court process.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: We perhaps require legislation on unfair contract terms to protect freelancers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: In the interim, we need to, perhaps, have tripartite standards set in place that guides service buyers and freelancers.

sections.label: SEPs cannot form unions
sections.summary: The passage states SEPs cannot form unions under existing laws, so their rights and voices go unheard, with a bargaining power gap with platform companies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: First, according to existing laws, SEPs cannot form unions, resulting in their rights and voices not being heard.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: This is especially the case with SEPs who rely on contracts.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: There is a big gap in the bargaining power between them and the major platform companies.

sections.label: Legislation on unfair contract terms
sections.summary: The passage suggests considering legislation on unfair contract terms for freelancers and notes the President's speech highlighted concerns about socio-economic policies and jobs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: Perhaps, we should consider legislation on unfair contract terms to protect the interest of freelancers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: The President’s speech has highlighted many of the concerns of the Singaporeans who generally feel that the current socio-economic policies are not in their favour and are looking for change.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: In particular, they wish to know, why there are seemingly fewer good jobs for Singaporeans while the immigrant workforce has grown rapidly over the last two decades.

sections.label: Taxes and immigrant workforce
sections.summary: The passage asks why Singaporeans pay higher taxes when 40% of the workforce are immigrants whose taxes should have reduced the tax burden.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Why are Singaporeans paying higher and higher taxes when there are 40% of immigrants in our workforce whose taxes should have helped to reduce the tax burden?

sections.label: Foreigner share and workplace discrimination
sections.summary: The passage states foreigners are about 40% of the population after two decades of immigration and cites over 1,200 companies on the Fair Consideration Framework watch-list.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: After two decades of rapid immigration growth, the foreigner's share of our population stands at about 40% today.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: The recent announcement by MOM that there are now over 1,200 companies on the watch-list of the Fair Consideration Framework is one more confirmation of discrimination taking place at the workplace.

sections.label: Foreigner to Singaporean workforce ratio
sections.summary: The passage states the workforce is about four foreigners to six Singaporeans, and estimates six foreigners to four Singaporeans if the population reaches 10 million.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Currently, there are about four foreigners to six Singaporeans in the workforce.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: But, if the population will to reach 10 million, it is estimated that there will be six foreigners to four Singaporeans.

sections.label: Designating Offshore Companies
sections.summary: It proposes designating a group of Offshore Companies whose products and services are sold predominantly overseas and which Singaporeans lack skills to produce.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Borrowing from the experience of the Offshore and Onshore Banks in the early 1980s, we propose the designation of a group of Offshore Companies which have products and services that are sold predominantly overseas and Singaporeans do not yet have the skills to produce.

sections.label: Foreigner-to-citizen ratio cap
sections.summary: A foreigner-to-citizen ratio cap is applied to all Onshore companies and their business and functional departments.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Second, we apply a foreigner-to-citizen ratio cap to all Onshore companies and their business and functional departments.

sections.label: Reinstating localisation as KPI
sections.summary: Localisation is reinstated as a key performance indicator, with a succession plan to replace each foreign manager at the end of his visa period.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Third, we reinstate localisation as an important key performance indicator.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: We should stipulate that there is a succession plan to replace each foreign manager at the end of his visa period.

sections.label: Foreign workers in construction
sections.summary: In the construction sector, about 341,000 foreign workers make up 75% of the 457,000-strong construction labour force.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: In particular, in construction sector, we have something like 341,000 foreign workers out of the workforce of 457,000; or 75% of the construction labour force.

sections.label: Committee of Inquiry dormitory measures
sections.summary: A Committee of Inquiry recommended measures including self-contained dormitories with better amenities and a tighter regulatory framework, after high transmissibility among migrant workers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: In the aftermath, a Committee of Inquiry (COI) was formed and the COI report recommended a series of measures, such as the provision of self-contained dormitories that come with better amenities on site, tighter regulatory framework, among the many measures.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: The high transmissibility among the migrant workers at the dormitories led to a massive response and the mobilisation of resources within our system to prevent the further spread of the virus to the rest of the almost 400,000 workers at the dormitories.

sections.label: Economic Strategies Committee recommendations
sections.summary: The 2010 Economic Strategies Committee recommended moderating growth and managing foreign workforce dependence through phased foreign worker levy increases and funding support for productivity investments.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: Besides during the Little India Riot COI, the last major review on the foreign workers policy was in 2010 by the Economic Strategies Committee or ESC.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: The ESC recommended that we moderate the growth and manage the dependence on the foreign workforce through a phased increase in foreign worker levies and, in tandem, funding support for productivity investments.

sections.label: Public construction tender system change
sections.summary: The tender system for public construction projects must change, giving more weight to productive methods and less migrant worker dependence.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: The tender system for public construction projects has to change, with greater scores weightage to tenderers who use more productive construction methods and lesser dependence of migrant workers.

sections.label: En bloc development criteria tightening
sections.summary: En bloc development criteria should be tightened, allowing projects only for much older buildings or major land use changes like GFA adjustment.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: Besides consuming a significant number of migrant workers, it is also not environmentally friendly from a resource and sustainability standpoint.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: We should further tighten the criteria for en bloc development and only allow projects to go ahead for buildings that are much older or there are major changes to the land use, such as intensifying its use through the Gross Floor Area (GFA) adjustment.

sections.label: Changi T5 project under new landscape
sections.summary: Airlines may consolidate at cheaper locations and relocated major airlines may never return, raising whether the massive T5 project should proceed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: Airlines may consolidate and hub at cheaper locations and we may never be able to bring back again the major airlines that have relocated out of Changi Airport hub during this period.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: So, under this new operating landscape, should we still go ahead with the massive T5 project?

sections.label: Tightening Employment Passes and S Passes
sections.summary: In the weak labour market, foreign manpower levers can manage domestic unemployment, so MOM's tightening of Employment Passes and S Passes is welcomed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: However, in a recessionary economic environment like what we are in today where we are increasingly seeing a slack in the labour market, this lever of external foreign manpower can now be used to manage our domestic unemployment and to nudge employers to hire more locally available workers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: We have done that in past economic downturns, such as during the Global Financial Crisis in 2008 and 2009 where we also reduced the Employment Passes and S Passes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: Hence, I welcome the MOM announcements last week to tighten up our Employment Passes and S Passes, in particular, to step up scrutiny on those employers that have not been responsive to Government efforts to recruit more Singaporean PMETs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: This can be a more an effective measure than raising the qualifying salaries.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: These measures are necessary steps in response to the very weak labour market that we are in today and the likelihood of rising local retrenchments in the months ahead as the Jobs Support Scheme tapers off.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: About one-third of our labour force are foreigners.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: We have about 194,000 Employment Pass holders and 200,000 S Pass holders working in Singapore, not a small number at all.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: Two weeks ago, MAS revealed that non-citizens account for about 30% of our workforce in the financial sector.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: And for senior management roles, more than half are non-Singaporeans.

sections.label: DBS leadership Singaporean composition
sections.summary: The current DBS top management is all Singaporean except for one person, who is Malaysian and a PR.

sentences.speaker: Mr Derrick Goh (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: I did hear, Mr Speaker, Sir, the PSP Member did say of his disappointment that DBS, since the days of Mr John Olds till now, that the leadership of DBS is not to the level of the Singaporean percentage.

sentences.speaker: Mr Derrick Goh (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: I want to say that the DBS leadership of now is where all the top management is Singaporean except for one person, who is Malaysian and a PR.

sections.label: TikTok top app downloads 2018
sections.summary: By first quarter of 2018, TikTok was the number one most downloaded application on Apple's app store and Google Store globally, with 45.8 million downloads.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: By first quarter of 2018, TikTok was the number one most downloaded application on Apple's app store and Google Store globally, with 45.8 million downloads worldwide.

sections.label: Generational age ranges
sections.summary: The passage states the current age ranges of Baby Boomers, Gen X, Millennials and Gen Z, and their ages at the end of this Government's term.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: The Baby Boomers are now between 56-74 years old, Gen X is now between 40-55 years old, and the Millennials are now between 24 to 39 years old – that includes me, Gen Z, the Centennials, are now aged between eight and 23 years old.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: At the end of this Government’s term, they will be between 13 and 28.

sections.label: Tharman on evolving governance
sections.summary: In 2015 Tharman Shanmugaratnam said Lee Kuan Yew never expected Singapore's governance model to remain forever, so it must keep evolving.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: In 2015, Senior Minister Tharman Shanmugaratnam told the world before the St Gallen Symposium that our Founding Prime Minister Lee Kuan Yew never expected Singapore's model of governance to remain this way forever.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: We cannot be trapped by our history, and we have to keep evolving.

sections.label: Weariness over workplace injustices
sections.summary: Graduates expect career progression, but many residents feel the system does not cultivate local talent, with top managerial posts filled by foreigners.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: They graduate with dreams and aspirations and expect opportunities, promotions, and progression in their careers; rightfully so.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: But many of my residents have also become weary over the perceived injustices at work.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: Enough Singaporeans have begun to feel that our system does not cultivate our local talent as much as it should.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: We have all heard anecdotes like this – top managerial positions continue to be filled by foreigners who may not be even as academically qualified as our local graduates.

sections.label: Employers preferring Singaporean hires
sections.summary: Stricter Employment Pass quotas and higher minimum wages are needed, but it is more meaningful for employers to prefer Singaporeans by belief.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: Setting stricter quotas and higher minimum wages for Employment Passes are needed to address systemic vulnerabilities.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: But it is much more meaningful to have employers preferring to hire a Singaporean not just because they are obliged by our laws, but because they believe Singaporeans are worth the premium.

sections.label: Three balances for Singapore
sections.summary: The passage lists three balances: present and future, needs of every generation, and openness of society versus citizens' interests.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: First, balance between the present and the future, grasp opportunities and speed up transformation.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: Second, balance the needs of every generation, maintain equity across generations and preserve our social compact.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: Third, strike a balance between maintaining the openness of our society and safeguarding the interests of citizens.

sections.label: Digital Conversion Bonus for seniors
sections.summary: The passage asks whether a Digital Conversion Bonus, similar to the Digital Resilience Bonus, can be given to encourage seniors to use technology.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: Besides providing subsidies for senior-centred courses, purchase of devices and mobile data plans, can we also give out a "Digital Conversion Bonus" that is similar to the Digital Resilience Bonus, to encourage seniors to use technology and digital payment?

sections.label: Citizen feedback platforms redesign
sections.summary: The passage calls for rethinking citizen feedback platforms and whether they can oblige agencies to review, not just defend, policies.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: It is one way to show trust in our increasingly sophisticated people.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: We need to rethink how current citizen feedback platforms are designed and to what extent does it have the power to oblige relevant agencies to review and not just defend policies.

sections.label: Employees taking two jobs
sections.summary: The passage proposes allowing employees to take two jobs, subject to labour regulations protecting workers from overwork and regulating conflict of interests.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: For better job security, employees should be allowed to take up two jobs, subject to labour regulations to protect the workers from overwork and also to regulate potential conflict of interests.

sections.label: F&B pandemic sector impact
sections.summary: The passage notes that F&B, though seen as resilient, was badly affected during the pandemic, while supermarkets and online grocers saw a jump in orders.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: For example, from a layman's point of view, food and beverage or F&B, is always resilient because people need to eat no matter what.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: But during this pandemic, F&B is one of the most badly affected sectors.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: However, the supermarkets and online grocers see a jump in orders.

sections.label: HDB flat prices affordability
sections.summary: The passage argues HDB flat prices and the home price to annual income ratio should be adjusted downwards, with affordability measured on a tenure under 25 years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: With lower employment security and reduced market predictability, HDB flat prices should be lower and the home price to annual income ratio should be adjusted downwards to adequately reflect this new normal.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Affordability of HDB flat prices should also be measured based on a tenure that is less than 25 years.

sections.label: Recalibrating assistance scheme criteria
sections.summary: The passage asks the Ministry to fine-tune and recalibrate schemes and criteria so those with genuine needs are not completely excluded from assistance programmes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Within this group, there are those with genuine needs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: I join fellow Members – Mr Christopher de Souza, Mr Lim Biow Chuan and Mr Henry Kwek – in asking the Ministry to fine-tune and recalibrate the schemes and criteria, so that they are not completely excluded from assistance programmes.

sections.label: HDB flat prices median income
sections.summary: The passage states the Minister reiterated that HDB flats are accessible, with flat prices kept below five times median household income.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: The Minister had reiterated that our HDB flats are accessible, as our flat prices are kept at below five times our median household income.

sections.label: HDB flat price affordability
sections.summary: Lower employment security and reduced market predictability should lower HDB flat prices and the home price to annual income ratio, with affordability measured on a tenure under 25 years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: With lower employment security and reduced market predictability, HDB flat prices should be lower and the home price to annual income ratio should be adjusted downwards to adequately reflect this new normal.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Affordability of HDB flat prices should also be measured based on a tenure that is less than 25 years.

sections.label: HDB flat value convergence
sections.summary: The basis must be reassessed as some HDB flat values converge with past private housing pricing, and asset-rich-cash-poor Singaporeans have problems monetising assets during the pandemic.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: We have to reassess this basis as we can already see convergence in the value of some HDB flats with the level of pricing ascribed only to private housing properties in the past.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: There is a group of asset-rich-cash-poor Singaporeans who have problems monetising their assets during this pandemic.

sections.label: Triple Uplift for low-wage workers
sections.summary: Singapore helps low-wage workers through a Triple Uplift formula of Progressive Wage Model, Workfare Income Supplement and National Wage Council recommendations.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: In Singapore, our way of helping the low-wage workers is via, what I will call, the “Triple Uplift” formula: Progressive Wage Model or PWM, plus Workfare Income Supplement or WIS, and, of course, National Wage Council (NWC) recommendations – using all these three – to uplift their wages.

sections.label: Wage growth of lowest percentile
sections.summary: Through the Triple Uplift formula, wages of the lowest 20th percentile grew 4.4% annually from 2014 to 2019, compared to 2.3% in the preceding five years.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: Through this "Triple Uplift" formula, the wages of the lowest 20th percentile have seen a higher annual growth rate of 4.4% from 2014 to 2019, as compared to 2.3% in the preceding five years.

sections.label: PWM wage rises in sectors
sections.summary: PWM, mandated in cleaning, security and landscaping, helped raise wages of workers in these three sectors by around 30% between 2013 and 2018.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: Currently mandated in the cleaning, security and landscaping sectors, PWM has helped to substantially raise the wages of workers in these three sectors by around 30% between 2013 and 2018.

sections.label: Three sectors worker coverage
sections.summary: With overtime pay and AWS or bonuses this could be higher, but these three sectors account for about 78,000 workers, about 15% of the lowest 20th percentile.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: With overtime pay and AWS or Bonuses, this could actually be higher.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: However, I must say that these three sectors account for only about 78,000 workers, representing only about 15% of all the workers in the lowest 20th percentile of salary ranges.

sections.label: Lift and escalator PWM 2022
sections.summary: Tripartite efforts before COVID-19 will make a PWM mandatory for the lifts and escalator sector by 2022.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: Some of our efforts undertaken by the tripartite partners prior to COVID-19 will lead to the lifts and escalator sector having a PWM becoming mandatory by 2022.

sections.label: Sectoral wage benchmark first step
sections.summary: Towards universal PWM, a sectoral wage benchmark could be explored first in sectors with no regulatory levers to mandate a PWM.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: In moving towards universal PWM, we should explore setting a sectoral wage benchmark for companies as a first step in sectors where there are currently no regulatory levers to mandate a PWM.

sections.label: Workfare Income Supplement enhancements
sections.summary: WIS was enhanced with the qualifying income gap raised to $2,300 monthly and maximum payout increased to $4,000 yearly.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: Hence, to further boost wages across the board for many low-wage workers in Singapore beyond the PWM, the Workfare Income Supplement or WIS scheme is an important one.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: This was recently enhanced with the qualifying income gap raised to $2,300 a month and the maximum payout increased to $4,000 per year.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: Today, WIS contributes to almost a third of the take-home pay of our low-wage workers.

sections.label: NWC recommendations for low-wage workers
sections.summary: NWC recommendations in March 2020 sought to safeguard low-wage workers, particularly front-line COVID-19 workers earning up to $1,400 monthly.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: The NWC recommendations early this year – in March 2020 – have sought to further safeguard the interests of our low-wage workers, particularly those in the front line of our COVID-19 response and earning a basic monthly salary of up to $1,400.

sections.label: NWC reconvening earlier
sections.summary: Tripartite leaders agreed to reconvene NWC later this year, earlier than usual, to review wage guidelines given COVID-19's impact.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: Given the profound impact of COVID-19 on the economy, companies and workers, the tripartite leaders have agreed to reconvene NWC again later this year, much earlier than the usual time frame to review the wage guidelines.

sections.label: Low-wage wage growth and PWM
sections.summary: From 2013 to 2018 low-wage workers' wages rose about 30%, but PWM is mandated only in cleaning, security and landscape sectors.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: From 2013 to 2018, the wages of these low-wage workers have increased by about 30%.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: However, PWM is only mandated in the cleaning, security and landscape sectors, which benefits 78,000 low-wage workers and represents 15% of all low-wage workers.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: PWM will be made mandatory for the Lift and Escalator sector in 2022.

sections.label: Workfare Special Payment for low-wage workers
sections.summary: The Workfare Special Payment of $3,000 will help low-wage workers tide through this difficult period.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: In addition, the Workfare Special Payment of $3,000 will help low-wage workers to tide through this difficult period.

sections.label: NWC recommendation for low-wage workers
sections.summary: If an employer is doing well and can raise salaries across the board, NWC recommends up to $50 increase for low-wage workers.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: Conversely, if the employer is doing well and able to raise the salaries across the board, NWC recommends up to $50 increase for low-wage workers.

sections.label: Worker's family hardship and adjusted hours
sections.summary: A worker who became sole breadwinner after his parents lost jobs took extra delivery work, so his working hours were adjusted instead of releasing him.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: As a result and after quite some digging, we discovered that he had recently become the sole breadwinner in a family of seven, and that was because both his parents had lost their jobs because of COVID-19.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: In order to support his family, extended family actually, he had to take on extra work as a delivery driver from 10.00 pm to 4.00 am every day.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Understanding his story helped me empathise with his situation and allowed us to work out a favourable solution, instead of releasing him on the basis of moonlighting and poor performance, we decided to adjust his working hours to allow him to come in to work later in the day and make up for the lost time over the weekends.

sections.label: Close neighbour versus distant relative
sections.summary: The saying states that a close neighbour is better than a distant relative.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: As the saying goes, 远亲不如近邻, better a close neighbour, than a distant relative.

sections.label: Resolving economic crisis and redefining job
sections.summary: While overcoming the outbreak, we must resolve the COVID-19 economic crisis and relook our definition of a job.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: While we work to overcome challenges of the outbreak, we must work even harder to resolve the economic crisis brought forth by COVID-19.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: I feel that while we actively promote training and transformation amongst workers so that they are equipped with future skills, and advocate for diversity at the workplace, we should also relook our definition of a "job".

sections.label: Reviewing freelancer welfare and employment concept
sections.summary: As the gig economy grows, the policy framework must be reviewed to safeguard freelancers' Medisave and retirement funds, and human resource policies adjusted.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: In the future, the gig economy will become a common trend, and there will be greater needs from freelancers.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Therefore, there is now a greater need for us to review the policy framework to safeguard the welfare of freelancers, to ensure they have adequate Medisave and retirement funds.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: This is why we also need to adjust our human resource policies and change the concept of employment, even as we embark on economic transformations.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Only then can we attract more Singaporeans to take on jobs in the emerging industries and to build a more inclusive and diverse workplace with a Singaporean Core.

sections.label: Resident unemployment rate 3.9%
sections.summary: The resident unemployment rate is 3.9% in the second quarter, better than many countries.

sentences.speaker: Mr Derrick Goh (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Our resident unemployment rate is at 3.9% in the second quarter, faring better than many countries.

sections.label: Self-employed Person Income Relief Scheme
sections.summary: SIRS was announced in March to support self-employed workers affected by COVID-19, with over 100,000 eligible for $3,000 payouts over three quarters.

sentences.speaker: Mr Derrick Goh (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The Self-employed Person Income Relief Scheme or SIRS was announced in March to support self-employed workers affected by COVID-19.

sentences.speaker: Mr Derrick Goh (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Over 100,000 were identified as eligible for cash payouts of $3,000 for three quarters.

sections.label: Property annual value criteria
sections.summary: A property annual value criterion of more than $21,000 excludes residents from getting the relief.

sentences.speaker: Mr Derrick Goh (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: An example is the use of the property annual value criteria of more than $21,000 that excludes residents from getting the relief.

sections.label: Pandemic relief and reserves
sections.summary: SIRS and construction sector efforts arose from the pandemic, with almost S$100 billion invested in relief programmes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Derrick Goh (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Both the SIRS and the effort on the construction sector are great examples of actions that arose out of this pandemic.

sentences.speaker: Mr Derrick Goh (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: I am proud that our country was able to dig deep, accessed its reserves and invested almost S$100 billion in relief programmes to help us steer through this crisis.

sections.label: SIRS implementation gaps and exclusions
sections.summary: SIRS helped self-employed workers but some faced rejection without clear explanation, exclusions due to simplified criteria, and migrant workers were quarantined again.

sentences.speaker: Mr Derrick Goh (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: For example, the SIRS disburses cash pay-outs to the self-employed and has been of great help to them, but some of them are also disappointed and unhappy over perceived unfairness due to minor issues in policy implementation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Derrick Goh (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: For instance, some applicants may have been rejected by the Government because they did not meet the eligibility criteria, but were not given a clear explanation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Derrick Goh (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: There are also some people who have been impacted by the COVID-19 outbreak but are excluded from the scheme due to overly simplified criteria, and these include residents who live in private properties as well as hawkers who did not file their taxes in time.

sentences.speaker: Mr Derrick Goh (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: In another example, even though the Government has rolled out many measures to facilitate the resumption of construction projects, some migrant workers still ended up being quarantined again due to gaps in policy implementation.

sections.label: Good policies need good execution
sections.summary: Policies are generally good but need to be executed well to truly benefit people.

sentences.speaker: Mr Derrick Goh (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: In general, we have good policies, but they need to be executed well to truly benefit our people.

sections.label: Four Budgets of support
sections.summary: The Government introduced four Budgets of support costing close to $100 billion, with Jobs Support Scheme salary support up to 75%.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: The Government has already introduced four Budgets of support costing close to $100 billion.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: Salary support under the Jobs Support Scheme went up to 75% during the circuit breaker, far higher than the 12% under the Jobs Credit Scheme in 2009.

sections.label: NTUC Progressive Wage Model
sections.summary: NTUC pioneered the Progressive Wage Model in 2012, which now covers about 80,000 workers in cleaning, security, and landscaping.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: NTUC pioneered Progressive Wage Model or PWM, in 2012, which now covers about 80,000 workers in the cleaning, security, and landscaping sectors.

sections.label: PWM sector wage growth
sections.summary: In the last five years, workers in PWM sectors saw cumulative wage growth of around 30%, compared to 21% at the median.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: In the last five years, workers in PWM sectors have seen cumulative wage growth of around 30%.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: This is compared to 21% for workers at the median.

sections.label: Workfare coverage and payouts
sections.summary: Earlier this year, Workfare coverage was expanded and payouts raised, and a $3,000 Workfare Special Payment helped cushion COVID-19's impact on lower income workers.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: Earlier this year, we expanded Workfare coverage and raised payouts.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: A Workfare Special Payment of $3,000 has also helped to cushion the impact of COVID-19 on lower income workers.

sections.label: Introducing a PWM Mark
sections.summary: The Government will work with tripartite partners to introduce a PWM Mark to give this effort a bigger push.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: To give this effort a bigger push, the Government will work with the tripartite partners to introduce a PWM Mark.

sections.label: EP and S Pass growth
sections.summary: In the last five years, 2014 to 2019, the number of EP and S Pass holders grew on average less than 9,000 annually.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: In the last five years, 2014 to 2019, the number of EP and S Pass holders has grown on average, less than 9,000 annually.

sections.label: Drop of 22,000
sections.summary: Between January and July this year, the figure has dropped by 22,000.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: Between January and July this year, it has dropped by 22,000.

sections.label: Retrenchments conducted fairly
sections.summary: In vast majority of cases, retrenchments have been conducted fairly and responsibly.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: In vast majority of the cases, retrenchments have been conducted fairly and responsibly.

sections.label: Resorts World foreign employee bar
sections.summary: At Resorts World, a foreign employee must meet a higher performance bar than his local colleague to be retained.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: In the case of Resorts World, for example, a foreign employee must meet a higher performance bar than his local colleague to be retained.

sections.label: EP and S Pass emphasis
sections.summary: In last week's EP and S Pass tightening announcement, MOM will place additional emphasis on whether the employer has kept up support of local PMETs.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: In last week's announcement of the tightening of EP and S Pass requirements, one aspect was not prominently reported.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: We had made clear that in evaluating EP and S Pass applications, MOM will place additional emphasis on whether the employer has kept up its support of local PMETs in its employment.

sections.label: Work pass privileges suspended
sections.summary: This year alone, 90 employers have had work pass privileges suspended for Fair Consideration Framework infringements.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: And this is one of the reasons why the company is in Singapore in the first place.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: This year alone, 90 employers have had their work pass privileges suspended because of infringements under the Fair Consideration Framework or FCF.

sections.label: 12-month hiring penalty
sections.summary: As a penalty, it will not be able to hire or renew EP holders for 12 months.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: As a penalty, it will not be able to hire or renew EP holders for 12 months – one full year.

sections.label: Employers scrutinised under FCF
sections.summary: Since 2016, over 1,200 employers were scrutinised under the FCF, while about 40,000 applied for EPs in five years.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: Since 2016, more than 1,200 employers have been scrutinised under the FCF.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: To put the number into context, in the last five years, about 40,000 employers have applied for EPs, at least once.

sections.label: EP applications rejected or withdrawn
sections.summary: 3,200 EP applications were rejected, withheld or withdrawn, but these employers hired over 4,800 Singaporean PMETs.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: In all, 3,200 EP applications have been rejected or withheld by MOM, or withdrawn by employers while they were being scrutinised.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: But these employers have hired more than 4,800 Singaporean PMETs as a result.

sections.label: Penalty on hiring work passes
sections.summary: As a penalty, the company cannot hire or renew work passes for 18 months.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: As a penalty, the company will not be able to hire or renew work passes for 18 months – one and a half years.

sections.label: Action on false declarations
sections.summary: In five years, action was taken in over 1,200 false declaration or kickback cases, securing nearly 388 convictions through prosecution.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: In fact, in the last five years, we have taken action in over 1,200 cases of false declarations or kickbacks and secured nearly 388 convictions through prosecution.

sections.label: Raising EP and S Pass salaries
sections.summary: Due to drastic job market changes, MOM announced it would further raise EP and S Pass salary requirements.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: However, because there were drastic and rapid changes in the job market over the past few months, MOM had to take further action.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: Therefore, MOM announced last week that we would further raise the EP and S Pass salary requirements.

sections.label: Foreign professionals on Employment Pass
sections.summary: Foreign professionals on an EP make up less than 15% of PMETs in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: On the other hand, the number of foreign professionals that come to Singapore on an EP is relatively smaller.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: They make up less than 15% of PMETs in Singapore.

sections.label: Local PMETs versus EP holders
sections.summary: Local PMETs outnumber EP holders seven to one, and the figure dropped by 22,000 in the first seven months of this year.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: In the first seven months of this year, it dropped by 22,000.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: In fact, local PMETs outnumber EP holders 7:1.

sections.label: Tilting balance to local PMETs
sections.summary: The passage asks what can be done to further tilt the balance in favour of local PMETs, including those in their 40s and 50s.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: What then can we do to further tilt the balance in favour of local PMETs, including those in their 40s and 50s?

sections.label: One billion dollar manpower push
sections.summary: One billion dollars is set aside for Singapore's biggest push to help employers stretch manpower budgets and expand local hiring.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: With $1 billion set aside, this is Singapore’s biggest push ever to help employers stretch their manpower budgets and expand the hiring of locals.

sections.label: PCPs training and salary support
sections.summary: PCPs give employers training and salary support to re-skill and hire mid-career local jobseekers, with higher support for workers aged 40 and above.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: PCPs provide employers with generous training and salary support to re-skill and hire mid-career local jobseekers, with higher support for mature workers aged 40 and above.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: This also benefits the PCP employees, with about nine in 10 remaining employed 24 months after being placed, and about seven in 10 earning higher wages after starting in their new jobs.

sections.label: PMET, EP, PR and citizen numbers
sections.summary: The passage reports average yearly increases: 35,000 local PMETs from 2014 to 2019, 50,000 EPs and PRs, 20,000 citizens and 30,000 new PRs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
sentences.text: The Minister mentioned that from the period of 2014 to 2019, the average increase of PMETs for locals is 35,000.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: He mentioned the number of 50,000 of increase every year in EPs and PRs.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: I think we have regularly reported that, on average, in the last couple of years – not the entire few decades that Mr Leong may be referring to – every year, the number of Singapore citizens goes up by around 20,000 and then the number of new PRs is about 30,000.

sections.label: Citizen marriages with non-citizens
sections.summary: The passage states that in today's context, one in three marriages involving a citizen also involves a non-citizen.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: In case Mr Leong has not noticed, if I remember correctly from my population portfolio, I believe, in today's context, one in three marriages involving a citizen also involves a non-citizen.

sections.label: Rise in local PMET jobs
sections.summary: Local PMET jobs rose from three in 10 to six in 10 locals from the 1990s to today, called a remarkable accomplishment.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: Or do we look at the broader picture and ask ourselves whether over the last few decades from the 1990s to what it is today, from three in 10 locals in PMET jobs, to six in 10 locals in PMET jobs, is an amazing accomplishment not so easily achieved elsewhere – a remarkable accomplishment.

sections.label: Pressure on PMET job market
sections.summary: The speaker says no distinction is made between original and new Singaporeans, but notes pressure in the PMET job market.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
sentences.text: But I would also like to stress that what we are talking about here is actually the pressure on our people, whether it is the original Singaporeans or the new Singaporeans, we actually do not make that distinction.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
sentences.text: However, if the Minister is saying that there is an increase of 50,000 every year and you have only an increase of 35,000 in PMETs, then we cannot deny the fact that there is pressure in the job market of the PMETs.

sections.label: Dependents of PRs and citizens
sections.summary: The speaker clarifies that the Minister said dependents from the 50,000 PRs and new citizens number more than 15,000.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: It is fine if you do not want to answer the questions posed to you.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
sentences.text: I just want to clarify that what the Minister said is that the number of dependents from the 50,000 PRs and new citizens, is more than 15,000.

sections.label: Helping Singaporeans stay employed
sections.summary: The question is what it takes to help Singaporeans stay employed, avoid unemployment, achieve income growth and retirement adequacy.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: Ultimately, we have to ask ourselves what does it take to help Singaporeans stay in employment, stay out of unemployment and over time, to achieve income growth, to achieve retirement adequacy.

sections.label: Reducing reliance on foreigners
sections.summary: The speaker says yes if good outcomes can continue without more EP and S Pass holders, less unproductive manpower-intensive work, and more Singaporeans in good jobs.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: If we can do so without adding to the number of EP and S Pass holders for that matter, continue to deliver good outcomes, help Singaporeans enjoy higher employment, low unemployment, income growth and retirement adequacy without using more foreigners as complements to our workforce, if we can reduce the reliance on unproductive manpower-intensive methods of work in some of our business sectors today, if we can groom more Singaporeans to take up the good jobs that we are creating, then of course, the answer is yes.

sections.label: Fall in EP and S Pass holders
sections.summary: In the first seven months of this year, the total number of EP and S Pass holders fell by 22,000.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: Supposing we can bring it down to zero or even negative which is what has happened in the first seven months of this year.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: I reported to Members, that in the first seven months of this year, total number of EP and S Pass holders has gone down by 22,000.

sections.label: MOM handling non-nationality discrimination
sections.summary: The passage asks how MOM handles discrimination on grounds other than nationality, such as gender, and whether anti-discrimination legislation could help.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: My question would really be: how does MOM handle cases where the axis of discrimination is in fact not nationality but something else, for example, gender?

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: What else can be done and how does MOM handle those cases.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: This is really where, perhaps something like an anti-discrimination legislation could provide a solution.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: But how is that being addressed right now?

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: And if we find evidence of it, we can also curtail their work pass privileges.

sections.label: Work pass penalty versus fine
sections.summary: The passage states that not many businesses can operate with a 100% local workforce, so a work pass penalty is more painful than a fine.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: Not so many businesses are able to operate with a 100% local employment workforce.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: So, this kind of a penalty is actually much more painful than if we were to say, introduce a fine.

sections.label: Singapore senior employment rate comparison
sections.summary: The passage states that Singapore's senior employment rate is above that of the UK.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: You compare ourselves to a country like the UK.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: But if you look at their senior employment rate and compare it to Singapore, we are above.

sections.label: Women's labour force participation
sections.summary: The passage states women's labour force participation in Singapore is lower than desired but far higher than in some jurisdictions with gender discrimination law.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: Gender discrimination – look at women's participation in the labour force in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: It is not as high as we would like it to be but it is far higher than in some jurisdictions that claim to have gender discrimination law.

sections.label: Reason for reduction to zero
sections.summary: The passage states that the reduction to almost zero was because unemployment rates shot up.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
sentences.text: Of course, we all know that the reason why they were reduced to almost zero was because unemployment rates shot up.

sections.label: Singaporeans' biggest worry is jobs
sections.summary: The passage states that jobs are the biggest worry for most Singaporeans and notes efforts by Government agencies and volunteers to reach jobseekers.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: The biggest worry most Singaporeans have now is jobs.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: I am heartened by the efforts of the various Government agencies and volunteers to reach out to jobseekers.

sections.label: Career coaches deployment and recruitment
sections.summary: The Ministry has deployed career coaches and needs to recruit and train more for the crisis and future.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: The Ministry has deployed career coaches to advise and guide them.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: From deciding which sectors to explore to drafting resumes – having a trained and well-informed counselor by your side can really make the difference between failure and success.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: We need to recruit and train more career coaches because they are needed not only during this crisis but also in the future, as job cycles become shorter, even as people live longer and work well into their 60s or 70s.

sections.label: Progressive Wage Model wage effects
sections.summary: The Progressive Wage Model has lifted wages for workers in limited sectors.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: The Progressive Wage Model or PWM has lifted wages for workers in limited sectors.

sections.label: Hiring biases and MOM oversight
sections.summary: The speaker urges MOM to rein in errant employers, step up hiring oversight, and adopt a consultative process with employers.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: In other cases, the hiring biases could be due to the inherent cultures and working environments within the organisations, which may make it more favourable for foreign employees to land jobs and thrive.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: I urge MOM to do more to rein in errant employers.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: While I appreciate and support the higher qualifying salaries for Employment Passes, more can be done as I feel the measure is not enough.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: We need to step up oversight of the hiring processes, the actual hires and the types of roles that are going to locals and foreigners.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Next, I would like to request that going forward, MOM and MTI adopt a consultative process to work more closely together with employers to find out what difficulties they have faced in hiring the right local citizen talents for the jobs and to work through these issues in a constructive manner.

sections.label: MOM and MSF job termination alerts
sections.summary: The speaker hopes MOM can work with MSF to be alerted in the event of any job termination.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: In addition to greater publicity and a bigger presence in our heartlands, I hope MOM can work with MSF to be alerted in the event of any job termination.

sections.label: MOM and MSF job termination alerts
sections.summary: The speaker hopes MOM can work with MSF to be alerted in the event of any job termination.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: In addition to greater publicity and more satellite career centres in our heartlands, I hope the Ministry of Manpower can work with the Ministry of Social and Family Development to be alerted in the event of any job termination.

sections.label: Financial sector jobs for Singaporeans
sections.summary: About 22,000 financial sector jobs were created over the past five years, with 15,000 going to Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: About 22,000 financial sector jobs were created over the past five years, with 15,000 going to Singaporeans.

sections.label: Financial services workforce composition
sections.summary: The financial services sector employs about 171,000 workers, with Singaporeans at 70% overall and 44% of senior roles.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: At 13% of our economy, the financial services sector employs about 171,000 workers.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: Based on MAS’ estimates, about 70% of the workforce are Singaporeans, 14% PRs and 16% work pass holders.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: If we zoom in on the more senior roles, Singaporeans account for 44%, PRs 20% and work pass holders 36%.

sections.label: Concern over senior positions
sections.summary: A concern arose that 44% of senior positions going to Singaporeans could be too low.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: When MAS released its figures recently, one concern came up, which was that 44% of senior positions going to Singaporeans could be too low.

sections.label: Senior roles in banks
sections.summary: In 2019, Singaporeans held 70% of senior roles in retail banks' local functions and about 40% in non-retail banks.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: As MAS has shared recently, in 2019, for senior roles in retail banks' local functions, Singaporeans accounted for 70%.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: In the non-retail banks, where there is a higher concentration of regional and global functions, the proportion is lower, at about 40%.

sections.label: Growth in senior positions
sections.summary: From 2014 to 2019, senior positions in Singapore grew from 3,900 to 5,900, with Singaporeans' share rising from 1,700 to 2,600.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: To illustrate, MAS estimates that from 2014 to 2019, the number of senior positions sited in Singapore grew from 3,900 to 5,900.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: And the absolute number of senior jobs that went to Singaporeans increased correspondingly from 1,700 to 2,600.

sections.label: Finance Associate Management Scheme
sections.summary: The Finance Associate Management Scheme supports financial institutions to hire and groom Singaporeans through structured talent development programmes.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: One such scheme is the Finance Associate Management Scheme or FAMS, which supports financial institutions to hire and	groom Singaporeans through structured talent development programmes.

sections.label: Offshoring lower value-add functions
sections.summary: Offshoring lower value-add business functions employing foreign manpower is a possible approach, but must be approached with caution.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: Another possible approach is to encourage the offshoring of certain business functions that are lower in value-add, and which employ a disproportionate share of foreign manpower.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: But any such measures must be approached with a lot of caution, because it may not be straightforward to dissect a business into high value-add and low value-add, and then outsource the latter.

sections.label: Singapore financial centre and Singaporeans
sections.summary: Singapore is emerging as a global financial nerve centre with most jobs going to Singaporeans, but competition is relentless.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: The more widely held view, I think, understands the international character of our financial centre, but wants to see Singaporeans do better, with greater assurance of fair hiring practices that put us on a level playing field and these are valid concerns.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: The fact is – small and young as we are, we are emerging as one of the nerve centres in the global financial system, sharing a stage with places like New York, London and Hong Kong, and with the largest chunk of jobs going to Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: But the competition is relentless and our competitors are hungry.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: So, this is not about growth at all costs, or accepting "trade-offs" for the sake of growth, but about whether as a people we can strengthen our place in the financial world, hold our own, develop the expertise, seize the opportunities, to make Singaporean lives better.

sections.label: Partnership to grow financial centre
sections.summary: Working together to strengthen the international financial centre in Asia, grow Singaporean talents and improve lives.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: In turn, we work with them to catalyse new areas of growth and create new opportunities for Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: We must continue to work in concert, to further strengthen this partnership, grow this international financial centre in Asia, invest in and grow our Singaporean talents, and make lives better through the generations.

sections.label: Expanding Progressive Wage Model
sections.summary: Many workers can still benefit from the framework, and Government is keen to expand the Progressive Wage Model into more sectors.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mohd Fahmi Aliman (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: While much has been achieved by the tripartite partners, there are still many workers who stand to benefit from this framework.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mohd Fahmi Aliman (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: I am encouraged to hear that Government is keen to expand Progressive Wage Model or PWM into more sectors.

sections.label: Enhancing WIS Scheme payouts
sections.summary: Workfare Special Payment will be extended, and Government is urged to enhance the WIS Scheme with higher payouts for essential services workers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mohd Fahmi Aliman (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: In the recent Ministerial Statement by Deputy Prime Minister Heng Swee Keat, the Workfare Special Payment will be extended to include more workers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mohd Fahmi Aliman (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: While this effort should be applauded, let us not rest on our laurels and continue to work to enhance the WIS Scheme to benefit more workers and their families and strengthen our social security net.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mohd Fahmi Aliman (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: I urge Government to consider suggestions such as providing a higher WIS payout to workers in the essential services to acknowledge their social value and to have greater differentiation in the payouts for full-time versus part-time workers.

sections.label: Youth mental health issues
sections.summary: A study found Singaporeans aged 18 to 34 more likely to have mental health issues, with more youths seeking help during COVID-19.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mohd Fahmi Aliman (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: In a recent study done by the Institute of Mental Health last year, it was revealed that Singaporeans aged between 18 and 34 were more likely to have experienced mental health issues.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mohd Fahmi Aliman (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: Silver Ribbon Singapore, an organisation working to dispel myths surrounding mental illness, also observed an increase in youths coming forward to seek help during the COVID-19 outbreak for depression and anxiety.

sections.label: Madrasah academic performance improvement
sections.summary: Since Compulsory Education and the Joint Madrasah System, madrasah academic performance improved, with 99.6% of PSLE students suitable for secondary school.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mohd Fahmi Aliman (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: Since the introduction of Compulsory Education and the formation of the Joint Madrasah System (JMS), the academic performance of madrasahs has improved significantly.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mohd Fahmi Aliman (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: Between 2017 and 2019 alone, the number of PSLE students assessed to be suitable for secondary school rose to 99.6% and the percentage of students with at least three or five 'O' level passes is close to matching the national average.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mohd Fahmi Aliman (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: In addition, with the M3 Framework, madrasah students have also been able to understand the needs and concerns of the community.

sections.label: Madrasahs and COFA recommendations
sections.summary: Madrasahs must anticipate emerging community challenges, and the speaker looks forward to implementing COFA's recommended ideas.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mohd Fahmi Aliman (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: Madrasahs will thus need to anticipate the emerging challenges and needs of the community.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mohd Fahmi Aliman (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: I look forward to the implementation of the recommended ideas put forth by Committee on Future Asatizah or COFA.

sections.label: Three issues spoken on
sections.summary: The speaker spoke on essential workers' wages and welfare, care-givers and youth mental health, and uplifting Madrasah education for national goals.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mohd Fahmi Aliman (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: Today, I spoke on three issues, first acknowledging the social value of our essential workers through better wages, welfare and recognition; second, supporting the care-givers and addressing mental health issues especially for our youths; and thirdly, uplifting the Madrasah education towards achievement of national goals such as social cohesion and economic progress.

sections.label: Redundancy insurance scheme proposal
sections.summary: An earlier redundancy insurance scheme would have built up funds and acted as an automatic stabiliser during a crisis.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Many of us in this house would have been inundated by appeals from Singaporeans whose SIRS' applications have been turned down.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Had we instituted a redundancy insurance scheme much earlier and given it time to build up funds, that would have acted as an automatic stabiliser kicking in during a crisis without Government discretion and reducing the need for executive disbursement surveyed.

sections.label: Help schemes involve multiple steps
sections.summary: Seeking help through SIRS, ComCare, MediFund or HDB resale levy reduction involves multiple steps, forms and interviews.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Appealing for help when in distress for example, through schemes like SIRS, ComCare, MediFund and even a reduction in HDB resale levy when downgrading, involves multiple steps.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: One often needs to come down physically to a meeting, bringing multiple forms of the applicant may, or may not have – though to be fair, exceptions will be made for those with disabilities as clarified in an exchange I had in this House last term.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Sometimes, the officers processing the claim will ask to interview relatives to ascertain if the applicant receives family support.

sections.label: Singaporeans, skills and job design
sections.summary: The speaker asks why Singaporeans lack requisite skills for desirable jobs and why re-skilling into sunrise sectors is slow.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: There are some jobs that Singaporeans are not attracted to – based on current job design.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: But have we thought hard enough about why not enough Singaporeans have the requisite skills for some of these desirable jobs?

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Why Singaporeans who faced skill obsolescence and so-called sunset-industry jobs are not re-skilling fast enough to sunrise sectors?

sections.label: Foreign worker source countries changing
sections.summary: Ms He Ting Ru said countries exporting foreign workers may not stay poor and may stop coming to Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: As my colleague Ms He Ting Ru said in one of our panel discussions, the countries exporting foreign workers today may not remain poor forever.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: There may come a day when they do not want to come to Singapore to do such jobs or, at least, not at current rates of pay.

sections.label: Singapore absent from entrepreneurship index
sections.summary: Singapore is not featured as a participating country in the global entrepreneurship monitors' Entrepreneurial Eco-system Quality Composite Index.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In the global entrepreneurship monitors, Entrepreneurial Eco-system Quality Composite Index, for example, Singapore is simply not featured as a participating country.

sections.label: Supporting suppliers in ASEAN
sections.summary: Companies could be supported in helping local suppliers and partners in Indonesia and Vietnam adopt such practices, aiding Singapore FDI and public diplomacy.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Our companies could also be supported in their efforts to help their local suppliers and partners adopt such practices in ASEAN countries like Indonesia and Vietnam that will help ensure that Singapore FDI in ASEAN is welcome, and may even bolster our public diplomacy efforts, and the Singapore National brand in our ASEAN neighbourhood.

sections.label: Mandatory fortnightly retrenchment data
sections.summary: Retrenchment data reporting should be mandatory even for micro-SMEs under 10 persons, published fortnightly during crises for a more comprehensive data set.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In times of crisis, more frequent data on how many people are losing their jobs would help inform decision-making and public debate.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: We should make retrenchment data reporting mandatory even for micro-SMEs employing less than 10 persons.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
