sentences.text: With the data published every fortnight, during crises like the current one, this would provide a more comprehensive, sensitive and useful data set in times of crises, compared with current unemployment reporting or even the job situation report published on 11 August.

sections.label: Stronger civil society for resilience
sections.summary: A stronger civil society with a louder voice may bring diversity in debate that enhances resilience rather than depending on a one-party-dominated state.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: A stronger civil society with a louder voice may bring that element of diversity in debate that can enhance resilience, rather than over depending on a strong state apparatus that is dominated by one political party.

sections.label: State funding and NPOs
sections.summary: The perception that state-funded NPOs risk funding if they contradict Government policy should be addressed, and matching grants given to NPOs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Next, we should address the perception that NPOs who receive state funding, to some degree, risk that funding if they publish research or ideas that contradict Government policy or are seen to criticise Government policy to some degree.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Next, we can be more aggressive in providing matching grants to NPOs that aim to address issues of public policy with a proven track record of making good contributions to public debate.

sections.label: Educating students beyond one answer
sections.summary: Students should not be educated to second-guess the right answer, since the world offers different answers equally consistent with the facts.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: We must not educate our students to always be aiming to second-guess what the right answer is and provide that answer in a formulae fashion.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: That can easily translate into a future workplace attitude of second-guessing what the boss wants rather than figuring out the best solution for the customer of the company or the company to achieve the end goal.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In the world they will grow up in, there will be no one right answer but rather different answers, approaches and strategies that could all be equally consistent with the facts.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Rather, the villain was a system that was as adaptable to every conceivable circumstance as the hubris of the designers led them to believe.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: It is up to us to do better from this crisis to equip our successes for the next.

sections.label: SIRS helped self-employed persons
sections.summary: SIRS has helped about 180,000 self-employed persons in the last couple of months.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: Just to remind the Members of the House, all in all, SIRS has helped about 180,000 self-employed persons in the last couple of months.

sections.label: Automatic help to 100,000 people
sections.summary: A system was designed that eventually delivered help automatically to 100,000 people over a couple of weeks.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: Nonetheless, we designed a system that eventually delivered help automatically to 100,000 people.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: To do that, over the course of a couple of weeks is actually a very challenging thing to do.

sections.label: System ramp-up and NTUC constraints
sections.summary: The system took a while to ramp up, and NTUC was doing this under very difficult constraints.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: The system did take a while to try and ramp up.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: I should say that NTUC was doing this under very, very difficult constraints.

sections.label: Additional 80,000 SIRS payouts
sections.summary: As a result, an additional 80,000 people eventually got their SIRS payouts.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: Having done all this, I think, as a result, an additional 80,000 people eventually got their SIRS payouts.

sections.label: Why NTUC administered SIRS
sections.summary: A Member asked why SIRS administration went to NTUC rather than a Ministry or Statutory Board, noting NTUC's less experience and resources.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera
sentences.text: The Minister, if I heard her correctly, also alluded to how NTUC perhaps did not have the the resourcing necessary to take on this task.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera
sentences.text: So, my question would really be: could the Minister shed some light on the Government's thinking why the administration of SIRS was given to NTUC rather than to a Ministry or a Statutory Board?

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera
sentences.text: One imagines that an organisation like the NTUC, being a collective, a union, has less experience and less resources when administering a national level policy likes SIRS, as compared to Ministries and Statutory Boards.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: In the case of the SGUnited Traineeships Programme, the Singapore Business Federation put its hand up and say that, "We would like to be a part of it." And we saw that they had some capabilities that they could deliver this programme and so we partner with them.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: We had partnered the Singapore National Employers Federation for other schemes before.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: And so, when the opportunity presented itself, other organisations besides the Government wanting to deliver help to Singaporeans, we do not stop them.

sections.label: Four Budgets blunted worst effects
sections.summary: Four Government Budgets totalling close to $100 billion helped blunt the worst effects, saving jobs and reducing retrenchments.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: The unprecedented four Government Budgets in the first half of this year, totalling close to $100 billion, helped blunt the worst effects.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: They helped to save jobs and reduce retrenchments even when most companies and industries have little or, in some cases, no revenue.

sections.label: Companies shedding workers ahead
sections.summary: More companies will shed workers through downsizing or closure as demand and revenue stay weak and cost pressures continue.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: In the months ahead, we will see more companies shedding workers through downsizing or even closure because demand and revenue conditions will not return to normal for many industries, while cost and cash pressures will continue to bear down on businesses.

sections.label: Singapore Core and older workers
sections.summary: The speaker supports securing the Singapore Core and says job displacement and hiring must not discriminate against older workers.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: I support these efforts to secure our Singapore Core.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: I also strongly believe that we must clearly signal that job displacement and job hiring must not become areas for discriminating against older workers as a category.

sections.label: Older displaced workers' re-employment difficulty
sections.summary: Older displaced workers find new work harder even in a buoyant economy and often face significant wage drops.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: Furthermore, older displaced workers will have a harder time finding new work even in a buoyant economy and often face a significant drop in wages when they do find new jobs.

sections.label: Senior worker support and incentives
sections.summary: The 2020 Budget had a Senior Worker Support package, and an extra $1 billion went to the Jobs Growth Incentive for workers aged 40 and above.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: In the 2020 Budget, there was indeed a Senior Worker Support package comprising the Senior Employment Credit, the Senior Worker Early Adopter Grant and the Part-time Re-employment Grant.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: In the most recent announcement, Deputy Prime Minister Heng allocated an additional $1 billion in the Jobs Growth Incentive aimed at spurring the hiring of workers aged 40 and above.

sections.label: NTUC Jobs Security Council matching
sections.summary: The NTUC Jobs Security Council has matched 20,000 jobseekers to new job openings, as recently reported.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: The NTUC Jobs Security Council, for example – it was reported in the papers recently – has matched 20,000 jobseekers to new job openings.

sections.label: Monitoring older worker job outcomes
sections.summary: The speaker urges the National Jobs Council to monitor job matching, switching and retraining outcomes for older workers and adjust efforts to prevent a permanent precariat.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: I have a whole list here, but I will not belabour the point – anything from jobs to traineeships, support for training, satellite centres.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: I do urge our National Jobs Council to closely monitor the job matching, switching and retraining efforts and outcomes for older workers, which is my subject matter today, and to make the necessary adjustments, enhancements and interventions in the weeks and months ahead, in order to prevent the build-up of a sticky or permanent precariat of older involuntarily displaced workers.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: The Tripartite Alliance for Fair and Progressive Employment Practices or TAFEP works closely with MOM to promote and police fairness at work.

sections.label: COVID-19 relief for displaced workers
sections.summary: The speaker urges MSF to consider a second tranche of the COVID-19 Support Grant and Temporary Relief Fund and to give Social Service Offices more flexibility to help displaced workers.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: I support MSF’s stance to “leave no one behind”.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: I urge MSF to consider a second tranche of the COVID-19 Support Grant (CSG) and the Temporary Relief Fund (TRF) to provide more relief to workers who may be displaced in the months ahead.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: I also seek MSF’s support to empower the Social Service Offices or SSOs with greater flexibility to help displaced workers promptly to cope with family expenses arising out of COVID-19 through ComCare and other schemes – give them more leeway to exercise.

sections.label: Support for older lower-wage workers
sections.summary: The speaker hopes MOM will review and expand qualifying criteria and parameters for the Silver Support Scheme and Workfare Income Supplement.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: To help provide greater support to our older workers who face financial hardship, especially those of lower wages, I hope that MOM could consider reviewing and expanding qualifying criteria and parameters for schemes such as the Silver Support Scheme and the Workfare Income Supplement or WIS.

sections.label: CPF-Medisave caps for older Singaporeans
sections.summary: The speaker hopes MOH will consider higher CPF-Medisave thresholds or caps for older Singaporeans or greater case-by-case flexibility, citing a resident's $800 bill.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: In this regard, I would also hope that MOH would please consider whether there could be higher thresholds or caps on CPF-Medisave for older Singaporeans, or greater flexibility on a case-by-case basis to help with coping with cash expenses without sacrificing or delaying medical treatment.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: Just last night, at my Meet-the-People Session, I had such a case where the bill was $800 and because of the cap, $300 was allowed to be deducted from MediSave and the resident had to come out with $500.

sections.label: Resident's daughter unable to secure aid
sections.summary: A resident's daughter, a local polytechnic graduate, found a place at a private university but could not secure a loan or financial aid.

sentences.speaker: Ms Raeesah Khan (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Two weeks into my role as a Member of Parliament-elect, I received a plea from my resident, a father, for help.

sentences.speaker: Ms Raeesah Khan (Sengkang)
sentences.text: He went on to share that his second daughter, a graduate from a local Polytechnic, wanted to pursue further studies at university.

sentences.speaker: Ms Raeesah Khan (Sengkang)
sentences.text: She found a place at one of the private universities last year but has been unable to secure a loan or financial aid.

sentences.speaker: Ms Raeesah Khan (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Should she have received the aid she was looking for, she could have been just starting her first year at university by now.

sections.label: Minimum wage and redundancy insurance
sections.summary: The speaker says introducing schemes like a national Minimum Wage and redundancy insurance improve workers' accessibility to opportunities.

sentences.speaker: Ms Raeesah Khan (Sengkang)
sentences.text: More broadly, introducing schemes like a national Minimum Wage and redundancy insurance improve workers' accessibility to opportunities.

sections.label: Opportunities for young creatives
sections.summary: The speaker calls for an independent arts body to oversee licensing and funding and for reforming the media landscape, which lacks competition.

sentences.speaker: Ms Raeesah Khan (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Let us give young creatives more opportunities by setting up an independent body for the arts to oversee licensing and funding, and by reforming our media landscape which has far too long has suffered from a lack of competition.

sections.label: Job discrimination against Singaporeans
sections.summary: The passage argues that workers should not face employment discrimination based on age, gender, race or hijab, and that legislation is needed.

sentences.speaker: Ms Raeesah Khan (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Job discrimination is a real problem that has real consequences for Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: Ms Raeesah Khan (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Workers looking to make an honest living to support their families should not have to face employment discrimination in the job market because of their age, gender or race, and certainly should not be discriminated because they wear a hijab.

sentences.speaker: Ms Raeesah Khan (Sengkang)
sentences.text: We must legislate to this end not only because fostering an inclusive job market for Singaporean workers makes economic sense but also simply because this is the right thing to do.

sections.label: Lowering voting age to 18
sections.summary: The passage proposes considering lowering the voting age to 18 to give young people a say in Singapore's future.

sentences.speaker: Ms Raeesah Khan (Sengkang)
sentences.text: For starters, we should consider lowering the voting age to 18 to give more young people a say in Singapore's future, propel them to follow politics and legislation more closely and include their voices in the process.

sections.label: Young women career and family
sections.summary: The passage states young women are torn between growing a family or pursuing a career, and recalls a 2016 speech about a Perfect Storm.

sentences.speaker: Ms Raeesah Khan (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Young women today, many of whom I have met, continue to be torn between the decision of growing the family or pursuing a fulfilling career.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: In my maiden speech in this House in 2016, I spoke of imagining a Perfect Storm, "… a global downturn lasting many years; divisions of race, language, religion; social class, inequality and culture; a fractured national consensus, divisive politics.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: And then having to face a major crisis – a terrorist attack on Singapore soil, a pandemic, or a regional conflict where old friends ask us to choose between them." It has been nearly five years and a storm has gathered all around the world.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: Economic crisis – all around the world, the worst in the history of independent Singapore.

sections.label: Parliamentary Question on patient care
sections.summary: The passage states a Parliamentary Question was filed to look further at an issue with implications for patient care and safety.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: I have filed a Parliamentary Question on this, so that we can look at this issue further.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: This is a serious development, implications for patient care and patient safety.

sections.label: Regulators and insurance companies
sections.summary: The passage calls on MOH and MAS to see if regulators need to level the playing field for patients.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: We have also seen from the SMA letter that even individual healthcare practitioners, despite assessing a diagnostic procedure to be medically necessary, in some cases cannot move the insurance companies.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: I call upon MOH and MAS to look at this, and to see if the visible hand of the regulators needs to come in to level the playing field for patients and our people.

sections.label: Patent system and cheaper medications
sections.summary: The passage asks whether the patent system can be relooked so cheaper effective medications enter the market while the pharmaceutical industry still creates jobs.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: Are there also ways to relook our patent system so that cheaper but equally effective medications can more easily enter the market, while still allowing our pharmaceutical industry to create jobs and opportunities for Singaporeans and maintaining our forward position as an intellectual property hub and intellectual property thought leader?

sections.label: Nurses and allied health pay
sections.summary: An MP asks how often MOH compares public and private sector pay for nurses and allied healthcare workers, and whether they can be paid more.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: As one auntie said in Mandarin, "有这个亲密感, 有这个亲切感" – someone who can be a familiar-sounding voice in difficult times for our seniors.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: So, I would like to ask the Government: how often does MOH compare the pay of our nurses and allied healthcare workers across the public and private sector?

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: Can we pay our nurses and allied health workers more?

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: The Minister for Finance has spoken about fiscal prudence but, in a deep recession, we should also be willing to spend counter-cyclically, to invest further in our fellow Singaporeans and further build up capabilities within Singapore and in our public sector healthcare, especially in areas where the market alone may not generate the most optimal outcome straightaway.

sections.label: Healthcare and people's lives
sections.summary: The passage states that healthcare concerns the lives of all Singaporeans, regardless of background.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: Mr Speaker, healthcare is about our people’s lives – your life and mine, the lives of our loved ones, the lives of every Singaporean, regardless of background.

sections.label: Cancel culture on the Internet
sections.summary: The passage describes negative online conduct and defines cancellation as a targeted attack on a person's reputation by critics.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: We have been seeing some negative conduct on the Internet for some time now.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: There is increasing cognisance of the "cancel culture" which is causing some concern. "Cancellation", basically, refers to an attack on someone’s reputation by a determined group of critics because of an opinion or action of that individual that is deemed to be unacceptable.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: It is a targeted effort to destroy the individual, to get them de-platformed or put out of business.

sections.label: Online virality and mob mentality
sections.summary: The passage states that online issues can go viral quickly and a mob mentality can form before facts are verified or discussed.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: For one, online, a certain issue or matter can get viral very quickly and a mob mentality can form long before facts can be verified or discussed.

sections.label: Podcast criticised for misogynistic comments
sections.summary: The passage states a popular podcast channel was criticised after episodes were found to contain misogynistic and degrading comments about women.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: A popular podcast channel was criticised when it was found to have certain episodes where comments which were misogynistic and degrading to women were made.

sections.label: Power shifted to the people
sections.summary: The passage states power has shifted to the people, with the Internet and social media as accessible battlefields, citing US movements.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: Power has shifted to the people, with the Internet and social media platforms as accessible battlefields.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: We have seen the #MeToo and #BlackLivesMatter movements in the US.

sections.label: Youths fear online backlash
sections.summary: Youths say they fear backlash from others with different views, not the laws, when expressing views online.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: The youths shared that it was not so much the laws they were afraid of.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: They feel afraid of expressing their views online because they fear backlash from others who have different views.

sections.label: Reviewing discriminatory conduct frameworks
sections.summary: Policies or legislation may need to shift to shape behaviours, and frameworks on employer discriminatory conduct need review and improvement.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: Some policies or legislation may need to shift to shape behaviours.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: There have been concerns by some in this House about the issues of discriminatory conduct on the part of employers and we need to review and look at the frameworks in place and improve them.

sections.label: Negative online discussions divide society
sections.summary: Online discussions can be negative, leading to personal attacks, and online campaigns and cultures can divide society and lead to violence.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: What is bad is that sometimes the discussions that we see online are very negative, leading to personal attacks on someone and running away from the original topic of discussion.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: This is worrying because we can see how online campaigns and cultures that spread in other countries, can divide society and lead to violence.

sections.label: Ayden has Down Syndrome
sections.summary: Ayden has Down Syndrome.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: Ayden, as many of you know, has Down Syndrome.

sections.label: Incentivising employers not enough
sections.summary: Incentivising employers to employ people with disabilities is not enough for awareness and inclusivity in workplaces.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: When we talk about creating awareness and being inclusive in workplaces, it is not enough to just incentivise employers to employ people with disabilities.

sections.label: Building educator capacity and capability
sections.summary: Training select or all teachers is not enough; educators need skills, values, inclusivity culture, and enhanced special needs career pathways.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: When we talk about building the capacity and capability of educators, it may not be enough to just train a select group of teachers or provide basic training for all teachers.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: We must provide the skills to all educators to identify needs, teach the right values and attitudes and inculcate a culture of pervasive inclusivity within our education system.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: We need to also look at enhancing the career pathway of educators in the special needs sector.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: The reality is that embracing and supporting this community bring great value to Singapore as a whole.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: There is great economic value in empowering this group with the necessary skills to take care of themselves and be as independent as possible.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: If we deal with this issue upstream, we will spend less in providing support for them in the future.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: When we enable people with disabilities, we enable the whole community.

sections.label: Labour Movement COVID-19 support
sections.summary: The Labour Movement processed 180,000 applications, with successful self-employed persons receiving up to $9,000, among examples of Singaporean spirit.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: While there were some questions raised on SIRS yesterday, including conducting interviews for families to approve applications, I would like to remind everyone that in the past few months, the Labour Movement, in supporting Singaporeans through this crisis, assisted in processing 180,000 applications.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Successful self-employed persons (SEPs) received up to $9,000 to tide their families through this challenging time.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: They tried their best to help the applicants get the support that they needed, from taxi drivers, wedding photographers, property agents, tuition teachers to asatizahs and many others.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: These, together with many other fantastic activities that fellow Singaporeans have done – such as SG BukaPuasa who delivered 20,000 meals daily to needy families during the Ramadan month at the height of the circuit breaker and Engineering Good who provided refurbished laptops to kids from disadvantaged families – are just some examples of the Singaporean spirit.

sections.label: Joint Wage Support Scheme
sections.summary: For sectors affected by COVID-19 such as hospitality, MICE and retail, the Joint Wage Support Scheme kept businesses afloat and workforces employed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: For these sectors and others similarly affected by COVID-19 such as hospitality, meetings, incentives, conference and exhibitions (MICE) and retail, the Joint Wage Support Scheme has been integral in keeping businesses afloat and its workforce employed.

sections.label: SkillsFuture support for older workers
sections.summary: SkillsFuture, with added support for older workers to reskill and upskill and a focus on skills over paper qualifications, is a step in the right direction.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: SkillsFuture, especially the additional support for older workers to reskill, upskill and the focus on skills over paper qualifications at the workplace, is a step in the right direction for our society.

sections.label: Retrenched senior workers re-employment struggle
sections.summary: Despite hiring incentives, retrenched senior workers still struggle to seek re-employment, with the majority left with security or cleaning employment.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Even with incentives for hiring, retrenched senior workers still struggle to seek re-employment and the majority are left presented with either employment in security or cleaning.

sections.label: EngageRocket work-from-home study
sections.summary: A study by EngageRocket with the Singapore Human Resource Institute and the Institute for Human Resource Professionals found nine of 10 employees want some work from home.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: In fact, a study by EngageRocket, in partnership with the Singapore Human Resource Institute and the Institute for Human Resource Professionals, revealed that nine of 10 employees shared that they would like to continue with some form of work from home as a new way of working.

sections.label: Unemployed resident in rental flat
sections.summary: A resident in a rental flat is a 45-year-old digitally literate man, father of two boys aged 12 and eight, and unemployed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: To cite an example, one of my resident lives in a rental flat.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: He is a 45-year-old man, digitally literate, a father of two boys aged 12 and eight, and unemployed.

sections.label: Employment quotas for seniors
sections.summary: The speaker says government efforts need organisational support and hopes minimum employment quotas for seniors and the less-able will not be needed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: However, efforts by Government agencies can only go so far without support from organisations who are willing to make the change.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: I believe that we should not come to a point where we must legislate minimum employment quotas for seniors and the less-able to move towards a more inclusive society.

sections.label: PME jobs done anywhere
sections.summary: Digitalisation and working from home have shown that most PME jobs can be done anywhere in the world.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Digitalisation and working from home have shown that for most of our PME jobs – my job, too, for that matter – can be done anywhere in the world.

sections.label: Pandemic job losses
sections.summary: The COVID-19 pandemic has affected the whole world, and even with the Jobs Support Scheme, jobs and livelihoods may be lost.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: (In Malay):   The COVID-19 pandemic has affected the whole world.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: We need to be prepared for a reality that, even with support such as the Jobs Support Scheme (JSS), there are jobs that may be lost and there are workers who will lose their livelihood.

sections.label: Digital platforms during circuit breaker
sections.summary: During the circuit breaker, enterprises with digital platforms could continue and even expand operations to new customers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: During the circuit breaker, when access to customers is limited, enterprises with digital platforms are not only able to continue operations but also expand operations to new customers.

sections.label: Training for affected workers
sections.summary: Workers whose livelihoods are affected can undergo training such as SkillsFuture courses to enhance skills, especially in the digital field.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Regarding workers whose livelihood are affected, they can make use of the opportunity to undergo training, such as SkillsFuture courses, to enhance their skills and increase their capabilities, especially in the digital field.

sections.label: Working together for displaced workers
sections.summary: Government and people should work with employers and businesses to create opportunities for displaced Singaporean workers and build a resilient society.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: The Government and our people should continue to work hard and work with employers and businesses to create opportunities for displaced Singaporean workers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: By working together to transform our economy and taking care of each other to ensure inclusive transformation, we can build a more resilient society and create better jobs for our children in the future.

sections.label: Crisis permanently changes Singapore
sections.summary: The crisis will permanently change lives and there is no going back to the status quo ante.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
sentences.text: They developed our industries, forged a new society and built a modern Singapore, handing it over to us in excellent order.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
sentences.text: That Singapore is now in our hands and what we do in this crisis matters.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
sentences.text: This crisis is not a temporary deviation from our previous path but one that will permanently change our lives as we know it.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
sentences.text: As President Halimah Yacob said last week, there is no going back to the status quo ante and COVID-19 has indeed reshuffled the deck.

sections.label: Sustainability sector new jobs
sections.summary: The Minister said 55,000 new jobs will be created in the sustainability sector over the next decade.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
sentences.text: As the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment mentioned last week, 55,000 new jobs will be created in the sustainability sector over the next decade in areas such as high-tech agriculture and aquaculture.

sections.label: Digitalisation displaces jobs, hits industries
sections.summary: The great reset accelerated digitalisation, displacing jobs and significantly hitting aviation, tourism and construction.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
sentences.text: Mr Sharael Taha had mentioned earlier the great reset has accelerated the process of digitalisation faster than any of us has expected.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
sentences.text: It has displaced jobs and many of our industries like aviation, tourism and construction have been significantly hit.

sections.label: Industry Transformation Maps and Reserves
sections.summary: The Industry Transformation Maps continue efforts to keep Singapore in the best possible condition, with Reserves deployed in this crisis.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
sentences.text: The Industry Transformation Maps are the latest version of a long line of efforts to ensure that we keep Singapore in the best possible condition, not just for now but also for the future.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
sentences.text: Well, we have seen clearly why we have safeguarded our Reserves.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
sentences.text: We have now deployed them in this crisis to help our people to reinvent themselves and to create opportunities for us to keep on going into the future.

sections.label: Singapore benefited from digital investment
sections.summary: Given rapid global digitalisation, Singapore benefited from its early investment in digital transformation.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
sentences.text: Given the rapid global digitalisation, Singapore benefited from its early investment in digital transformation.

sections.label: Most in-demand global jobs
sections.summary: LinkedIn data shows the most in-demand jobs globally are in sales, healthcare, software engineering and project management.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
sentences.text: LinkedIn data shows that the most in-demand jobs globally are in sales, healthcare, software engineering and project management.

sections.label: SGUnited Traineeships Programme
sections.summary: The SGUnited Traineeships Programme enhances younger Singaporeans' competitiveness and helps them get on-the-job training.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
sentences.text: For younger Singaporeans, the SGUnited Traineeships Programme is enhancing their competitiveness too, helping them get valuable on-the-job training.

sections.label: Measures against lottery of birth
sections.summary: The Government has rolled out measures to mitigate the lottery of birth, though concerns remain that the system penalises people for past setbacks.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
sentences.text: To this end, the Government has rolled out measures in recent years to mitigate the lottery of birth.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
sentences.text: And yet too far, we often hear concerns that our system penalises people too heavily for the setbacks of their past – where grades from your "O" levels or "A" levels disproportionately dictate your career path; where we congratulate people for defying the odds without questioning why the odds were put there in the first place.

sections.label: Hiring beyond grades and schools
sections.summary: The speaker says that when hiring, they looked beyond grades and schools to skills and micro-credentials, such as Google credentials.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
sentences.text: In my time interviewing and hiring people for our companies, I looked beyond traditional barometers of success, like grades and schools to skills and micro-credentials, which is what Ms Mariam Jaafar mentioned yesterday, the Google credentials.

sections.label: Failure and past failures
sections.summary: Failure will have consequences, but people should not be bound to their past failures and denied the chance to shape different futures.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
sentences.text: Failure will have consequences, but we must not and should not bind people to their past failures denying them the chance to learn from them and shape their futures differently.

sections.label: Shame over mental health resources
sections.summary: A resident refused to call the MSF careline out of shame, so inclusive policies and norms are needed for people to use mental health resources unashamedly.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
sentences.text: Closer to home, I remember one of my residents refusing to call the Ministry of Social and Family Development (MSF) careline because she felt it was shameful to do so.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
sentences.text: We need inclusive policies and norms to ensure that people feel safe and unashamed to use Mental Health resources.

sections.label: Resident using text-to-speech technology
sections.summary: A resident texts using text-to-speech recognition software and now works in a multinational's technology department communications team, benefiting from an inclusive employer.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: Mr Alvin Tan, you need to wrap up.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: She texts me using text-to-speech recognition software and is now working in the communications team in a technology department of a multinational.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: She adapted using technology to augment her ability and benefited from having an inclusive employer who treasured for her abilities.

sections.label: Courage of Singapore's Pioneers
sections.summary: Courage is the will to overcome fear, and in crisis Singapore must overcome worries and seize opportunities to build a better future together.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: Courage, Mr Speaker, the quality which our Pioneers exemplified is not the absence of fear, but the will to overcome it.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: In our moment of crisis, we must meet this moment by overcoming our worries and seizing opportunities to build a better future, not clinging on to the shadows of a distant past, by working together in spite of our differences.

sections.label: Doing our best together
sections.summary: If Singaporeans do their best, stick together and stay nimble and courageous with Singaporeans at the heart, the moment would have been met.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: For today, as long as we do our best, as long as we stick together and stay nimble and courageous with Singaporeans at the heart of all we do, I believe we would have met this moment.

sections.label: Thanking the President
sections.summary: The speaker thanks the President for sharing hard truths and jolting us into a new age for policy-making.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: First, I would like to thank the President for sharing with us some hard truths and for jolting us into a new age for policy-making.

sections.label: Change in internal politics
sections.summary: A second change lies in Singapore's internal politics.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: A second change lies in our internal politics.

sections.label: Evolving Singapore's model of democracy
sections.summary: The aspiration is to evolve our own model of democracy where differences do not tear or polarise, though unity in diversity is not a given.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: This is the aspiration towards evolving our own model of democracy, where differences do not tear the social fabric or polarise and fragment.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: We have today before us, a chance to forge our own path but this will not be easy, as the hon Leader of the House cautioned us earlier this week, "Unity in diversity is not a given." About 2,500 years ago, in another time, another place, Pericles, a leader of Athens, a small city state, urged his people to find their own way in an uncertain world.

sections.label: Better use of First Reading
sections.summary: The First Reading of a Bill can be used by the Minister to give Members a non-specialist understanding of the issues and how the Bill addresses them.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: To help them, the First Reading of any Bill, which is currently rather formulaic, can be put to better use by the Minister by giving Members a non-specialist understanding of the issues at play, how they impact the ordinary lives of Singaporeans and how the Bill proposes to address these concerns.

sections.label: Lodging speeches as read
sections.summary: A suggestion that Parliament allow speeches to be lodged, taken as read and made public.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: They obviously will not be able to consider what will be said later by other Parliamentarians.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: I suggest that Parliament make available the option of lodging our speeches to be taken as read and made public to all.

sections.label: MP accountability and IT system
sections.summary: A call for an IT system letting the public check MPs' attendance, questions asked and times spoken.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: This will also hold Members to account, and for our constituents to see if we do, indeed, put our time and attention to Parliamentary matters or whether we are simply going through the motion.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: I would like Parliament to also invest in a new information technology (IT) system to make it easier for any member of the public to hold MPs to account – to check the attendance of any Member, to find the number of Parliamentary Questions (PQs) asked, the number of times spoken on Bills, Budgets, Committee of Supply debates, Motions and so on.

sections.label: Probate lobbying and Civil Service paper
sections.summary: Cites three-year probate lobbying and calls for a paper on MPs' constituent letters and response times.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: For example, my lobbying for a simplification of probate processes that leverage on technology, which, I am happy to note, found its way into the Addendum to the President’s Address issued by the Minister for Law, has taken three years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Another call I would make in relation to accountability is for the Civil Service to publish and present in Parliament a paper regularly stating the number of letters it and Statutory Boards receive from MPs petitioning on behalf of their constituents on a per constituency basis.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: The paper should indicate the percentage of the substantive responses to the MPs which are made within the time period stipulated in the Government Instruction Manual.

sections.label: UK Cabinet memo on MPs
sections.summary: Quotes a 2016 UK Cabinet memo on MPs raising constituents' cases and ministerial accountability.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: In response, let me highlight what the UK Cabinet said in a memo issued in March 2016: “The right of MPs to take up constituents’ cases and other issues directly with Government is an important part of the democratic process and underlines the accountability of Ministers to Parliament.” Voters are maturing, more demanding, and very rightly so, in terms of what they can and should expect from all of us in this House.

sections.label: President Halimah's advice and vision
sections.summary: Recounts the President's advice and quoted vision, thanking her and urging Singaporeans to unite.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: The President gave some valuable advice on how to live in what can appear to be very fraught times.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: She paints a new vision and exhorts us to a new mission: “The new generation of leaders and Singaporeans will have to form bonds and connections afresh…They have to continue to deliver effective and sound government, while accommodating the growing diversity of views.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: And they have to foster a more open spirit in our society, even as we strengthen the common cause holding us together as Singaporeans.” I thank President Halimah for reminding us of who we really are and for writing the first page of our new term.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Once again, we, a people of many races, cultures and religions, all of us Singaporeans, must come together to find strength and common purpose.

sections.label: Addenda lists of bodies and schemes
sections.summary: Notes the many maps, committees, centres, schemes and funds in the Addenda and asks for simplification.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Indeed, the Addenda to the President's Address alone contain mentions of around 12 maps and master plans, 24 committees, task force and networks, 32 centres and agencies, 32 schemes and programmes, and 24 funds, packages and grants.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: It is no wonder that people and enterprises are confused and often end up feeling demoralised and helpless when faced with problems.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: While we acknowledge that Singapore faces complex issues and appreciate that the Government and its agencies are working hard to address problems and issues faced by Singaporeans, surely there can be scope to simplify these grants plans policies and initiatives.

sections.label: Unified government transactions portal
sections.summary: Mr Leon Perera previously spoke of the need for a unified portal for residents and companies to transact with Government and access eligible schemes.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Indeed, my colleague, Mr Leon Perera, has previously spoken of the need for a unified portal for residents and companies to transact with Government and have better access to schemes that they are eligible for.

sections.label: Reviewing meritocracy's limits
sections.summary: The passage says we must review accepted norms, recognise meritocracy's limits and failure, and not become a harsh society blaming the vulnerable.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: To respond adequately, we must be willing to review some previously accepted norms and principles.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: It is a good start that we are now, like many other developed economies, finally recognising the limits and even failure of meritocracy.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: We must not let blind reliance on what meritocracy can achieve turn us into a harsh and unforgiving society, where the vulnerable are blamed for their plight for not being hardworking or talented enough to strive for a better life for themselves and their families.

sections.label: Reply on tokenism
sections.summary: When asked if he was a sterling example of meritocracy, he replied firmly that he was instead an example of tokenism.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: When asked if he was a sterling example of our meritocracy, he replied firmly that he was instead an example of tokenism.

sections.label: Nimble economy and education
sections.summary: The economy must become more nimble and education must encourage inquisitive exploration and less rote learning to produce an adaptable workforce.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: To deal with this and remain sustainable, our economy must therefore become more nimble and our education system needs to encourage inquisitive exploration and less rote learning in order to produce a workforce that is able to adapt to disruptive new horizons and opportunities.

sections.label: Green financing and school savings
sections.summary: A gap remains between enterprises and green financing, green bonds are 1.4% of corporate debt, and a Finnish town's school example is cited.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: However, there remains a large gap between enterprises and access to green financing and technology remains challenging for SMEs.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: This is also reflected in green bonds forming just 1.4% of Singapore's total corporate debt market.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Awareness of green issues, too, should start from a young age.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: We should look to the example set by a tiny town in Finland, which has managed to reduce its carbon emissions by half between 2007 and 2015.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: As an added sweetener, if the school is successful in reducing its bills due to successful green practices, students are given unfettered freedom to decide what to spend 50% of the savings on.

sections.label: Ageing Singapore care integration
sections.summary: The pressing problems of an ageing Singapore must first be tackled by further integrating social, health and informal care systems.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: The pressing problems faced by an ageing Singapore must first be tackled by further integrating our social, health and informal care systems.

sections.label: Measuring unpaid work
sections.summary: The passage states the issue's magnitude is unclear and trending is unknown, so unpaid work must be measured to make it visible.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Yet, the magnitude of the issue is unclear, and we do not have a good idea of how this has been trending.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: We must therefore measure unpaid work to make it visible.

sections.label: Time use surveys
sections.summary: The passage states many countries conduct regular time use surveys, while Singapore does not conduct such regular surveys.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: In many countries such as South Korea, Australia, New Zealand and Japan, time use surveys are now a key part of the national statistics systems and these are conducted regularly.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: In Europe, these surveys have been conducted since the 1970s and have continued with relative frequency across the region.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: It is significant that Singapore does not conduct such regular time use surveys.

sections.label: Reviewing Jobs Support Scheme
sections.summary: The passage states some companies returned JSS payments and urges a review to claw back JSS from profitable companies and re-channel resources.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Several companies have returned the JSS payments, and the Government is urging all other companies that do not require this subsidy to do likewise.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: I urge a review of the unconditional JSS to explore clawing back JSS from companies that are still profitable, and companies that continue to pay million-dollar executive salaries, and re-channel these resources to where they are more needed, like unemployment support.

sections.label: Job losses and COVID-19 support
sections.summary: The passage states employment fell by 131,500 in the second quarter, describes the COVID-19 Support Grant, and MTI's expected 5% to 7% shrinkage.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Despite our best efforts to stem job losses, according to the economic survey, employment decreased by 131,500 in the second quarter of this year.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: The COVID-19 Support Grant currently provides for cash payment of up to $800 per month for three months for those who have lost their jobs or suffered a significant drop in income.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: The Ministry of Trade and Industry (MTI) expects the economy to shrink by 5% to 7% this year.

sections.label: Enhancing COVID-19 Support Grant
sections.summary: The passage states there is room to adjust the balance between Government Reserves and household reserves and calls for enhancing the COVID-19 Support Grant.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: There is therefore a lot of room for adjustments in the balance between Government Reserves and household reserves.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: We need to enhance the COVID-19 Support Grant to offer financial assistance for a longer period of time.

sections.label: Deferring mortgage payments
sections.summary: The passage hopes the Government will grant further deferment of mortgage payments for households with members who lost jobs or income, up to December 2021.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Lastly, with all the current anxieties about losing jobs and incomes, let our people not have to worry about losing their homes.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: I hope the Government will grant further deferment of mortgage payments for households with members who have lost their jobs or suffered a loss in income, for up to December 2021.

sections.label: Recognising echo chamber bias
sections.summary: Everyone needs to recognise the bias of one's echo chamber and that we view everything through filters, whatever the issue.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Whether it is addressing issues of job security, saving jobs, creating new jobs, job discrimination, existential threats, strengthening social safety nets, national identity or retirement adequacy, everyone needs to recognise the bias of one’s echo chamber, that we view everything through filters.

sections.label: Honest evaluation of Singapore Story
sections.summary: Dwelling on past successes does not help chart the future; the pandemic exposes vulnerabilities and we must tackle sacred cows.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Dwelling on past successes does not help us chart the path to the future.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: This pandemic is like a tide rolling out, exposing our vulnerabilities previously under the surface.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: We need to muster the courage to have an honest evaluation of where we are in the work-in-progress we call "The Singapore Story".

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: We need to keep an open mind and be prepared to tackle sacred cows.

sections.label: Declined community gardeners' grass cutting offer
sections.summary: Residents' offer to cut overgrown grass was declined over injury, insurance and liability concerns, confined by business-as-usual procedures.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (East Coast)
sentences.text: In good spirit, some of my residents and community gardeners offered to do the grass cutting in case the overgrown fields may become sources of dengue cluster, which is another trend that we worry amid COVID-19.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (East Coast)
sentences.text: However, their kind offer was declined as there were concerns they may injure themselves in the process and there is no insurance coverage for them as they are not officially contracted essential workers.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (East Coast)
sentences.text: Further, the agencies were worried of the liability in case the community gardeners made claims against them in the event of any incident.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (East Coast)
sentences.text: While I can understand all this, I felt it is a pity that under such circumstances, our constraint is confined by the "business as usual" operating procedures instead of focusing on the outcome or community needs.

sections.label: Agencies bound by rule books
sections.summary: Agencies and schools found little breakthrough on options as each seemed bound by their rule book, so mindsets must change.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (East Coast)
sentences.text: There was a possibility to trial a combination of different approaches to find a balance, where the residents living in the area could leave for work and parents could drop off their children and expeditiously exit without increasing the congestions within the area.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (East Coast)
sentences.text: However, when the agencies and schools came together to work on options, there was little breakthrough as each seem bound by their rule book.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (East Coast)
sentences.text: When resolving community issues, we must depart from the mindset of “it is not in my backyard” and focus on the community that is affected.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (East Coast)
sentences.text: We have to empower the agencies and community partners, allow them to solicit external advice and resources if not found within the Ministries and open to pilot new and unproven methods without fear of violation, as long as the interest of the public and the community affected is being placed first.

sections.label: Strengthening safety net long run
sections.summary: A crisis of this scale needs immediate support like the year's Budgets, and additional options to strengthen the safety net long term.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (East Coast)
sentences.text: A crisis of this scale needs to have other aspects of immediate support, just like what is offered in the Budgets that we have had in this year, if we want to cushion the impact more broadly for the different individuals and the families that are being affected.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (East Coast)
sentences.text: So, I believe we do need to look at the additional options to strengthen the safety net for our citizens in the long run.

sections.label: Fair distribution and expanding merit
sections.summary: The process can ensure benefits are fairly distributed, and the definition of merit and success needs to be expanded.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (East Coast)
sentences.text: And through the process, we can ensure that the benefits are fairly distributed.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (East Coast)
sentences.text: And the second area, Sir, would be the need to expand our definition of merit and success, as I think it is a necessary step towards becoming an inclusive society.

sections.label: Emotional support post-COVID-19
sections.summary: The passage states that post-COVID-19 rebuilding needs more than financial aid, and that emotional support and ground-up initiatives are necessary additional safety nets.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (East Coast)
sentences.text: From crisis to rebuilding our lives post-COVID-19, we need more than financial aid.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (East Coast)
sentences.text: The emotional support that is offered and the ground-up initiatives may be unofficial, but they are necessary additional safety nets that will truly make a difference to people's lives.

sections.label: Redefining measure of success
sections.summary: The passage states that over generations success surpasses examination scores and school rankings, and quotes Minister of State Alvin Tan on a true shift in measuring success.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (East Coast)
sentences.text: Over generations, our measure of success surpasses that of examination scores, school rankings and, in turn, pursue the finer essence of life.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (East Coast)
sentences.text: And if I may just quote how Minister of State Alvin Tan has put this, he mentioned that this would be a real measure and true shift in the barometer that we measure success.

sections.label: Open collaborative spirit
sections.summary: The passage states the first point: foster an open and collaborative spirit between the people, Government and authorities.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (East Coast)
sentences.text: First, foster an open and collaborative spirit between the people, Government and authorities.

sections.label: Expanding definition of success
sections.summary: The passage states the second point: expand the definition of success to step towards an inclusive society.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (East Coast)
sentences.text: Second, expand the definition of success to step towards an inclusive society.

sections.label: Safety nets and volunteerism
sections.summary: The passage states additional safety nets will ensure a more secure life for affected people, and that volunteerism should be promoted and included in students' assessment framework.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (East Coast)
sentences.text: Additional safety nets will ensure a more secure life for people whose lives have been affected.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (East Coast)
sentences.text: We need to encourage and promote volunteerism more actively and include this into the assessment framework of a student's basic learning capabilities.

sections.label: Supporting the Motion
sections.summary: The passage expresses hope to move forward embracing diversity, partnering in putting the country first, and becoming an inclusive nation, and states support for the Motion.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (East Coast)
sentences.text: I sincerely hope we will take this opportunity to move forward embracing diversity, partner one another in the spirit of putting the country first and taking steps in becoming an inclusive nation.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (East Coast)
sentences.text: And Sir, with that, I support the Motion.

sections.label: Unemployment rate at decade high
sections.summary: The unemployment rate is at its highest level in a decade.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Our unemployment rate is at its highest level in a decade.

sections.label: Female respondents on hiring discrimination
sections.summary: About half of 255 female respondents said they were asked about children at recruitment, over 60% felt unlikely to be hired and over a third expected lower pay.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Out of 255 female respondents to the public consultation, about half said they were asked whether they had or planned to have children at the point of recruitment.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Over 60% felt they were unlikely to be hired and over a third felt they would be offered a lower salary if they had or planned to have children.

sections.label: Women's pay gap and employment
sections.summary: Women earned $342 less than men for similar work on average, and last year the figure was 61%, far below 77% for men.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: On average, women earned $342 less than men for similar work.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Last year, it was 61%, far below the 77% for men.

sections.label: Ziqing's promotion during pregnancy
sections.summary: In Nee Soon East, constituency manager Ziqing was considered for promotion while pregnant, promoted to deputy constituency director on maternity leave, and took up the post on return.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: In Nee Soon East, Ziqing, our constituency manager was considered for promotion when she was pregnant with her second child, received the promotion to deputy constituency director when she was on maternity leave and took up the post when she came back from her leave.

sections.label: Extending preschool support programmes
sections.summary: The speaker hopes the Development Support and Learning Support programme is extended to all preschools and nursery children, and that NIEC courses train teachers to support differently abled children.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: First, I hope the Development Support and Learning Support programme, which provides trained specialists, can be extended to all preschools rather than just some and extended also to nursery-level children.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Second, I hope that as part of their professional development, all new pre-school teachers undergoing courses at the National Institute of Early Childhood Development (NIEC) are offered modular courses and top-ups that train them to support differently abled children in their classrooms.

sections.label: Hanif's 14 years as cleaner
sections.summary: Hanif has worked as a cleaner in Singapore for 14 years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Hanif has worked as a cleaner in Singapore for 14 years.

sections.label: Cleaners quarterly outings
sections.summary: The speaker has been bringing local and migrant cleaners out for outings almost every quarter for five years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: For the past five years, I have been bringing our cleaners, both local and migrant, out for outings almost every quarter.

sections.label: Members join cleaner outings
sections.summary: The speaker recommends Members join and organise outings for cleaners when safe, and help humanise cleaners.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: My first recommendation is that Members of this House join us and organise these outings for our cleaners once it is safe to do so.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: My second recommendation is that Members will also help humanise our cleaners.

sections.label: Members host inclusive events
sections.summary: The speaker recommends Members host more inclusive events when it is safe to do so.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: My third recommendation is that Members will host more inclusive events, again, when it is safe to do so.

sections.label: Cleaner's diploma results
sections.summary: A woman many did not view for who she was is now doing a diploma and scored straight A's in her first semester.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Many did not view her for who she really was and the difficult journey she was going through.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: I am glad to share with everyone that she is now doing her diploma, and she proudly sent me the results of her first semester.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: She had scored straight "A"s for all the modules.

sections.label: Biased assumptions of deservingness
sections.summary: The speaker says biased assumptions may exist in notions of deservingness, and cites GDP and unemployment figures.

sentences.speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: We need to first acknowledge that there could be biased assumptions in our current notion and perceptions of deservingness.

sentences.speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: We projected our gross domestic product (GDP) to shrink by 5% to 7% in 2020.

sentences.speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Our unemployment rate is at 2.9% and it could rise further despite our best efforts.

sections.label: ComCare automatic renewal
sections.summary: The speaker was delighted by Minister Masagos' 7 August announcement of automatic ComCare renewal for those whose support ended this quarter.

sentences.speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: When Minister Masagos made an announcement on 7 August that there would be an automatic renewal of ComCare for those whose support was due to end in the current quarter, I was delighted.

sections.label: Shift to growth-based assistance
sections.summary: The speaker urges rethinking social assistance from a needs-based to a growth-based approach and renaming needy families as challenged families.

sentences.speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: We put them and their family back on their feet.

sentences.speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: I urge this House to rethink our social assistance approach, from a “needs-based approach” to a “growth-based approach”.

sentences.speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: For a start, I recommend that we shift our language to stop referring to these families as “needy” families and start addressing them as “challenged families” to kickstart a mindset shift in our society.

sections.label: Women's earnings and birth rate
sections.summary: AWARE research shows women earn about $550,000 less over 40 years, and the 2018 birth rate of 1.14 was the lowest in eight years.

sentences.speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: According to research by AWARE Singapore, women earn close to $550,000 less than their male counterparts, over the course of a standard 40-year career.

sentences.speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Less people working means a shrinking tax base, while we face rising healthcare costs due to our ageing population.

sentences.speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: So far, measures such as the Baby Bonus scheme have not been effective in improving outcomes, as our birth rate remains far lower than our replacement rate at 1.14 in 2018, the lowest in eight years.

sections.label: Strategies for women and caregivers
sections.summary: The speaker urges the House to consider valuing unpaid care work, workplace policies, re-entry to work and upstream gender education.

sentences.speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The strategies I urge this House to consider and debate in the coming months are: valuing the unpaid care work of women; legislating adequate workplace policies to support working caregivers, men or women; facilitate easier re-entry back to work; and reducing the burden of care on women with upstream gender and care education in our schools.

sections.label: Jobseeker discrimination stories
sections.summary: The speaker asks whether enough effort is made to know families' stories and lists instances of jobseekers facing discrimination.

sentences.speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Are we making enough and intentional effort to get to know their stories?

sentences.speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: And similar to Mr Louis Ng, some of the instances I have seen in my work at Daughters Of Tomorrow are the following: a pregnant job seeker in a dilemma whether to disclose her pregnancy to a prospective employer; a single mother being asked how she expects to turn up for work on time with four kids on her hands; a Malay or Indian jobseeker being turned away because employers prefer “Chinese-speaking” individuals for jobs that may not require this; a tattooed individual being turned away for a job at a childcare centre and a Muslim woman being asked to remove her headscarf to perform her customer service duties.

sentences.speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Recently, due to several notable incidents, our racial and religious harmony has been tested.

sections.label: Loosen out-of-bounds markers
sections.summary: The speaker believes the Government can loosen out-of-bounds markers and practise more tolerance at the leadership level.

sentences.speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: At the leadership level, I believe that the Government can loosen out-of-bounds (OB) markers and practise more tolerance.

sections.label: Magnanimity towards young dissenters
sections.summary: The speaker urges the House for magnanimity and forbearance towards the young and dissenting while evolving a new social compact.

sentences.speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: I look forward to enabling young people to step forward, to take on this mantle of nation-building work.

sentences.speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: I urge the House for magnanimity and forbearance towards the young and the dissenting, while we figure things together in all our messiness and diversity as one people, as we evolve a new social compact for Singapore, together.

sections.label: COVID-19 testing, ICU beds, migrant workers
sections.summary: Singapore did about 20,000 laboratory tests a day, more than doubled ICU capacity, created more beds than all acute hospitals, and mobilised SAF and Home Team for 300,000 migrant workers.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister (Mr Lee Hsien Loong)
sentences.text: Today, we can do about 20,000 laboratory tests a day and with pooled testing, that means we are able to test several times that number of persons.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister (Mr Lee Hsien Loong)
sentences.text: We more than doubled our our Intensive Care Unit (ICU) capacity, in case we were swamped with gravely ill COVID-19 cases, like what happened in Wuhan, Milan or New York.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister (Mr Lee Hsien Loong)
