sentences.text: In total, we created more beds than all our acute hospitals put together – all within a few weeks.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister (Mr Lee Hsien Loong)
sentences.text: To handle the migrant worker dormitories, where we had most of our COVID-19 cases, we mobilised the SAF and the Home Team.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister (Mr Lee Hsien Loong)
sentences.text: They did a magnificent job in the most testing circumstances – ensuring the well-being of some 300,000 migrant workers, taking care of their health and welfare and keeping them, as well as our general population, safe.

sections.label: Low fatality rate and numbers
sections.summary: Singapore's fatality rate and absolute numbers are one of the lowest in the world.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister (Mr Lee Hsien Loong)
sentences.text: Our fatality rate and absolute numbers are one of the lowest in the world.

sections.label: Survey on weariness of safety measures
sections.summary: A Straits Times survey showed almost half of respondents were weary of safety measures, and success in keeping cases low makes people question whether painful measures are necessary.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister (Mr Lee Hsien Loong)
sentences.text: A recent The Straits Times survey showed that almost half of the respondents were weary of the safety measures.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister (Mr Lee Hsien Loong)
sentences.text: The irony is that the more successful we are in keeping cases low, the more people wonder whether all these painful measures are necessary.

sections.label: Virus infectiousness and resurgence risk
sections.summary: The COVID-19 virus remains as infectious and potent as before, and relaxing measures now because numbers have come down will cause a resurgence.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister (Mr Lee Hsien Loong)
sentences.text: The COVID-19 virus remains as infectious and potent as it was before.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister (Mr Lee Hsien Loong)
sentences.text: If we relax these measures now because the numbers have come down, we will have a resurgence.

sections.label: Disease X possibility
sections.summary: COVID-19 is not the worst new disease that can befall mankind, and it is only a matter of time before Disease X happens.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister (Mr Lee Hsien Loong)
sentences.text: It is, by far, not the worst new disease that can befall mankind.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister (Mr Lee Hsien Loong)
sentences.text: But it is only a matter of time before Disease X happens.

sections.label: Strengthened social safety nets
sections.summary: In the last 15 years, Singapore shifted its approach and progressively strengthened social safety nets, introducing ComCare in 2005, Workfare in 2007 and Silver Support in 2016.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister (Mr Lee Hsien Loong)
sentences.text: Therefore, in the last 15 years or so, we shifted our approach and progressively strengthened our social safety nets.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister (Mr Lee Hsien Loong)
sentences.text: We introduced many schemes in these last 15 years – ComCare in 2005, Workfare in 2007 and Silver Support in 2016.

sections.label: COVID-19 emergency support measures
sections.summary: Social spending tripled in 15 years, but COVID-19 required emergency measures funded by past Reserves.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister (Mr Lee Hsien Loong)
sentences.text: Altogether, we now spend three times as much on social programmes every year as we did 15 years ago.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister (Mr Lee Hsien Loong)
sentences.text: But when COVID-19 hit us, they could not be enough.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister (Mr Lee Hsien Loong)
sentences.text: So, we implemented multiple emergency measures for COVID-19 – the Jobs Support Scheme (JSS), Self-employed Income Relief Scheme (SIRS), COVID-19 Support Grant and now, the Jobs Growth Initiative.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister (Mr Lee Hsien Loong)
sentences.text: We had to draw on our past Reserves to fund them.

sections.label: Best unemployment insurance
sections.summary: The best unemployment insurance is the assurance of another job.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister (Mr Lee Hsien Loong)
sentences.text: The best unemployment insurance is, in fact, the assurance of another job.

sections.label: Older workers and bottom quintile wages
sections.summary: Older workers stay longer and bottom-quintile real wages grew faster than median wages over five years.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister (Mr Lee Hsien Loong)
sentences.text: Older workers are staying in the workforce longer and, over the last five years, real wages of our bottom quintile have consistently grown faster than median wages and that clearly shows that our approaches are working.

sections.label: Social safety nets funding principle
sections.summary: Social safety nets should be paid from current revenues, not inherited reserves or mortgaging children's future.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister (Mr Lee Hsien Loong)
sentences.text: As a matter of principle, our social safety nets should be paid for out of current revenues.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister (Mr Lee Hsien Loong)
sentences.text: We should not draw down on what we have inherited, nor should we mortgage the future of our children.

sections.label: Reserves down $70 billion
sections.summary: Plans to add to past Reserves changed to being down more than $70 billion a few months later.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister (Mr Lee Hsien Loong)
sentences.text: We thought we could meet our current commitments and put aside funds for the long term to offset the Goods and Services Tax (GST) increase and fund climate change defences and many other things and still expect to have something left over at the end of that term of Government to add to our past Reserves.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister (Mr Lee Hsien Loong)
sentences.text: But just a few months after that, we are down more than $70 billion.

sections.label: Do not touch Reserves normally
sections.summary: Reserves, big or small, should not be touched in normal times.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister (Mr Lee Hsien Loong)
sentences.text: Whatever Reserves we have, big or small, let us not think of touching them in normal times.

sections.label: PMET share of workforce
sections.summary: The proportion of PMETs in the workforce rose from 40% twenty years ago to close to 60% today.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister (Mr Lee Hsien Loong)
sentences.text: The proportion of PMETs in the workforce has grown steadily from 40% 20 years ago, to close to 60% now, today.

sections.label: Tightening EP and S Pass criteria
sections.summary: The EP entry floor was raised from $3,600 to $3,900 in May and further to $4,500, with $5,000 for financial services, and the S Pass salary floor is being raised.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister (Mr Lee Hsien Loong)
sentences.text: But we need to tighten the EP qualifying criteria, and this is what we have been doing.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister (Mr Lee Hsien Loong)
sentences.text: We raised the EP entry floor from $3,600 to $3,900 in May this year.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister (Mr Lee Hsien Loong)
sentences.text: And MOM just announced last week a further tightening to $4,500, with a higher floor of $5,000 for the financial services sector.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister (Mr Lee Hsien Loong)
sentences.text: We are raising the S Pass salary floor too.

sections.label: Single foreign nationality concentration
sections.summary: A red flag is a company with an over-concentration of a single foreign nationality, especially compared to other companies in the same sector.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister (Mr Lee Hsien Loong)
sentences.text: One specific red flag is when we see a company that has an over-concentration of a single foreign nationality in its ranks, especially when compared to other companies in the same sector.

sections.label: DBS picture taken in India
sections.summary: People berated DBS over a picture that was taken in India, where DBS had opened a new office, not in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister (Mr Lee Hsien Loong)
sentences.text: Many people took offence, and got worked up and berated DBS, flamed them.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister (Mr Lee Hsien Loong)
sentences.text: That picture was taken in India, where DBS had opened a new office, not in Singapore.

sections.label: EDB pipeline higher this year
sections.summary: This year, the Economic Development Board's pipeline is higher than their pipeline was last year.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister (Mr Lee Hsien Loong)
sentences.text: In fact, this year, the Economic Development Board’s (EDB) pipeline is higher than their pipeline was last year.

sections.label: Hyundai Motor R&D facility
sections.summary: Hyundai Motor has announced plans to set up a major facility here for research and development and future mobility technologies.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister (Mr Lee Hsien Loong)
sentences.text: For example, Hyundai Motor has just announced plans to set up a major facility here to undertake research and development (R&D) and develop future mobility technologies.

sections.label: Pharmaceutical company building Singapore facility
sections.summary: A pharmaceutical company plans to build a facility in Singapore to manufacture vaccines.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister (Mr Lee Hsien Loong)
sentences.text: For example, a pharmaceutical company is planning to build a facility in Singapore to manufacture vaccines.

sections.label: Fortune 500 firms considering regional headquarters
sections.summary: Several Fortune 500 firms are considering moving their regional headquarters to Singapore because of political uncertainties elsewhere.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister (Mr Lee Hsien Loong)
sentences.text: Several Fortune 500 firms are considering moving their regional headquarters here because of political uncertainties elsewhere.

sections.label: Foreign companies, talent and Singaporeans
sections.summary: Foreign companies bring talent and cannot be staffed by Singaporeans alone, but once established they create opportunities for Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister (Mr Lee Hsien Loong)
sentences.text: They had the feel of different markets and they could fit into different cultures.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister (Mr Lee Hsien Loong)
sentences.text: And if we want good companies to come to Singapore, we must be prepared to have them come and to bring to Singapore that constellation of talent, to be able to operate out of Singapore and manage activities and locations all over the world.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister (Mr Lee Hsien Loong)
sentences.text: They will employ Singaporeans too, but they cannot be staffed by Singaporeans alone.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister (Mr Lee Hsien Loong)
sentences.text: Once these companies establish themselves here, more Singaporeans will be able to take advantage of the opportunities they create, pick up the skills and knowledge and rise up the ranks.

sections.label: Economic benefits of foreign worker policies
sections.summary: Such companies create good new jobs for Singaporeans and promote entrepreneurship, making the economic benefits of foreign worker policies clear.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister (Mr Lee Hsien Loong)
sentences.text: And, by doing so, they too, create good new jobs for Singaporeans, besides promoting entrepreneurship and making it easier and more attractive to start companies in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister (Mr Lee Hsien Loong)
sentences.text: So, the economic benefits of our foreign worker policies are very clear.

sections.label: Adjusting policies, not turning inwards
sections.summary: Despite current stress, Singapore cannot turn inwards; it will adjust policies to safeguard Singaporean jobs while showing confidence in Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister (Mr Lee Hsien Loong)
sentences.text: We may be under stress now, but we cannot afford to turn inwards.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister (Mr Lee Hsien Loong)
sentences.text: We will adjust our policies to safeguard Singaporean jobs but let us show confidence that Singaporeans can hold our own in the world.

sections.label: Stronger Opposition in Parliament
sections.summary: With a stronger Opposition, PAP Ministers and MPs must raise their game, and the Opposition should put up serious proposals of their own.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister (Mr Lee Hsien Loong)
sentences.text: In Parliament, with a stronger Opposition presence, I expect the tone of the debate to shift.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister (Mr Lee Hsien Loong)
sentences.text: PAP Ministers and MPs will have to raise their game, be prepared for sharper questioning and defend the Government’s policies and decisions while speaking up for their constituents.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister (Mr Lee Hsien Loong)
sentences.text: They also must be prepared for more substantive debates and engagement with the Opposition.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister (Mr Lee Hsien Loong)
sentences.text: I hope the Opposition will also step up, go beyond asking questions and criticising the Government’s proposals, which is part of their responsibility, to go on to put up serious proposals and ideas of their own to be examined and debated and, if found meritorious, adopted, to show that they are willing and able to play their part as a loyal Opposition.

sections.label: Government cannot wait for consensus
sections.summary: The Government must ensure discussions are supported by facts and logic, but cannot wait passively for consensus on major issues affecting the country's fundamental interests.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister (Mr Lee Hsien Loong)
sentences.text: But we, of course, have to make sure that the discussions are supported by facts and logic, and informed by our context and experience.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister (Mr Lee Hsien Loong)
sentences.text: But if it is a major issue which concerns the fundamental interests of the country, the Government cannot wait passively for a consensus to form.

sections.label: Elected government must govern
sections.summary: Having been elected to govern, the Government must govern.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister (Mr Lee Hsien Loong)
sentences.text: Having been elected to govern, we must govern.

sections.label: Government answers questions, increases opposition MPs
sections.summary: The Government shows it has nothing to hide and answers all questions, which is why elected Opposition MPs were increased to 12, including two NCMPs from PSP.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister (Mr Lee Hsien Loong)
sentences.text: It shows the public that the Government has nothing to hide and will answer all questions, however awkward.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister (Mr Lee Hsien Loong)
sentences.text: And that is why we increased the minimum number of elected Opposition MPs in Parliament to 12 and why in this Parliament we have two Non-Constituency MPs (NCMPs) from the Progress Singapore Party (PSP) to top up the 10 from the WP.

sections.label: Government and Opposition share objective
sections.summary: Both Government and Opposition must share an overriding objective to work for Singapore, not just party or supporters, with debate based on principles and facts.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister (Mr Lee Hsien Loong)
sentences.text: At the most fundamental level, to make our politics work, both the Government and Opposition must share an overriding objective – to work for Singapore and not just for our party or our supporters.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister (Mr Lee Hsien Loong)
sentences.text: Our debate must be based on principles and facts and guided by shared ideals and goals.

sections.label: Think for yourself, protect Singapore
sections.summary: One must think for yourself and not just be a mouthpiece, being in politics to protect Singapore's security, grow the economy and secure the future.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister (Mr Lee Hsien Loong)
sentences.text: But to think for yourself and not just to be a mouthpiece.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister (Mr Lee Hsien Loong)
sentences.text: We must be in politics in order to protect Singapore’s security, grow our economy and secure our future.

sections.label: Voters engage and reward parties
sections.summary: Voters have a vital responsibility to engage in public discourse, send the right signals at the ballot box and reward political parties that deliver for the people.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister (Mr Lee Hsien Loong)
sentences.text: Because they have a vital responsibility to engage in the public discourse, to send the right signals at the ballot box and to reward political parties that do the right thing and deliver for the people.

sections.label: PAP special responsibility to Singapore
sections.summary: The PAP says it has a special responsibility to make the system work and provide Singapore's needed leadership.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister (Mr Lee Hsien Loong)
sentences.text: Speaking for the PAP, we have a special responsibility to make our system work and provide the leadership that Singapore needs and deserves.

sections.label: Juncker quote and PAP re-election
sections.summary: Juncker said politicians know what to do but not how to get re-elected, yet the PAP does right and still gets re-elected.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister (Mr Lee Hsien Loong)
sentences.text: Jean-Claude Juncker, who was Prime Minister of Luxembourg and, more recently, the President of the European Commission, said this about European politics and politicians: "We all know what to do; we just do not know how to get re-elected after we have done it." But in Singapore, the PAP Government has been able to do the right thing for Singaporeans – sometimes difficult and hard things – and still get re-elected.

sections.label: No incentive to delay plans
sections.summary: The PAP says it has no incentive to kick the can down the road, so it plans over 50 to 60 years, or 100 for climate change.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister (Mr Lee Hsien Loong)
sentences.text: We have no incentive to kick the can down the road because down the road, we will very likely meet the can ourselves again.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister (Mr Lee Hsien Loong)
sentences.text: Therefore, we make plans over 50 to 60 years, or in the case of climate change, 100 years.

sections.label: Votes for Opposition questions
sections.summary: The passage asks how long Singaporeans can vote for the Opposition expecting other Singaporeans to return the PAP to power.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister (Mr Lee Hsien Loong)
sentences.text: How long can Singaporeans vote for the Opposition in some constituencies, in the expectation that somehow, somewhere else, their fellow Singaporeans will ensure that the PAP is returned to power?

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister (Mr Lee Hsien Loong)
sentences.text: At what point does a vote for a strong Opposition become a vote for a different government?

sections.label: PAP persuading, fighting for support
sections.summary: The PAP says it will persuade good people into politics, fight to win hearts and minds, and win every vote.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister (Mr Lee Hsien Loong)
sentences.text: The PAP feels acutely its special responsibility to keep on doing its best for Singapore and to keep Singapore working in this unique way.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister (Mr Lee Hsien Loong)
sentences.text: We will do our utmost to persuade good men and women to enter politics, to take over the torch and lead the next generation forward.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister (Mr Lee Hsien Loong)
sentences.text: We will fight hard to win the hearts and minds of Singaporeans and win every vote and show Singaporeans that the PAP continues to deserve their support and trust.

sections.label: Airport and airline halted by COVID-19
sections.summary: Forty years of building up the airport and airline came to a halt when COVID-19 came.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister (Mr Lee Hsien Loong)
sentences.text: Forty years of building up our airport and airline, COVID-19 came and all of that suddenly came to a halt.

sections.label: COVID-19 crisis and unity
sections.summary: COVID-19 will be an occasion to do better, emerge stronger and become more united, as in previous crises.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister (Mr Lee Hsien Loong)
sentences.text: As in all the previous crises, COVID-19 will be the occasion for us to do better, emerge stronger and become more united.

sections.label: Reserves and Temasek NIRC
sections.summary: The aim is slowing the growth slope of the Reserves, and in 2015 the House agreed to include Temasek in the NIRC formula.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: When we talk about the Reserves, we are not talking about raiding them.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: It is about slowing the growth slope of the Reserves.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In 2015, this House, including the Members of the Workers’ Party (WP), we agreed to include Temasek in the Net Investment Returns Contribution (NIRC) formula.

sections.label: HDB offices before 1991
sections.summary: Before 1991, HDB built offices for everybody, every MP, including Opposition MPs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The position prior to 1991, HDB built offices for everybody, every MP, including Opposition MPs.

sections.label: Police, Armed Forces, Opposition
sections.summary: The Police and the Armed Forces will carry it through, and the speaker believes in an Opposition in a Parliamentary democracy.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The Police, the Armed Forces will carry it through.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: I believe in an Opposition in a Parliamentary democracy.

sections.label: Rule on expected earnings
sections.summary: The House agreed that of expected earnings, half will be spent and half reinvested for the future, and should stick to this for a long time.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Hsien Loong
sentences.text: We thought this over carefully and we debated this in the House.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Hsien Loong
sentences.text: We agreed upon a rule which we felt was a fair distribution between the present and the future generations – which is that, of the expected earnings, half will be taken to be spent, half will go back and be reinvested and will be for the future.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Hsien Loong
sentences.text: We made that decision knowing that there would be ups and downs, knowing that one day, we would be short of money, knowing that we should stick to this for quite a long time and not revisit this as soon as we need money.

sections.label: Drawing on reserves
sections.summary: It can come down for any number of reasons, and they may have to draw on them, like this year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Hsien Loong
sentences.text: It can come down for any number of reasons.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Hsien Loong
sentences.text: We may have to draw on them, like we did this year.

sections.label: Opposition and voting government out
sections.summary: The passage says there will be Opposition to hold the party and Government to account, and voters can vote the Government out to change policy.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Hsien Loong
sentences.text: There will be Opposition in this House, to hold a party to account and to hold the Government to account.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Hsien Loong
sentences.text: So, if you think that the Government is doing the wrong thing in terms of MPs' offices, in terms of MPs and the community centres, by all means, vote the Government out, put a new government in, change the government and change the policy.

sections.label: Sincere honest voting system
sections.summary: The passage states the system works only if people vote sincerely and honestly according to what they really want.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Hsien Loong
sentences.text: Because the system can only work if people vote sincerely and honestly in accordance with what they really want and to produce a result which matches their true intentions.

sections.label: Minister decides Ministry direction
sections.summary: The passage describes a Minister deciding contents, direction and details, overriding officials if necessary, and how the Ministerial Task Force operated.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Hsien Loong
sentences.text: And when he runs the Ministry, he must decide what the contents are, what the direction is, the details; and if necessary, override the officials and decide on the direction.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Hsien Loong
sentences.text: That is how the Ministerial Task Force has operated – long discussions, all views heard.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Hsien Loong
sentences.text: The staff did not recommend the circuit breaker.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Hsien Loong
sentences.text: I said better think about this carefully, do not make a seat-of-the-pants decision; go back, sleep on it, work out the proposal, work out another proposal, 30% more draconian; come back day after tomorrow, come back tomorrow morning, talk about it, discuss, decide.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Hsien Loong
sentences.text: It is a big decision, $5 billion dollars of Supplementary Budget.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Hsien Loong
sentences.text: If the new government comes in, can it know how to do this and have that feel and that trust and that confidence of Singaporeans as well as their officials as well as investors and everybody else watching us?

sections.label: Free rider voting PAP
sections.summary: The passage says telling voters someone else will vote PAP is a free rider, taking advantage of others electing a government.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Hsien Loong
sentences.text: But I would say however, if you stand and you tell people, "Vote for me, I will be a better MP than the other one, the PAP MP", I think that is entirely reasonable.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Hsien Loong
sentences.text: But if you say, "Vote for me; somebody else will vote for the PAP and therefore the PAP will be the government", that the economists will call a free rider.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Hsien Loong
sentences.text: It means that you are taking advantage of somebody else who is doing the duty of electing a government for the nation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Hsien Loong
sentences.text: And you are not doing your part expressing your true views and preference as a voter whom you want to be the next government.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Hsien Loong
sentences.text: And if everybody takes that attitude, then you are going to end up with a government which you do not want.

sections.label: Elections beyond Town Council
sections.summary: The passage states that elections are not just about the Town Council.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Hsien Loong
sentences.text: Elections are not just about the Town Council.

sections.label: Strong Government seat margin
sections.summary: The passage asks the Prime Minister about voters seeing a gap because the Government controls over 90% of seats.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: What I want to ask the Prime Minister is, Singapore voters looking at the situation today see that there is actually a gap between having a strong Government, because the Government at the moment controls over 90% of the seats.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Because of that margin, you cannot prevent the voters from thinking, "Actually, there is a margin of error I can afford.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: So, as a result, I can have the best of both worlds – a strong Government and a strong Opposition voice in Parliament.

sections.label: Social safety net and Reserves
sections.summary: The passage asks whether national Reserves returns should be used to improve Singaporeans' financial position so they can participate in the new economy.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: For example, on the issue of social safety net, what we are saying is, "Do you not think Singaporeans' livelihoods now is too hard?" And they are so hard to the extent that you cannot expect them to become entrepreneurs because their financial security is not there.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: As a result, we say, "We know we have this amount of national Reserves, can we not use the returns and help to improve the financial position of the Singaporeans so that they can have peace of mind to think of participating in the new economy that we are trying to put into our country?" A lot of the debates have gone on about recruitment drop, how to create jobs and how to take back some of the jobs from the foreigners, which is not really something that we want to go very far with.

sections.label: Pritam Singh's argument
sections.summary: Mr Pritam Singh is not the only one making this argument, and if everyone makes it, everyone will be in trouble.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Hsien Loong
sentences.text: Mr Pritam Singh is not the only one making this argument.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Hsien Loong
sentences.text: And if everyone makes this argument, everyone is going to be in trouble.

sections.label: Global Financial Crisis Reserves use
sections.summary: During the Global Financial Crisis, while running MAS, the speaker sought the President's approval to use $150 billion of past Reserves to safeguard bank deposits.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister, Minister for Finance and Coordinating Minister for Economic Policies (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: The first time was during the Global Financial Crisis when I was running the Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS) and we sought the President's approval for the use of $150 billion of our past Reserves to safeguard bank deposits.

sections.label: Approval and $52 billion draw
sections.summary: After tough questions, approval was given and $52 billion of past Reserves was drawn as part of an almost $100 billion package.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister, Minister for Finance and Coordinating Minister for Economic Policies (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: Eventually, they approved, after very, very tough questions given to me and my team, and we drew $52 billion of past Reserves as part of this almost $100 billion package.

sections.label: Debts paid by future generations
sections.summary: The massive debts incurred will have to be paid for by future generations.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister, Minister for Finance and Coordinating Minister for Economic Policies (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: The massive debts that have been incurred will have to be paid for by future generations.

sections.label: Volatile economy and crises
sections.summary: The speaker says he asks that question of himself because the economy will be more volatile, citing past crises including COVID-19.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister, Minister for Finance and Coordinating Minister for Economic Policies (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: I can tell Mr Pritam Singh that I asked that question of myself all the time, because the nature of the economy is that it is going to be more volatile.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister, Minister for Finance and Coordinating Minister for Economic Policies (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: We had the Asian Financial Crisis, we had the Global Financial Crisis, in between, we had SARS, the dotcom bubble and now, we have COVID-19.

sections.label: Global financial crises and crashes
sections.summary: The speaker says a serious financial and economic crisis occurred and that panics and crashes will continue in the global economy.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister, Minister for Finance and Coordinating Minister for Economic Policies (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: A financial crisis and economic crisis of a very serious nature, I think we must expect that panics and crashes will continue to happen in the global economy.

sections.label: Second diploma or degree option
sections.summary: Polytechnics and universities could offer graduating students the option to study a second diploma or degree in a different field instead of adding to jobseekers.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Given the challenging job market now and instead of adding to the jobseekers' pool, polytechnics and universities could consider offering graduating students the option to study a second diploma or degree in a different field.

sections.label: Retirement age of 70
sections.summary: The passage proposes considering 70 as a new retirement age.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Consider 70 to be a new retirement age.

sections.label: Women leaders and Singaporean women
sections.summary: The speaker cites international women leaders who managed COVID-19 well and urges harnessing Singaporean women for roles before hiring foreign talents.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
sentences.text: I believe it is no coincidence that several international women leaders have managed the COVID-19 crisis well, for example, Prime Minister Jacinda Adern of New Zealand, Prime Minister Sanna Marin of Finland, Chancellor Angela Merkel of Germany and so on.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
sentences.text: We can harness the potential of our Singaporean women and encourage qualified Singaporean women to fill the roles first before hiring foreign talents.

sections.label: Permanent workplace shifts and HR review
sections.summary: The passage says work from home, e-commerce and home-based businesses are now the norm and should be made permanent, and suggests MOM review unfair HR practices.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Work from home, e-commerce and home-based businesses have now become the norm and we should make these structural shifts in the workplace permanent.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Perhaps MOM could embark on a review of potentially unfair or even discriminatory HR practices, such as reducing the gender wage gap.

sections.label: 200-runner charity relay
sections.summary: A 200-hour relay by 200 runners covering 2,000 kilometres raised $1.6 million, above the $1 million target, with five MPs among the runners.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Each runner ran either 10 kilometres or 20 kilometres and had to raise at least $5,000 each.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
sentences.text: After months of hard work and fund-raising, the 200-hour relay by the 200 runners, covering 2,000 kilometres, was completed successfully.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
sentences.text: That relay raised a total of $1.6 million, well over the target of $1 million.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Amongst the 200 runners, there are five MPs in this House, including Mr Speaker, Sir, who ran in that relay.

sections.label: Business competitiveness and workforce balance
sections.summary: Businesses should improve competitiveness, stay agile, cut middle and senior executives, and balance local and foreign employees.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Businesses should improve their competitiveness, keep agile, reduce the number of middle and senior executives and balance the proportions between local and foreign employees.

sections.label: Older workers and ageing demographics
sections.summary: The speaker notes older workers' vulnerability and Singapore's ageing population, with citizens 65 and older nearly doubling by 2030.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: I resonate with them because I have been seeing the vulnerability of our older adult workers over 50 years old and those above 60 years old feel even more uncertain and anxious this period in my constituency.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: We have started the most significant demographic shift of this generation – the near doubling of citizens aged 65 and older by 2030, with the number of elderly citizens projected to be about 900,000, or one in four by then.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: As Minister of State Ms Gan Siow Huang had mentioned, the median age of our resident labour force today has also risen to 44, compared to 41 just a decade ago, and it will continue to rise.

sections.label: Support for older worker employability
sections.summary: Support comes from the SG United Jobs and Skills Package, Jobs Growth Incentive, and Tripartite Committee on Employability of Older Workers.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Whether it be the strong support from the SG United Jobs and Skills Package, the new Jobs Growth Incentive or efforts from the Tripartite Committee on Employability of Older Workers.

sections.label: Job redesign for mature workforce
sections.summary: The speaker helped NCSS and Pan Pacific Hotel Group start partnership dialogues on job redesign for mature workers, such as urban farming roles.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: To begin with, I have helped to bring together the NCSS and Pan Pacific Hotel Group to start dialogues on partnership to join forces and combine the social and business perspectives to enable awareness and resources for new job redesigns for the mature workforce.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: For example, the hotel group in their sustainability pursuit are thinking of new roles such as urban farming specialists where they will encourage older workers to pursue and in a dignified way.

sections.label: Surveys on older adults' wellbeing
sections.summary: Surveys reported in The Straits Times found older adults' life satisfaction dropped and social isolation and anxiety rose during the period.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: The findings from their population-representative monthly survey, with about 7,500 respondents, tracking the lives of Singaporeans aged 55 to 75 during this period were reported in The Straits Times on 28 August this year.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: There was an important finding: older adults experienced a drop in overall life satisfaction by 3.8% in April 2020 and 4% in May, as compared to January 2020.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Respondents mentioned that they experienced a sharp increase in feelings of social isolation, with individuals living alone experiencing larger increases.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: One factor that impacts quality of life is job security, and it is telling that many respondents in the survey expressed anxiety about the future, with about a third of respondents expressing being very or extremely worried about the health of their loved ones and the economy.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: In another survey conducted by the National University Health System (NUHS) Mind Science Centre on mental health resilience published in The Straits Times on 19 August this year, it found that younger Singaporeans 45 years and below are more likely to feel anxious and less mentally resilient than those aged 45 and above.

sections.label: Preventive mental health support
sections.summary: The speaker urges reducing stigma of help-seeking and expanding preventive mental health support in polyclinics and GP clinics.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: We must continue to reduce the stigma of help seeking behaviours for Singaporeans, especially when it is at the early onset of mental health issues, such as mild depression or anxiety, for preventive care nearer to home in the community.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: I hope to encourage more preventive mental health support in primary care providers, including the polyclinics and general practitioner (GP) clinics, which are closer to most people, with more support in terms of subsidies and integrated care with social services.

sections.label: MSF income mobility paper
sections.summary: A 2018 MSF paper found 14.3% of Singaporeans born 1978-1982 to lowest-income families reached the top 20%.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth and Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: According to a 2018 paper published by the MSF, 14.3% of Singaporeans born between 1978 and 1982 to families from the lowest 20% in terms of household income made it to the top 20%, significantly higher than other developed countries, like the US and the UK.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth and Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: Families who make up this statistic are completely uplifted in a single generation.

sections.label: ASPIRE, UPLIFT, KidSTART efforts
sections.summary: ASPIRE, UPLIFT and KidSTART have addressed uneven starting points, but society's view of success has barely changed.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth and Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: To be sure through the work of the work of the ASPIRE committee and programmes such as UPLIFT and KidSTART, we have done quite a fair over the years to address uneven starting points.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth and Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: But little has changed in the way that we, as a society, perceive success and how to get there.

sections.label: Respect for blue-collar work
sections.summary: Dr Cheng Ching Siang, echoed by Mr Louis Ng, suggested Singaporeans develop respect for blue-collar work.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth and Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: A good start, perhaps, is for Singaporeans to develop a sense of respect for blue-collar work, an idea put forth by Dr Cheng Ching Siang in his Forum page contribution to The Straits Times and echoed by Mr Louis Ng earlier.

sections.label: Apprenticeships defined
sections.summary: Apprenticeships, not internships or cheap labour, offer a blend of on- and off-the-job learning.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth and Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: Not to be confused with internships or mistaken as a euphemism for cheap labour, apprenticeships offer a blend of on- and off-the-job learning.

sections.label: European apprenticeships pathway
sections.summary: Apprenticeships are widely offered in Germany and Switzerland, leading to skilled blue- and white-collar employment.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth and Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: Apprenticeships are widely offered in European countries like Germany and Switzerland as a pathway that eventually leads to skilled employment in both blue- and white-collared roles.

sections.label: OnePeople.sg CNA success survey
sections.summary: A 2018 OnePeople.sg and CNA survey found lower-class respondents cited hard work, education and knowing the right people for success.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth and Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: On success, a 2018 survey commissioned by OnePeople.sg and CNA revealed very telling differences between different social classes.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth and Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: Respondents from the lower class cited: (a) hard work, (b) education and (c) knowing the right people, in this order, as key factors for success.

sections.label: Mentorship for youths
sections.summary: Mentorship programmes give young people from families with limited networks access to advice on career, education and life.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth and Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: To provide access to young people from families where networks they can tap on for advice on career, education and lessons in life are limited.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth and Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: This is where mentorship programmes for our youths can be a useful counter against the natural forces of entrenchment, that critical leveller between the haves and the have nots.

sections.label: Social mobility in Singapore
sections.summary: Social mobility must remain a defining part of Singapore's social compact to keep Singapore going.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth and Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: For us here in Singapore, we can and will believe in Singapore, only if social mobility continues to feature as a defining part of our social compact.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth and Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: Deputy Speaker, Sir, it takes an entire village to raise a child, and we owe it to each of the 39,000 Singaporean babies that we welcome to this world each year to ensure the continued and deliberate injection of hope and conviction, so that as one people, we, can keep Singapore going.

sections.label: Voters want check and balance
sections.summary: Singapore voters want a more effective and constructive political landscape with a robust and cohesive check and balance system.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Singapore voters want a more effective and constructive political landscape.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
sentences.text: They want a robust and cohesive check and balance system, and not a political system guided by the “ownself check ownself” approach.

sections.label: Live telecast of Parliament
sections.summary: A spokesman said live broadcasts risk turning Parliament into theatre and do not add transparency, but the Member agrees to live telecast.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
sentences.text: A spokesman for Minister Grace Fu, responding to this through the media, said "Live broadcasts of Parliament risk turning the House into a ‘form of theatre’ and do not add to transparency", and further said, "An element of public performance is unavoidable because Singaporeans want to see their concerns expressed, and hear their questions asked and answered in Parliament." In short, the answer given is that the live telecast does not improve transparency; in fact, it poses a risk of transforming Parliamentary sessions into performance theatre.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
sentences.text: On this note, Sir, I would like to state for the record that I agree to having live telecast of Parliamentary sessions, because in my view, any Member who wants to put on a theatre performance in Parliament will still showcase their acting because they know that, although there is no live telecast, there are recordings done every second, from the start to the end of the Parliamentary session.

sections.label: PA grassroots advisers dissatisfaction
sections.summary: Many expressed dissatisfaction over PA grassroots advisers in alternative party constituencies being given to the defeated ruling party candidate.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Lately, many have expressed dissatisfaction, especially on social media, over the role of People's Association’s (PA) grassroot advisers in the constituency under the care of alternative parties being given to the defeated ruling party candidate in the general election.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The PAP candidate is also, at the same time, holding the post of PAP branch chairman for the same constituency.

sections.label: PA grassroots advisers proposal
sections.summary: Explanations failed to convince observers, and the Member proposed appointing non-partisan senior public officers as PA grassroots advisers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Among the reasons is that the main role of the grassroots advisers is to present and explain government policies and the opposition MPs will not be able to do this role well in situations where they do not support these policies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
sentences.text: But the explanation and reasons given failed to convince a large group of political observers amongst the public who still express the view that the PA is used as a platform to fulfil the political interests of the ruling party.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
sentences.text: I have proposed in this House to appoint senior public officers such as a Chief Executive Officer or Director, whether still in service or retired, and are not members of any political party, to be appointed as PA grassroots advisers.

sections.label: Turban and hijab workplace incidents
sections.summary: A Sikh man was asked to remove his turban for a telephone interview, and a Muslim salesgirl was told to remove her hijab as unprofessional.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
sentences.text: One, where a Sikh man was asked whether he could remove his turban during a telephone interview because the reason given was that his appearance could cause unease.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The second incident involved a Muslim salesgirl who was told to remove her hijab because it was considered unprofessional.

sections.label: Supporting families caring for seniors
sections.summary: Government, local communities and society need stronger interventions to support families providing dignified care for seniors.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
sentences.text: While the individual and family must continue to be cardinal and first line of support, we also need stronger interventions – by Government, local communities and society at large – to support families in providing dignified care for our seniors.

sections.label: Government bearing care costs
sections.summary: Higher care standards raise costs, and the Government should bear the bulk of incremental costs and review the subsidy framework.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
sentences.text: To raise and sustain an ecosystem of capability building, innovation and human capital development, cost of care in the sector would have to go up.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
sentences.text: I believe there is scope for the Government to bear the bulk of incremental costs for these higher standards of care.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
sentences.text: At the same time, while most nursing home residents are already getting some level of Government subsidies, I would urge a review of the current subsidy framework to see if we can do more and be even more progressive.

sections.label: Flattening healthcare cost inflation
sections.summary: As the population ages, healthcare spending demands grow, so the healthcare cost inflation curve must be flattened.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
sentences.text: At the same time, demands for healthcare spending will only grow as our population ages.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
sentences.text: Therefore, while we keep at flattening the epidemic and unemployment curves in the COVID-19 new normal, we must also urgently flatten our healthcare cost inflation curve.

sections.label: Growing home-based care capabilities
sections.summary: Home-based care capabilities must grow in a major way, including protocols, technology, financing and regulations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
sentences.text: Indeed, we need to grow our home-based care capabilities in a major way, including the protocols, technology, financing and regulations.

sections.label: Nursing workforce and foreign nurses
sections.summary: Care remains high-touch, so more nurses are needed, maintaining a strong Singaporean Core while complementing the workforce with foreign nurses.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
sentences.text: We continue to improve productivity through technology and job redesign, but fundamentally, care remains a high-touch, highly human endeavour, especially if we want care to be dignified.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
sentences.text: We need more nurses going forward and it is key that we maintain a strong Singaporean Core.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
sentences.text: So, to this end, we have intensified recruitment and reviewed salaries, training and career pathways for Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
sentences.text: But we also need to complement our workforce with foreign nurses.

sections.label: Dependency Ratio Ceiling healthcare review
sections.summary: The speaker suggests a comprehensive review of the Dependency Ratio Ceiling and manpower strategies for the healthcare sector, especially intermediate and long-term care.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
sentences.text: To this end, I would also suggest a comprehensive review of the Dependency Ratio Ceiling and manpower strategies for the healthcare sector, especially for intermediate and long-term care.

sections.label: Three suggestions for eldercare
sections.summary: The speaker makes three suggestions: build nursing homes and raise subsidies, explore home care services, and give caregivers financial help and parent care leave.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
sentences.text: Here I have three suggestions: first, the Government should focus on developing and building nursing homes, inject more resources, improve the quality of care beyond basic care, and at the same time increase subsidies for Singaporeans; second, explore more comprehensive home care services because hospital wards can never be as comfortable as a bedroom at home; and third, provide more financial assistance to full-time caregivers and establish a suitable parent care leave regime through the Tripartite partners.

sections.label: Dignified care for seniors
sections.summary: The speaker says hard choices on treatments are needed to limit costs, more people must provide care, and society must care for caregivers and seniors.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
sentences.text: At the same time, we need to make hard choices on treatments and therapies and involve our tertiary care model to keep a lid on overall costs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
sentences.text: Yet, overall costs would go up and these would have to be funded.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
sentences.text: And certainly, our society would need more passionate individuals, both local and foreign, to step forward to provide the best care possible for our seniors.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
sentences.text: And finally, as a society, we must also care better for our caregivers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
sentences.text: We must be a society that commits to dignified care for our seniors, because it is the right thing to do.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
sentences.text: And we must be a society that commits to stepping in and stepping up to help each other with the burdens of care, especially where the individual or the family is unable to manage, because this is who we must be as a people.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: On Monday, during the Debate on the Motion of Thanks to the President, Mr Dennis Tan stated that he had to rectify the position of his posters, arising from two complaints about his campaign posters to the Elections Department or ELD during the recent General Election or GE.

sections.label: Tan posters and ELD complaints
sections.summary: Mr Tan acknowledged ELD was even-handed in handling complaints from all parties, and ELD has received no report from him on his posters being pulled down.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: When challenged in this House by Mr Murali, Mr Tan acknowledged that ELD has been even-handed in handling complaints received from all political parties and candidates.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: ELD has not received any report from Mr Tan on his allegations that his posters were pulled down from the original height.

sections.label: Tan reply to ELD
sections.summary: Mr Tan told ELD on 2 September 2020 he made no report during the GE and has no plans to, and ELD will investigate such allegations thoroughly and impartially.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: Mr Tan has replied to ELD on 2 September 2020 that he did not make a report to ELD during the GE as he was focusing on his election campaign and he has no plans to do so now.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: ELD takes such allegations seriously and will investigate them thoroughly and impartially.

sections.label: Government-supported preschool places expansion
sections.summary: The Government announced it is raising Government-supported preschool places from just over 50% of the market today to 80% by 2025, with enhanced subsidies since January.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Education and Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: The Government has announced that it is ramping up the provision of Government-supported preschool places, from just over 50% of the market today to 80% by 2025.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Education and Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: Since January this year, many families are now paying less for preschool given enhanced subsidies.

sections.label: KidSTART support for lower income families
sections.summary: The speaker hopes scaling up programmes like KidSTART, which supports lower income families and children's health, nutrition and education, will benefit more families.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Education and Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: They say it takes a village to raise a child.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Education and Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: I hope that with the scale-up of programmes such as KidSTART, which provides holistic support to lower income families and focus on the health, nutrition and education of their children, more of these children and their families can benefit.

sections.label: Education system mindset shift
sections.summary: The education system is reducing assessments and changing PSLE scoring, but society, employers and parents must also shift away from overemphasising grades, with DSA changes ensuring holistic assessment.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Education and Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: Our education system has been making big moves to bring about a mindset shift to look beyond academic achievements, by reducing school-based assessments and making changes to the PSLE scoring system.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Education and Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: But to do this successfully, we all need to move away from an overemphasis on grades, not just within the school system but a broader mindset shift in society, including from among employers and parents.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Education and Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: And we need to make real changes to some of the current ways of doing things, such as a greater recognition of skills when evaluating someone for a job.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Education and Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: But even as we do so, we must be careful not to rely solely on tried-and-tested methods, such as assessing students based on certificates which show demonstrated achievements.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Education and Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: This would only serve to transfer the competition for results from the academic arena to the non-academic arena, with better off parents being more likely to send their children for extra training in DSA areas.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Education and Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: Instead, we have started making changes to DSA over the past few years, and parents and children can be assured that our schools are adopting a much more holistic assessment, looking beyond past achievements.

sections.label: Sports selection beyond specific competencies
sections.summary: In sports selection, schools are encouraged to look beyond sports-specific competencies and also for natural abilities such as agility, coordination and speed.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Education and Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: For example, in sports selection, we encourage schools to look beyond sports-specific competencies, such as the ability to dribble or serve a ball, but to also look for natural abilities such as agility, coordination and speed.

sections.label: Support for special educational needs
sections.summary: Children with special educational needs will access quality and affordable SEN support, with six SPED schools reducing fees by at least 25% and more SPED schools to be built.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Education and Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: And I thought to myself, "Isn’t this what the education system is about?" For our children with special educational needs, we will make sure they can access quality and affordable SEN support provisions in both mainstream and SPED schools.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Education and Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: We recently worked with six SPED schools to reduce their fees by at least 25% for Singapore Citizens since the start of this year, and will be building more SPED schools over the next few years.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Education and Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: Yesterday, I had also announced a new Human Resource package to support our SPED teachers in their career and professional development aspirations.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Education and Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: We are also intervening earlier through early intervention programmes in pre-schools and for those with moderate to severe developmental needs, through the Early Intervention Programme for Infants and Children.

sections.label: COVID-19 impact on families and marriages
sections.summary: Teenagers may be in low spirits staying home, family violence enquiries rose about 10% during circuit breaker, and marriages from January to July dropped 23%.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Education and Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: Teenagers may be in low spirits as they must stay at home for long periods and are unable to meet their friends as and when they like.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Education and Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: We saw an increase in family violence related enquiries during the circuit breaker period; the queries received by MSF increased by about 10% during the circuit breaker period as compared to the period before circuit breaker in March.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Education and Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: The total number of marriages registered from January to July this year dropped by 23% as compared to the same period last year.

sections.label: COVID-19 financial and psychological assistance
sections.summary: The Temporary Relief Fund, COVID-19 Support Grant extended to December, and National CARE Hotline launched in April, which received about 28,000 calls.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Education and Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: In terms of financial assistance, we introduced the Temporary Relief Fund to help lower and middle-income Singaporeans and families.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Education and Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: We also introduced the COVID-19 Support Grant, for Singaporeans who are unemployed or suffered significant income loss, and the application window for the grant has been extended to December this year.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Education and Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: To combat the psychological effects of COVID-19, we launched the National CARE Hotline in April this year to help Singaporeans who need emotional or psychological support during the pandemic.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Education and Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: It is worth noting that since its launch more than four months ago, the hotline has received about 28,000 calls for help.

sections.label: HDB mortgage late payment charges
sections.summary: HDB reports a threefold rise in households struggling with mortgage payments, and late payment charges are suspended until end of this month.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: According to HDB, from April to June this year, there has been a threefold increase of households facing financial difficulty to make their monthly mortgage payments, compared to the same period last year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: To address this, besides various repayment solutions offered by HDB, late payment charges have been suspended until the end of this month.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: I would suggest that HDB consider extending this until the end of this year.

sections.label: Family violence reports increase
sections.summary: Police reported a 22% rise in family violence reports since the circuit breaker, and MSF saw a 14% increase in related inquiries.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: The police reported an increase of 22% reports of family violence since the beginning of the circuit breaker period.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: According to MSF, adult and child protection services saw a 14% increase in inquiries related to domestic conflicts and violence in the first two weeks of the circuit breaker period alone.

sections.label: Children under her care
sections.summary: She currently has eight children under her care.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Currently, she has eight children under her care.

sections.label: Temporary foster care-givers pool
sections.summary: Some jurisdictions have licensed temporary foster care-givers who relieve current foster parents and may attract more temporary care-givers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Some jurisdictions have built up a pool of licensed, temporary foster care-givers who can step in and offer relief for current foster parents so that they can recharge and not now, but in the long-term, the flexibility and short-term nature may even attract more to be temporary foster care-givers before they decide to be full-time.

sections.label: Syariah Court jurisdiction for faraid wakaf
sections.summary: AMLA could be amended to widen the Syariah Court's jurisdiction to faraid, wakaf and inheritance disputes, with mediation or arbitration.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Here I would like to suggest that the Administration of Muslim Law Act (AMLA) can be amended to widen the Syariah Court's jurisdiction limits to not only handle divorce cases but also disputes involving faraid, wakaf and inheritance issues.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Now, although the faraid Certificate of Inheritance is issued by the Syariah Court and wakaf administration is under Muis' purview, any dispute related to it should be tried by the Civil Court.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: I am proposing for a dispute resolution framework in faraidh and wakaf cases, which can include mediation or arbitration at the Syariah Court.

sections.label: M3 approach leveraging Government resources
sections.summary: The M3 approach has enabled professionals and volunteers of any race to work together and generate new ideas.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: For example, by fully leveraging on Government resources and relooking issues from the national lens, the M3 approach has enabled professionals and volunteers, regardless of race, to work together, combine their efforts and generate new constructive ideas.

sections.label: GDP per capita 1960 to 1990
sections.summary: Singapore's GDP per capita rose from US$449 in 1960 to US$11,862 by 1990, when Lee Kuan Yew handed over to Goh Chok Tong.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: In 1960, our GDP per capita was US$449.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: By 1990, at the time Mr Lee Kuan Yew handed over to Mr Goh Chok Tong, it had risen to US$11,862 per capita.

sections.label: GDP per capita by 2006
sections.summary: By 2006, when Goh Chok Tong handed over, GDP per capita had risen to US$33,769.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: By 2006, when Mr Goh Chok Tong handed over, GDP per capita had risen to US$33,769.

sections.label: GDP in 2019 World Bank figures
sections.summary: In 2019, World Bank figures put GDP at around US$65,233, a little under double the 2006 figure.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: In 2019, when the last figures were available from the World Bank, the GDP stood at around US$65,233 – again, a very big number, a little under double from 2006.

sections.label: Currency trading hub sector employment
sections.summary: A currency trading hub started over 50 years ago evolved into a sector employing 170,000 people, 70% of them Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: But he highlighted that this sector really started again as an entrepreneurial venture in a little over 50 years ago when Singapore decided to open up as a currency trading hub.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: This slowly evolved into having more and more high-quality jobs here and we now have a sector that employs 170,000 people, of which 70% are Singaporeans.

sections.label: Racial and religious equality policies
sections.summary: The speaker commends racial and religious equality policies such as HDB racial quotas and the GRC system, and says they are important.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: One policy that I commend and which I think we should be very slow to release on is actually equality for the different races and religions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Some of these include racial quotas in HDB blocks as well as the GRC system that ensures minority representation in Parliament.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Earlier in the debate, Ms Sylvia Lim mentioned we should relook at these.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: It is okay to relook at these policies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: But I would firmly say that I think these policies are important.

sections.label: Free and compulsory primary education
sections.summary: In the early years of Independence, the Pioneer Generation saw education as an important leveller, so primary education was made free and compulsory.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: In our early years of Independence, the Pioneer Generation realised that education was an important leveller.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: So, Primary education was made free and compulsory.

sections.label: Pre-school enrolment not universal
sections.summary: Pre-school enrolment is improving but is still not universal.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: The result of this is that pre-school enrolment, while getting better, is still not universal.

sections.label: Vocational and academic salary gap
sections.summary: The speaker agrees all pathways should lead to success but notes a significant salary discrepancy between vocational and academic paths.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: I agree with the focus of the Ministry that different pathways to success should be there and all pathways should lead to success.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: But one area where there is significant discrepancy is the salaries that come out from the vocational path and the academic path.

sections.label: Foreign labour access lever
sections.summary: Employers deemed to discriminate against Singaporeans have their access to foreign labour cut or reduced.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: The current lever is that if an employer is deemed to be discriminating against Singaporeans, their access to foreign labour is cut or reduced.

sections.label: Legislation on workplace discrimination
sections.summary: MOM may act against companies acting unfairly, but dismissed individuals do not feel vindicated, so the speaker sees room for workplace discrimination legislation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: MOM may take action against the company, if it deems the company is not acting fairly, but the individual who feels he may have lost his job does not feel vindicated.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: It is here that I think there isroom for legislation on workplace discrimination.

sections.label: Culture and sports during COVID-19
sections.summary: With the COVID-19 pandemic, one may be tempted to put culture and sports on the backburner and focus on lower level needs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: As the world is battered by the COVID-19 pandemic, one may be tempted to say we should put culture and sports on the backburner and we focus all our energies on our lower level needs, such as physical safety, economic survival and so on.

sections.label: Importance of keeping people employed
sections.summary: The passage states it is important to keep people engaged through work, citing an occupational medicine saying that the most dangerous employment is unemployment.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: That is why it is so important to keep people engaged through work.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: That is why there is a saying in occupational medicine – the most dangerous employment is unemployment.

sections.label: Nation-building in adversity
sections.summary: Nation-building is argued to be more urgent in adversity and must include culture and sports.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: One may even argue, nation-building is more urgent and important when the nation is faced with great adversity.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: But these nation-building areas must also include our culture and our sports.

sections.label: Xinyao music and artistes
sections.summary: Xinyao songs gave pride to students and young adults, and its artistes mentored singers like JJ Lin, Kit Chan and Stephanie Sun.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: Great songs were written, and thousands of students and young adults derived great pride and joy from this uniquely Singapore genre of Chinese music.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: These Xinyao artistes later mentored younger singers and musicians such as JJ Lin, Kit Chan and Stephanie Sun.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: Famous Xinyao songs now etched into the consciousness of the Chinese-speaking community include "Voices from the Heart", 小人物的心声, which has been staged in two National Day Parades, and "The Small Stream that Flows Forever", 细水长流, which our Prime Minister sang in the 2014 National Day Rally.

sections.label: Sports and national consciousness
sections.summary: Sports add to a country's collective and national consciousness and can heal scars and unite a country.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: Sports add to the collective and national consciousness of a country.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: It can even heal scars and unite a country.

sections.label: Invictus, Xinyao, rugby examples
sections.summary: Invictus, Xinyao and the 1995 South African World Cup Rugby team embody youth, culture and sports, which MCCY focuses on.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: Invictus means "unconquered" in Latin which sort of sums up the spirit that is needed in adversity and crises. "Invictus" was a poem written by 18th century poet, William Ernest Henley, that Nelson Mandela often recited to inspire himself while he was imprisoned on Robben Island for 18 years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: I gave these two examples of Xinyao and The 1995 South African World Cup Rugby team because they embody the very elements that our society in which MCCY focuses on – the youth, culture and sports.
