sentences.text: And this is something that I think deserves a second look.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: I just want to point out that the self-help groups do actually provide monetary contributions to OnePeople.sg as well.

sections.label: PMEs reporting lost opportunities
sections.summary: At least 20 PMEs wrote in the past month about losing job and workplace opportunities and feeling somewhat discriminated against.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: At least 20 PMEs have written to me in the past month, sharing with me their loss of opportunities at taking on jobs and at our workplaces, to the extent of feeling somewhat discriminated against.

sections.label: MOM policy announcements welcomed
sections.summary: The speaker welcomes MOM's announcements on adjusting EP and S Pass qualifying salaries, new Fair Consideration Framework requirements, and greater scrutiny of applicants.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: In that same vein, I welcome the policy announcements last Thursday by MOM in (a) adjusting the Employment Pass (EP) and S Pass qualifying salaries, (b) imposing new Fair Consideration Framework Requirements, and (c) applying greater scrutiny on EP and S Pass applicants.

sections.label: Raised EP and S Pass salaries
sections.summary: MOM raised EP and S Pass qualifying salaries, with EP differentiation by sector, while union leaders and PMEs fear employers will repackage pay to retain foreigners.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: Although the EP salary minimum was just raised in May 2020, I am heartened that MOM has raised the qualifying salaries of both Employment Pass and S Pass holders to further level the playing field for our Singaporean PMETs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: While we raise the qualifying salary of EP holders, I am glad that MOM has put in a place a differentiation of the EP qualifying salaries for sectors such as the financial services sector.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: Since the announcement of these changes last Thursday, union leaders and PMEs I have spoken to have raised concerns that employers would merely raise the salaries or repackage the compensation and benefits of their foreign PMETs, to keep within the boundaries of the rules and retain them – something that is easily done in sectors which traditionally have higher-earning EP holders.

sections.label: FCF enhancement and ICT exemption
sections.summary: The speaker welcomes FCF extension to S Pass and doubled job advertisement, action against window-dressing firms, and notes ICTs are under 5% of EPs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: Increasingly, all Singaporean PMEs must embrace overseas opportunities as possible opportunities and be open to them regardless of where they are at, in their career life-stage.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: I am glad that MOM has heeded my call to enhance the FCF to include S Pass and doubled the duration of the mandatory job advertisement.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: I am encouraged to also see MOM and TAFEP taking firm action against companies who treat the FCF as mere window dressing.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: On the intra-corporate transfers or ICTs exemption, I take cognisance that ICTs make up less than 5% of EPs in Singapore and that this exemption is necessary in view of our obligations vis-à-vis our Free Trade Agreements’ obligations.

sections.label: Deterring triple weak companies
sections.summary: The speaker suggests publishing MOM and TAFEP's "triple weak" watchlist so reputational loss deters firms with disproportionate foreign PMEs and weak Singaporean Core commitment.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: I am not sure if this moral suasion approach has paid off, but it is certainly the right way to go for companies who fall within the size of company and salary point exemptions to the FCF.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: We can further safeguard the Singaporean Core through stricter enforcement against companies that treat the Fair Consideration Framework as mere window dressing or who continue to be "triple weak" – in other words, companies with highly disproportionate number of foreign PMEs, weak commitment to nurture and strengthen Singaporean Core, and weak relevance to Singapore’s economy and society.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: Besides administrative and penal sanctions that are already in place and can be enhanced, enforcement can come in the form of revealing or publishing the "triple weak" watchlist which MOM and TAFEP maintains, so that the potential reputational loss would serve as a deterrence.

sections.label: Considering fair employment legislation
sections.summary: The speaker notes fair employment legislation has not stopped London and New York being vibrant financial centres, and suggests exploring a Fair Employment or Anti-discrimination law in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: Similarly, Fair employment legislation has not stopped the likes of London and New York from being vibrant financial centres.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: I submit that we should explore and consider the utility and feasibility of a Fair Employment or Anti-discrimination legislation in Singapore.

sections.label: Two-tier PME quota
sections.summary: The quota could have two tiers: higher skilled PMEs with significantly higher salaries and mid-skilled PMEs at the sector median salary range.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: The quota could have two tiers: the first tier consisting of "higher skilled PMEs" with significantly higher salaries and the second tier consisting of "mid-skilled PMEs" who are at the median salary range of the sector or industry.

sections.label: NTUC PME Task Force
sections.summary: NTUC announced a PME Task Force with the Singapore National Employers' Federation to explore better protecting and enabling PMEs, especially those in their 40s to 60s.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: NTUC has also just announced the formation of a PME Task Force in partnership with the Singapore National Employers' Federation and will look into inducting major employer groups and the extended labour movement family, to explore how we can better protect and enable our PMEs, especially those in their 40s, 50s to 60s.

sections.label: ITM 2.0 suggestion
sections.summary: The speaker suggests embarking on an ITM 2.0 to refresh strategies so workers and companies can transform in tandem amid rapid disruption.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: With rapid disruption, accelerated by the COVID-19 pandemic and the next normal, I suggest we embark on an ITM 2.0; to refresh and relook these strategies so that both workers and companies can transform in tandem to meet the challenges ahead.

sections.label: Foreign labour and FCF watchlist
sections.summary: Importing foreign labour is necessary for true labour resource gaps, but some 1,200 firms remain on MOM's Fair Consideration Framework watchlist.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: We agree that as an open trade economy with low birth rates, importing foreign labour is necessary to address true labour resource gaps.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: However, as we have seen, there are still some 1,200 firms on MOM's Fair Consideration Framework (FCF) watchlist.

sections.label: Safeguards for Singaporean PMETs
sections.summary: Proper safeguards for Singaporean PMETs must be put in place to strengthen the Singaporean Core and enhance collaboration among tripartite partners, institutions, society and individuals.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: Proper safeguards for our Singaporean PMETs must be put in place to allow our tribe, the Singaporean Core, to flourish and uplift future generations of Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: With our community as the bedrock, strengthening our Singaporean Core, and enhancing collaboration between tripartite partners, academic institutions, society and individuals – each coming together to contribute their unique role to Singapore's success, so that together, we can become more than the sum of our individual parts.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: COVID19 has brought about a great reset and the next normal will forever transform our lives in more ways than one.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: From the health of our people, to the health of work and the economy, in the pursuit of fairness, justice and equality, we will ensure that no man is left behind, so that we can come out of the storm together, stronger than ever.

sections.label: Protecting livelihoods and businesses
sections.summary: To protect livelihoods, efforts are made to keep workers in jobs, preserve core capabilities and businesses, and support households, with around $100 billion committed.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: To protect livelihoods, we are doing all that we can to keep our workers in jobs, preserve the core capabilities and our businesses, and support households during this difficult period.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: We committed around $100 billion to fight at the pandemic and safeguard our people and businesses from the fallout.

sections.label: Global economy and unemployment
sections.summary: The global economy is projected to contract around 5%, and resident unemployment rose to 3.9% in the second quarter, with more job losses expected.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: The global economy is projected to contract by around 5% and will remain weak and fragile for years to come.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: Our resident unemployment rate has climbed to 3.9% in the second quarter of this year and we can expect more job losses.

sections.label: Industry Transformation Maps refresh
sections.summary: The latest refresh began in 2016 with Industry Transformation Maps for sector-specific adaptation, and productivity and wages rose before COVID-19.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: Our latest refresh started in 2016 with Industry Transformation Maps to spur sector-specific adaptation throughout our economy.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: Productivity and wages were going up before COVID-19.

sections.label: Lifelong learning and SkillsFuture
sections.summary: A holistic approach spanning birth to lifelong learning is needed, and about half a million took part in SkillsFuture programmes last year.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: We need a holistic approach for this that spans the lifetime of individuals from birth to pre-schools to schools, all the way to lifelong learning as part of SkillsFuture.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: I am glad that our workers are embracing upskilling, with about half a million taking part in SkillsFuture programmes last year.

sections.label: Emerging Stronger Task Force alliances
sections.summary: The Emerging Stronger Task Force, set up four months ago, commissioned seven alliances for action to pilot ideas in specific growth areas.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: Four months ago, we set up the Emerging Stronger Task Force to identify and seize new opportunities in emerging trends.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: The task force has made good progress and commissioned seven alliances for action.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: These industry-led coalitions to pilot ideas quickly represent the new action-oriented approach to pursue specific growth areas.

sections.label: Fair workplace consideration for Singaporeans
sections.summary: Manpower policies, including employment and S Pass policies, are being adapted to changing circumstances to uphold Singaporeans' interests and ensure fair workplace consideration.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: Singaporeans must receive fair consideration at the workplace – a point which Mr Patrick Tay has just emphasised.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: We are, therefore, adapting our manpower policies, including our employment and S Pass policies, to the changing circumstances to ensure the Singaporeans' interests are upheld.

sections.label: Social spending and worker support
sections.summary: Healthcare affordability was improved through MediShield Life and CHAS, lower wage workers' wages were uplifted, and social spending has tripled over 15 years.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: For example, we improved healthcare affordability through MediShield Life and CHAS and provided extra support for the Pioneer in Merdeka Generations.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: We uplifted the wages of our lower wage workers through Workfare and the Progressive Wage Model.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: Our social spending has tripled over the last 15 years and this is set to rise further as our population ages.

sections.label: Social spending, taxes and reserves
sections.summary: Higher social spending requires higher taxes or more debt, but Singapore funded over half of almost $100 billion in support using past reserves without debt.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: If we want higher social spending, taxes will have to go up, or it will mean spending more at the expense of future generations by what many countries are doing – by raising their debt.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: We must never forget that we have provided almost $100 billion of support for our people and businesses this year without incurring a single cent of debt because we are able to fund over half of this using past reserves.

sections.label: Masks Sewn With Love project
sections.summary: The Masks Sewn With Love project sewed more than 100,000 masks for vulnerable families, with some Members of Parliament deeply involved.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: One example is the Masks Sewn With Love project, a community effort that has sewn more than 100,000 masks for vulnerable families, which some of our Members of Parliament were very deeply involved in.

sections.label: Singapore Together Movement launch
sections.summary: The Singapore Together Movement was launched in June last year to harness diversity as a strength and create a shared future.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: Otherwise, change will cause a rupture in society as we have seen elsewhere.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: We launched the Singapore Together Movement in June last year, precisely to harness diversity as a strength and create a shared future for everyone.

sections.label: Emerging Stronger conversations
sections.summary: Emerging Stronger conversations let Singaporeans reflect on COVID-19 experiences and will lead to action through the Singapore Together Action Network and other partnerships.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: We want to build on these efforts too, as we recover from COVID-19.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: So, we have convened the Emerging Stronger conversations, which give Singaporeans a shared opportunity to reflect on the COVID-19 experiences and articulate how we can take Singapore forward together.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: These conversations are on-going and will lead to action through our Singapore Together Action Network and other partnerships.

sections.label: COVID-19 as severe test
sections.summary: The COVID-19 pandemic could be Singapore's most severe test so far.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: The COVID-19 pandemic could be our most severe test so far.

sections.label: Adapting, values, new MPs
sections.summary: Singapore must adapt to changes while staying true to its values, and welcomes 31 newly-elected Members of Parliament to this debate.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: We will have to adapt to these changes, but stay true to our values – the same values that have enabled us to stay united and succeed against the odds.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: We welcome the 31 newly-elected Members of Parliament in this Parliament and look forward to hearing from them in this debate.

sections.label: Goh as Prime Minister
sections.summary: Goh's 1990 to 2004 term as Prime Minister is remembered for stability, peace and growth, and steering through the Asian Financial Crisis and SARS.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: Mr Goh's years as a Prime Minister, from 1990 to 2004, are remembered as a time of stability, peace and growth during which we became a kinder, gentler society and a more confident people.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: He steered us through two major crises – the Asian Financial Crisis and SARS.

sections.label: Goh's counsel on bank guarantee
sections.summary: As Chairman, Goh gave wise counsel and support for seeking the President's approval of a $150 billion guarantee on all bank deposits.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: Emeritus Senior Minister Goh was then our Chairman and banks around the world were in trouble.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: So, when we had to make a momentous decision on whether to seek the approval from the President for $150 billion guarantee on all bank deposits, backed by our past reserves, I was very glad to have his wise counsel and his support for us to take difficult decisions head-on.

sections.label: Pritam Singh new roles
sections.summary: Pritam Singh has taken over as Secretary-General of the Workers' Party and been appointed Leader of the Opposition.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: Mr Pritam Singh has taken over as Secretary-General of the Workers' Party and has been appointed Leader of the Opposition.

sections.label: Serving Singaporeans after election
sections.summary: Elected as representatives, they must resolve to do their best to serve Singaporeans so Singapore emerges stronger from this test.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: Singaporeans have elected us to be their representatives.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: We must put our minds and efforts together, resolve to do our best, to serve Singaporeans in Singapore so that we can emerge stronger from this test of a generation.

sections.label: Leader of the Opposition announcement
sections.summary: After the General Election results, the Prime Minister announced the Leader of the Opposition position with support and resources, surprising the Workers' Party and public.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Immediately after the results of the General Election were known, the Prime Minister announced the position of Leader of the Opposition and that this would come with support and resources.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: It would be an understatement to say that this announcement came as a surprise to the Workers' Party and to members of the public.

sections.label: Institutionalising the Opposition office
sections.summary: The office of the Leader of the Opposition goes a long way to institutionalising an Opposition in Parliament and the political system.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The office of the Leader of the Opposition goes a long way to institutionalising an Opposition in Parliament and in our political system.

sections.label: PRs for 20 or more years
sections.summary: The information provided was narrower, specifically that about 15% of PRs have been PRs for 20 or more years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The information provided was far narrower, specifically that about 15% of PRs have been PRs for 20 or more years.

sections.label: Parliament as safety valve
sections.summary: The speaker argues the Government must find a new way to deal with difficult matters, and believes Parliament is an important safety valve and moderator of extreme conversations on immigration and population issues.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: But it is my case, Mr Speaker, that the Government will have to find a new way of dealing with such difficult matters.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: And I strongly believe Parliament is an important safety valve and a potential moderator of extreme conversations found offline and online on immigration and population issues.

sections.label: Allowances for Legislative and Secretarial Assistants
sections.summary: Every elected Member of Parliament gets a budget to hire a Legislative Assistant and Secretarial Assistant, paid $1,300 and $500 a month respectively.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Every elected Member of Parliament is given a budget to hire a Legislative Assistant and Secretarial Assistant.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The Legislative Assistant is paid an allowance of $1,300 per month and the Secretarial Assistant is paid an allowance of $500 a month.

sections.label: Three more LAs for Opposition Leader
sections.summary: The Government has allocated a budget for three more LAs for the Leader of the Opposition, each paid $1,300 a month.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: For the office of the Leader of the Opposition, the Government has allocated a budget for three more LAs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Applying the standard allowance for LAs, each of the three additional LAs for the Leader of the Opposition will be paid $1,300 a month.

sections.label: Five areas of focus
sections.summary: The five areas are health, ageing and retirement adequacy; jobs, businesses and the economy; education, inequality and the cost of living; housing, transport and infrastructure; and national sustainability.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The five areas are: (a) health, ageing and retirement adequacy; (b) jobs, businesses and the economy; (c) education, inequality and the cost of living; (d) housing, transport and infrastructure; (e) national sustainability – a broad-ranging area that looks at policies and proposals to ensure we leave behind a thriving Singapore that lasts far into the future for successive generations.

sections.label: Workers' Party loyalty position
sections.summary: The Workers' Party has always taken the position that when in the Opposition, it owes its loyalty to the President, the Republic of Singapore and the people.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The Workers' Party has always taken the position that when it is in the Opposition, it owes its loyalty to the President, the Republic of Singapore and the people.

sections.label: Workers' Party defence foreign policy support
sections.summary: The Workers' Party supports the Government's positions on defence and foreign policy.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The Workers' Party supports the Government's positions on defence and foreign policy.

sections.label: Workers' Party backs multilateral initiatives
sections.summary: The Workers' Party backs the Government in involving Singapore in United Nations, WHO, World Bank, UNESCO, ILO and other multilateral initiatives.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The Workers' Party backs the Government in involving Singapore in United Nations initiatives, and those of the World Health Organization, the World Bank, UNESCO, the International Labour Organization and other multilateral initiatives.

sections.label: South China Sea Code of Conduct
sections.summary: The Workers' Party supports Singapore's efforts with ASEAN and other countries to finalise the South China Sea Code of Conduct.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In particular, we support Singapore's efforts to work with ASEAN and other countries to finalise the South China Sea Code of Conduct.

sections.label: Workers' Party proposes more Select Committees
sections.summary: The Workers' Party proposes forming more Select Committees to leverage Parliament as an independent Organ of State.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: First, to leverage an independent Organ of State, namely Parliament, the Workers' Party proposes the formation of more Select Committees.

sections.label: Select Committees on sensitive issues
sections.summary: Regular Select Committees on sensitive and difficult issues let Parliament lead the conversation and champion the truth.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: By forming Select Committees that meet regularly on the most sensitive and difficult issues for Singapore, Parliament can play a bigger role in leading the conversation and championing the truth.

sections.label: Standing Select Committees with Opposition MPs
sections.summary: Prime Minister Goh Chok Tong introduced them for PAP self-checking; with 10 elected Opposition MPs, Standing Select Committees are feasible and desirable for accountability.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Prime Minister Goh Chok Tong introduced them as a method of PAP self-checking.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Now, with the presence of 10 elected Opposition Members of Parliament, Standing Select Committees are feasible and indeed desirable for greater accountability.

sections.label: Select Committee on Online Falsehoods
sections.summary: The speaker was a member of the Select Committee on Deliberate Online Falsehoods in the last term of Parliament, calling it a good start.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The Select Committee on Deliberate Online Falsehoods, of which I was a member in the last term of Parliament, was a good start.

sections.label: Forum letters and MOM watchlist
sections.summary: Letters by a retired banker and the MAS Managing Director appeared after MOM placed 47 companies on the Fair Consideration Framework watchlist.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In recent weeks, letters in The Straits Times Forum have been published, one by a retired senior Singaporean banker and another by the Managing Director of the Monetary Authority of Singapore or MAS, in reply.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: These appeared after MOM placed 47 companies on the Fair Consideration Framework watchlist.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: On the MOM’s website, examples are given of one wealth management firm where almost three-quarters of their PMET or professional, manager, executive and technician jobs are held by persons of the same nationality.

sections.label: Publishing recalcitrant employer names
sections.summary: The speaker says one way for Parliament and the public to know is for MOM to publish the names of recalcitrant employers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: One way for us in Parliament and for the public to know, is for MOM to publish the names of recalcitrant employers.

sections.label: Anti-discrimination legislation and penalties
sections.summary: The speaker proposes Parliament pass anti-discrimination legislation with penalties, noting current TAFEP breaches bring only debarment and no criminal penalties.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Beyond this, a far more purposeful way to prevent companies from hiring unfairly would be for Parliament to pass anti-discrimination legislation and impose penalties for discriminatory practices by egregious offenders.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: At the moment, the penalty for employers who breach TAFEP’s fair hiring requirements is a debarment of up to two years from hiring or renewing foreign workers, including work pass renewals – and that is for the most serious offenders.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: There are no criminal penalties for individuals who are responsible for unfair hiring practices.

sections.label: Standard Chartered local staff figure
sections.summary: Standard Chartered has said that 70% of its local subsidiary's staff are Singapore Citizens.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Standard Chartered has said that 70% of its local subsidiary’s staff are Singapore Citizens.

sections.label: Protecting Singaporean PMETs and tradesmen
sections.summary: The speaker says Singapore must position PMETs competitively against work pass holders, and cites Australia, New Zealand and Germany regulating trades.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: We should aim to welcome those looking to move.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: But if we do not move purposefully to consolidate and position the Singaporean PMET in a competitive position vis-a-vis the work pass holder, the Government will not be able to secure support or adequate support for its economic agenda and take advantage of opportunities while maintaining social harmony.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In places like Australia, New Zealand and Germany, tradesmen make good wages that match or even outstrip those of university graduates.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The way to protect our tradesmen is to regulate who can practice each trade.

sections.label: Pioneer and Merdeka schemes
sections.summary: The Workers' Party believes the Pioneer and Merdeka generation schemes are good ones.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The Workers' Party believes that the Pioneer and Merdeka generation schemes, for example, are good ones.

sections.label: Workers' Party national conversation role
sections.summary: The Workers' Party will seek to play a positive role in the national conversation in and out of Parliament.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The Workers' Party will seek to play a positive role in the national conversation both in and out of Parliament to leave behind a Singapore our children and future generations can be proud of.

sections.label: Jobs Support Scheme support
sections.summary: The Jobs Support Scheme has helped companies manage manpower costs and keep jobs during the COVID pandemic.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: With the sudden and severe impact of the COVID pandemic on businesses, support like the Jobs Support Scheme or JSS, has helped companies manage manpower costs and keep jobs.

sections.label: Tech jobs and skills gap
sections.summary: Tech jobs are in demand but not enough Singaporeans have the requisite skills.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: With the importance of digitalisation, tech and tech-related jobs in data analytics, artificial intelligence, cybersecurity, network and software engineering are up and will be in demand.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: These are quality jobs, but we do not have enough Singaporeans equipped with the requisite skills.

sections.label: Fair Consideration Framework watch list
sections.summary: MOM placed 47 more employers on the Fair Consideration Framework watch list and announced higher qualifying salaries.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: Just earlier this month, it was reported in the Straits Times that MOM has placed another 47 employers (on top of the current 1,200) on the Fair Consideration Framework (FCF) watch list for potentially discriminatory hiring practices.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: MOM has also announced last week that higher qualifying salaries for S Pass and EP will be effective 1 September 2020.

sections.label: MAS financial sector support package
sections.summary: MAS' $125-million package has structured talent development programmes for over 900 Singaporeans in financial institutions.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: At the sector level, a good programme is the launch of MAS’ $125-million support package launched in April this year.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: Apart from all the subsidies for training and for manpower cost which everybody talks about in the FinTech sectors and the financial services, what is important is the package has structured talent development programmes for more than 900 Singaporeans amongst the newly hired in the financial institutions (FIs) over the next three years.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: To prepare local mid-career workers as well for new or transformed roles, MAS is closely working with the Institute of Banking and Finance and Workforce Singapore to train and redeploy workers.

sections.label: Foreigners complement Singapore workforce
sections.summary: The passage states foreigners are required to complement the Singapore workforce and that Singapore must not become difficult for companies to operate in.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: While we must continue to grow the Singapore Core, I must say that we must not lock ourselves out as foreigners are required to complement the Singapore workforce.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: Singapore cannot become a place that is difficult for companies both Singaporean and foreign to operate as Singapore is a small market and dependent on external demand as well as resources to grow and to scale.

sections.label: Assess home ownership for schemes
sections.summary: The suggestion is that support schemes assess home ownership rather than mere residence.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: In light of the above, my suggestion is that support schemes assess home ownership rather than mere residence.

sections.label: Broadening support for Singaporeans
sections.summary: Suggestions include using personal income as an alternative basis of assessment and removing ABSD for Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: To address this, Mr Speaker, Sir, my suggestion is to take personal income as an alternative basis of assessment whenever the income household per capita disqualifies an adult Singaporean from financial support.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: My third suggestion on broadening support for Singaporeans is to consider removing the Additional Buyer’s Stamp Duty (ABSD) for Singaporeans.

sections.label: Dormitory and accommodation breaches
sections.summary: About 20 purpose-built dormitories breach licence conditions yearly, and an average of 1,200 employers are taken to task for unacceptable accommodation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: About 20 purpose-built dormitories for foreign workers breach dormitory licence conditions each year, almost half of the 43 dormitories regulated under the Foreign Employee Dormitories Act Each year, there is an average of 1,200 employers taken to task for unacceptable accommodation under the Employment of Foreign Manpower Act.

sections.label: Penalties disgorging profits
sections.summary: The suggestion is to introduce penalties that disgorge a percentage of profits to deter repeat offenders and harm from contraventions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: My suggestion is to introduce penalties that disgorge a certain percentage of profits to deter repeat offenders and the kind of harm caused by contraventions.

sections.label: Overseas study and Singapore universities
sections.summary: Singaporean students returning from overseas due to COVID-19 want overseas years to count towards a Singapore degree, and online tutorials could let students not in Singapore participate.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Many Singaporean students have had to return from universities overseas due to COVID-19 and want to make their first few years done overseas count towards a degree in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Singapore can use this opportunity to attract an even larger talent pool through Singapore Universities, both with Singaporean students and international students.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Through online tutorials, students not in Singapore can participate in courses that count towards a Singapore university degree.

sections.label: IP dispute resolution act
sections.summary: The Intellectual Property (Dispute Resolution) Act passed in 2019 will streamline IP dispute resolution in the Court system and clarified arbitrability of IP rights in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: For dispute resolution, the Intellectual Property (Dispute Resolution) Act passed in 2019 will streamline IP dispute resolution in the Court system and has clarified the arbitrability of IP rights in Singapore.

sections.label: Daren Tang WIPO candidature
sections.summary: IPOS' strong reputation likely had a positive impact on Mr Daren Tang's candidature as Director-General of WIPO, which he will commence on 1 October.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Indeed, IPOS’ strong reputation likely had a positive impact on Mr Daren Tang’s candidature as Director-General of the World Intellectual Property Organisation (WIPO), which he will commence on 1 October.

sections.label: Pandemic economic impact
sections.summary: The pandemic has significantly impacted the economy, with the worst recession in 55 years, a 13.2% second-quarter shrinkage, doubled retrenchments and 3.9% resident unemployment.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: The pandemic has a significant impact on our economy.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: We are facing our worst recession in 55 years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Our economy has shrunk 13.2% in the second quarter, retrenchments have doubled and resident unemployment rate has risen to 3.9%.

sections.label: SGUnited employment diversion
sections.summary: Through SGUnited, the Government seeks to help divert those seeking employment to industries in high demand.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Through SGUnited, the Government seeks to help divert those who are seeking employment to the industries that are in high demand.

sections.label: Japan funding production shift
sections.summary: The Japanese government has set aside S$2.2 billion to encourage companies to shift production out of China, amid a "China plus one" strategy.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: The Japanese government, for example, has set aside S$2.2 billion of funding to encourage companies to shift their production out of China.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: With the need to diversify, and rising tensions between US and China, firms are shifting to a "China plus one" strategy of spreading production between China and a Southeast Asian country.

sections.label: Singaporean Core motion
sections.summary: The speaker had raised a Motion on building the Singaporean Core and tightening job hiring practices, and urges MOM to expand the Capability Transfer Programme.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Back in November last year, I had also raised a Motion on the importance of building our Singaporean Core and tightening our job hiring and employment practices for older workers and minorities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: I urge MOM to consider my suggestion to expand the Capability Transfer Programme (CTP) to support companies to set localisation targets.

sections.label: Rising inflation risk projection
sections.summary: Prof Russell Napier projects inflation of 4% to 8% over the next 10 years, though there is little concern about inflation risk.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Adding on to these challenges is the possibility of rising inflation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: It is true that there is little concern about the risk of inflation, but market strategist and financial historian Prof Russell Napier projects that inflation in the next 10 years will be between 4% and 8%.

sections.label: Businesses ceasing operations in April
sections.summary: More than 8,600 businesses ceased and filed to cease operations in April, which the speaker worries forewarns a harsh, prolonged pandemic.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: More than 8,600 businesses have already ceased and filed to cease operations in April and I am worried that this is only a forewarning of an unforgivably harsh and prolonged pandemic.

sections.label: St Louis Fed capital study
sections.summary: A Federal Reserve Bank of St Louis study showed policies preventing capital depreciation or obsolescence can have substantial long-term effects despite modest immediate output effects.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: A study by the Federal Reserve Bank of St Louis recently showed that policies that help prevent capital depreciation or obsolescence, even if it has only modest immediate effects on output, can have substantial long-term effects.

sections.label: Bankruptcies eroding capital value
sections.summary: Widespread bankruptcies can destroy specific investments and permanently erode the value of certain types of capital.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: For example, widespread bankruptcies can lead to destruction of specific investments and a permanent erosion in the value of certain types of capital.

sections.label: Pandemic fear and investment risk
sections.summary: The passage asks whether firms will take risks if they fear another pandemic may wipe out their work and livelihoods, and how to prevent declining investments and jobs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Would firms and businesses be willing to take risks, if they fear that another pandemic may wipe out their hard work and even livelihoods?

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: How can we ensure that this fear does not lead to further decline in investments and, therefore, jobs in the long term?

sections.label: Post-pandemic business decisions and inflation
sections.summary: Policy planners must address how pandemic risk affects business decisions and investment appetite, while the Government cushions future inflation and sectoral issues despite almost $100 billion injected.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: It is not uncommon to hear or people talking about nothing is too big to collapse after the debacle.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: So, policy planners would need to address how businesses will be making decisions with the added element of what is the risk to them, should there be another pandemic, not necessarily the COVID-19 pandemic, and how this will impact the appetite for investments for venturing into new businesses for expansion and how to grab opportunities now if possible.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: While other modern economies are battered by high infections and death rates, we have been able to keep these numbers low in the community here in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: In the meantime, the Government must look beyond labour issues and take steps to cushion the potential impact of future inflation and sectoral issues, as we pick ourselves up in a post-pandemic world.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: Despite the injection of almost $100 billion into the economy, the pain and frustrations that our people and businesses are experiencing continue.

sections.label: New Employment Pass hiring measures
sections.summary: The Government announced new measures to raise the bar on hiring Employment Pass holders.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: The Government has announced a set of new measures to raise the bar on the hiring of Employment Pass holders.

sections.label: Singaporeans over equally qualified foreigners
sections.summary: Employers should be obliged to pick the Singaporean over the foreigner between two equally qualified candidates.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: In other words, between two equally qualified candidates, employers should be obliged – obliged – to pick the Singaporean over the foreigner.

sections.label: Dependency ratio for Employment Passes
sections.summary: Implement a dependency ratio or quota for Employment Passes, with differentiated ceilings and salary levels for different sectors.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: Two, implement dependency ratio or quota for Employment Passes, with differentiated ceilings and salary levels for different sectors.

sections.label: Senior management accountability for employment offers
sections.summary: Hold senior management accountable by requiring the most senior executive to sign off on employment offers to EP holders, including a compliance declaration.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: Four, hold senior management accountable – require the most senior executive to sign off on employment offers to EP holders, including a declaration that the firm has complied with the above-mentioned requirements.

sections.label: Equal Employment Opportunities framework
sections.summary: The speaker calls on the Government to consider an Equal Employment Opportunities framework to stem discrimination in employment practices.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: We have also often heard of discriminatory practices against mothers and minorities.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: I call on the Government to consider implementing an Equal Employment Opportunities framework to stem discrimination in employment practices.

sections.label: Sustainability of extending JSS
sections.summary: The speaker supports preserving core capabilities in key sectors but questions extending JSS indefinitely, urging more differentiated support for companies.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: Whilst I support the need to preserve our core capabilities in key sectors such as aviation, I question the sustainability of extending JSS indefinitely.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: It is about time that the Government transition to a much more differentiated level of support for companies.

sections.label: COVID-19 support and safety net
sections.summary: The COVID-19 Support Grant and SIRS are steps toward providing a universal safety net for basic income, medical coverage and retirement adequacy.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: The introduction of COVID-19 Support Grant to help the unemployed and SIRS to help the self-employed are steps in the right direction.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: At this time of great uncertainty and disruption, we owe it to our people to provide some universal safety net in the form of support for basic income, medical coverage and retirement adequacy, so that families can cope.

sections.label: High standards but challenges
sections.summary: Healthcare, housing, transport, education and security are of high standard, but Singaporeans face higher costs, stress, competition and income inequality.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: If you look at healthcare, housing, public transport, education opportunities, security and public order, they are all of a very high standard.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: But Singaporeans face challenges of higher cost of living, more stress, stiff competition and income inequality.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: We also live in a more inter-connected and complicating world order where governments in other countries have become protectionists and more inward looking.

sections.label: Policies involve trade-offs
sections.summary: Almost all policies are about trade-offs, including wanting a Singaporean Core employed first and in the best jobs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: I have come to acknowledge that almost all policies are about trade-offs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: We all want a Singaporean Core; we want Singaporeans to be employed first and to get the best jobs.

sections.label: Skilled foreign workers and Singaporeans
sections.summary: The solution is not to close the door to skilled foreign workers but to have policies that do not discriminate against Singaporeans and help them get better jobs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: Why not invest in another country where manpower cost is lower and there are less restrictions?

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: Thus, the solution is not to close the door to skilled foreign workers but to ensure that we have policies which do not discriminate against Singaporeans, that we have policies which will help Singaporeans to get better jobs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: So, I urge the Government to continue ensuring that Singaporeans remain at the centre of all that we do, and for the Government to do a better job of explaining in very simple terms the trade-offs faced by us as a small nation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: This is a pandemic that has caused the worst recession in Singapore since Independence.

sections.label: Help regardless of house type
sections.summary: Those who need help but live in homes above a certain annual value should not be deemed self-sufficient, as any Singaporean suffering income loss needs help.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: I agree that those who are low-income and need more help should get more help.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: But for those who need help but live in homes above a certain annual value, why should they be deemed to be self-sufficient?

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: When a Singaporean suffers loss of income, then regardless of his house type, he needs help.

sections.label: Residents of higher-value homes
sections.summary: Some residents of homes with higher annual value are tenants, some are children of owners, and some inherited the homes from their parents.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: Some of these residents are mere tenants of the homes with higher annual value; some are children of actual owners of the property; and some have inherited the homes from their parents.

sections.label: Property values and COVID-19 assistance
sections.summary: The speaker asks whether people must sell their homes before receiving COVID-19 short-term help and urges a review of pegging assistance to property annual values.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: Should we always insist that these people must sell their homes before they get the short-term help specifically targeted at those affected by COVID-19?

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: So, I urge the Government to review this policy of pegging our assistance to annual values of properties.

sections.label: Reasons for supporting enterprises
sections.summary: The passage states that even well managed companies are affected by external factors and that the electorate desires a more inclusive society on race, community and employment.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: First, even well managed companies have been adversely affected due to external factors.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Second, the desire of our electorate for a more inclusive society on matters pertaining to race, community and employment.

sections.label: Iterative view of enterprises
sections.summary: The passage argues that enterprise success should be assessed iteratively over time, reframing the belief of letting failing companies die to enabling them to rebound and restart.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: We must not assess the success of an enterprise at a single point in time but instead adopt an iterative perspective where all enterprises evolve over time and therefore will have many highs and lows as part of its development.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: This means that we need to reframe our belief of letting failing companies die to enabling failing companies to rebound and restart.

sections.label: Partnering every entrepreneur
sections.summary: The passage states that while not every business can be saved, every entrepreneur should be partnered to evolve, given a soft landing, a longer runway and help to re-start.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: While we cannot save every business, we should partner every entrepreneur to evolve, help them with a soft landing, provide them a longer runway and help them re-start.

sections.label: Five policy moves
sections.summary: The passage states that the speaker calls upon five policy moves.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: As such, I call upon the following five policy moves.

sections.label: EP and S Pass salary impact
sections.summary: The passage states that MOM's recent announcement of raising EP and S Pass minimum salary impacts industries unevenly.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: MOM's recent announcement of raising EP and S Pass minimum salary impacts industries unevenly.

sections.label: SMEs and Singaporean jobs
sections.summary: SMEs employ close to 70% of the workforce, so preserving them helps preserve Singaporeans' jobs and livelihood.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: In this way, we continue to help our Singaporeans by preserving their jobs and their livelihood as SMEs employ close to 70% of our workforce.

sections.label: Debt repayment and director liability
sections.summary: It proposes extending a repayment scheme to more debt categories with instalment plans and capped interest, and clarifying directors' liability for insolvency trading from 1 February 2020.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: As such, I would like to propose that: (a) a repayment scheme be extended for more categories of debts.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: The new categories can include other obligations, such as liabilities under personal guarantees or insurance bonds, trade financing and term loans.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: There should be an instalment plan outlining a clear debts repayment schedule with capped interest rates; and (b) we should make it clear that Directors should not be liable for insolvency trading if the insolvency period arises from 1 February 2020.

sections.label: Environment for SMEs and entrepreneurs
sections.summary: Beyond support measures, the Government needs to foster the best environment for SMEs and entrepreneurs, and MTI has convened a Fair Tenancy ProTem committee.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: And, last but not the least, beyond support measures, the Government needs to also foster the best environment for our SMEs and entrepreneurs to succeed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: I am heartened that MTI has convened a Fair Tenancy ProTem committee.

sections.label: Five policy advancements for enterprises
sections.summary: Five policy advancements can leverage enterprises' and entrepreneurs' capacities to create jobs, secure livelihoods, and evolve Singapore Inc.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Through the above five policy advancements, we can leverage our inherent capacities of our enterprises and entrepreneurs who continue contributing to the overall Singapore economic and social footprint, creating good jobs for Singaporeans and thereby securing their livelihoods.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: We must provide more hope and heart for greater value to emerge.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Let us walk this journey of "revive", "rejuvenate" and "restart" and with our entrepreneurs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Let us partner them as societal agents of change, facing each challenge with the conviction of carving out opportunities for sustainable good.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: I believe together we can evolve Singapore Inc which will ultimately not just provide good jobs but great livelihoods for the families of Singapore.

sections.label: Screening migrant workers in dormitories
sections.summary: The Joint Task Force completed screening migrant workers in all dormitories, most cleared to work, and passed the baton to the MOM ACE Group.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Manpower and Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: After close to five months of intensive effort, the Joint Task Force has completed the mammoth task of screening migrant workers in all dormitories, and the vast majority of them have been cleared to go back to work.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Manpower and Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: The Joint Task Force has passed the baton to the newly-formed MOM Assurance, Care and Engagement Group, or ACE Group for short.

sections.label: Healthcare for migrant workers
sections.summary: To reduce outbreak resurgence risks in dormitories, migrant workers get healthcare through 12 medical centres, telemedicine, and mobile clinical teams.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Manpower and Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: We will make sure that we reduce the risks of a resurgence of the outbreak in the dormitories.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Manpower and Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: We will provide comprehensive and accessible healthcare services to migrant workers through three main channels: first, they can visit one of our 12 medical centres providing primary care services island-wide; second, they can also seek medical attention via telemedicine anytime on their smartphones, through a mobile application; and third, mobile clinical teams will be activated in the event of an emerging cluster, so that we can mitigate any outbreaks.

sections.label: Quick Build Dormitory beds
sections.summary: 25,000 beds in Quick Build Dormitories will be available by early next year, with another 100,000 beds in the next few years.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Manpower and Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: In addition, we will make available 25,000 beds in Quick Build Dormitories by early next year, with another 100,000 beds coming onboard within the next few years.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Manpower and Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: These are temporary structures, the 25,000 beds in the Quick Build Dormitories.

sections.label: Fairness at Work and jobs
sections.summary: The National Jobs Council, led by Senior Minister Tharman, will bring together 100,000 opportunities through the SGUnited Jobs and Skills Package.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Manpower and Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: We will make every effort to come together and ensure that we do not have a “lost generation” of workers.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Manpower and Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: We will support our workforce by securing “Fairness at Work” – upholding fair opportunities, fair hiring, fair competition and fair support for everyone to progress at every stage of their working lives.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Manpower and Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: We promise to walk with every worker, even if we cannot preserve every job.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Manpower and Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: Our national effort to do so will be through the National Jobs Council, led by Senior Minister Tharman.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Manpower and Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: We will ensure that our jobseekers have fair opportunities and equitable ones at a good job by bringing together 100,000 such opportunities through the SGUnited Jobs and Skills Package.

sections.label: SGUnited Traineeships for young workers
sections.summary: The SGUnited Traineeships Programme will help young workers build professional skillsets, experience and networks.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Manpower and Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: Even though some of our young workers may find it challenging to secure a job opportunity during this period, we are committed to helping them to build their professional skillsets, experience and networks, through the SGUnited Traineeships Programme.

sections.label: Lucence blood test and expansion
sections.summary: Lucence developed a blood test detecting cancer-causing genes and viruses, used for thousands of patients, and plans to hire more in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Manpower and Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: Lucence has also developed the world’s first blood test that detects both cancer-causing genes and viruses in order to identify the best treatment for cancer patients, and it has been used for thousands of patients across the US and Asia.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Manpower and Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: On top of that, the company has also established laboratories in Silicon Valley and Suzhou Industrial Park and continues to expand their operations amidst the global pandemic, and they have plans to hire more research and medtech professionals in Singapore.

sections.label: Mid-career opportunities under SGUnited
sections.summary: Opportunities under the SGUnited Jobs and Skills Package let middle-aged mature workers upskill and reskill for quality job roles.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Manpower and Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: These permanent job opportunities will change in scope, they may remain scarce until the economy picks up again.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Manpower and Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: We have thus designed opportunities for mid-career individuals under the SGUnited Jobs and Skills Package, to allow our middle-aged mature workers to seize this opportunity to upskill and reskill for quality job roles and good future careers.

sections.label: Companies hired 2,800 local PMETs
sections.summary: Companies hired 2,800 local PMETs, more than the 2,000 E Passes they had given out.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Manpower and Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: What is important was that if you read from the same media release, the companies actually hired 2,800 local PMETs, more than the 2,000 E Passes than they had given out.

sections.label: No wanton discrimination local talent
sections.summary: The speaker states companies will not be allowed to practise wanton discrimination against local talent.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Manpower and Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: Regardless, we will not allow companies to practise wanton discrimination against our local talent.

sections.label: MOM boost Singaporean jobseekers
sections.summary: MOM will work with businesses to give Singaporean jobseekers a stronger boost in hiring consideration.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Manpower and Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: At MOM, we will give Singaporean jobseekers a stronger boost by working with businesses to give more serious consideration to Singaporeans when hiring, especially those who are willing to adjust their expectations and adapt.

sections.label: Helping businesses with new opportunities
sections.summary: Businesses seeing new opportunities in listed sectors will be helped to grow.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Manpower and Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: First, for businesses that are seeing new opportunities, such as those in the ICT, biopharma, agritech, advanced manufacturing sectors and those developing low carbon technologies, we will help them grow.

sections.label: Safe Business Event Risk Framework
sections.summary: STB developed a Safe Business Event Risk Management Framework, and the first event was held from 24 to 26 August 2020.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Manpower and Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: For example, to prepare for the safe resumption of meetings, conferences and other business-oriented events, STB has developed a Safe Business Event Risk Management Framework in consultation with the industry and in alignment with international best practices.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Manpower and Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: The first event, the IEEE International Conference on Computational Electromagnetics, was held successfully just a week ago, from 24 to 26 August 2020.

sections.label: Industry-led Alliances growth areas
sections.summary: The Alliances are industry-led coalitions that will prototype and execute ideas in key growth areas such as robotics and supply chain digitalisation.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Manpower and Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: The Alliances are industry-led coalitions that will rapidly prototype and execute ideas in key growth areas for Singapore, such as robotics and supply chain digitalisation.

sections.label: Agencies inroads COVID-19 test kits
sections.summary: Agencies in biomedical and ICT sectors are making inroads in novel COVID-19 test kits, using automation and robotics.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Manpower and Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: Already, many of our agencies in the biomedical ICT sectors are making significant inroads in the development of novel test kits for COVID-19.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Manpower and Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: Several of these areas include the use of automation and robotics to improve turn-around times in the processing of these tests, whilst improving the safety and protection of our lab technicians and bolstering the contact tracing applications.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Manpower and Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: Given the huge amount of creative and intellectual capital in our country, we have the means and the resources to transform many of our industries and services and to come out ahead.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Manpower and Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: In Singapore, we not only dream big, we also make it happen and we bring our dreams to reality – think about Jurong Island, think about Changi Airport – because we work hard together, because we have a collective desire to build a better and brighter future for Singapore together, not just for ourselves, but for our children, our grandchildren and hopefully, our great grandchildren.

sections.label: Transforming a small country
sections.summary: The speaker says this is the only way a country of less than 4 million citizens can transform, leapfrog, thrive and prosper.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Manpower and Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: Because this is the only way I know that our country, of less than 4 million fellow citizens, can transform, leapfrog, thrive and prosper in this brave new world.

sections.label: Firm barred from hiring foreigners
sections.summary: The firm was barred in mid-2017 from hiring foreign staff until it improved its practices, the standard outcome for unfair hiring employers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
sentences.text: The firm was barred in mid-2017 from hiring foreign staff until it improved its practices – which is the standard form of what happens to employers of who practise unfair hiring.

sections.label: Surveillance under Fair Consideration Framework
sections.summary: Surveillance of the Fair Consideration Framework has increased, with monitoring of companies having over-concentration problems.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: What we have started is an increase in terms of the surveillance with regard to the Fair Consideration Framework.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: Where we have started is, first and foremost, the Fair Consideration Framework or FCF where we are monitoring all these companies that have problems in terms of over-concentration.

sections.label: TAFEP resources and ACE Group
sections.summary: Resources will be beefed up, and amid COVID-19 resources were stepped up by taking over from the JTF and morphing it into the ACE Group.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
sentences.text: How will TAFEP be able to have an effective handle over some of the discriminatory or unfair hiring practices and improve the situation from yesteryear?

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: We certainly will look at beefing up the resources.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: At this particular point in time, given where we are in terms of dealing with the COVID-19 crisis, we have also stepped up resources in terms of taking over from the JTF, morphing it into the ACE Group, as I have alluded to earlier on.

sections.label: Complaint on election poster height
sections.summary: Part of the first complaint included 13 allegations that the speaker's election posters were below the requisite height of 2.2 m.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: Part of the first complaint included 13 allegations of my election posters being below the requisite height of 2.2 m.

sections.label: Second complaint and poster removal
sections.summary: A second complaint repeated 12 of the 13 allegations, and a resident said she saw the PAP team pulling down posters from the original height.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: Two days later, a second complaint was made which comprised, among other things, a repeat of 12 of the 13 allegations made earlier.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: During the election, one resident told me that she had witnessed the PAP team pulling down our posters from the original height.

sections.label: Failed criteria
sections.summary: Some people did not succeed because they fall foul of the criteria.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: Not all have succeeded as they fall foul of the criteria.

sections.label: Extending schemes to more people
sections.summary: It asks whether present schemes can be extended to help more people if difficult times persist.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: Can the present schemes be extended to help more such people, especially if these difficult times are here to stay for some time?

sections.label: Residents and relief measures
sections.summary: Many residents sought help under relief measures, but some fell through the cracks by not meeting criteria.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: Many residents have sought help under the relief measures, such as the COVID-19 Support Grant and Self-employed Income Relief Scheme (SIRS), which were rolled out under the four Budgets.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: However, some have fallen through the cracks as they do not meet the criteria for receiving the assistance.

sections.label: Extending schemes and Employment Pass policy
sections.summary: It asks if existing schemes can be extended and whether revised salary requirements address concerns of Singaporean workers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: We know that the difficult times may persist for some period to come.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: Therefore, is there a possibility to extend the existing schemes and measures to assist more Singaporeans?

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: As the competition for scarce jobs heats up, re-looking at our Employment Pass policy is necessary.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: I therefore welcome the announcement revising the minimum salary requirements for Employment Passes and S Passes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: However, are the new revised salary requirements sufficient to address the concerns of Singaporean PMETs and other workers losing their places to EP and SP holders?

sections.label: Public transport subsidies and sustainability
sections.summary: It questions how Singapore can achieve car-lite goals and public transport sustainability without subsidies, seeking figures for debate.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: While I see the need to ensure a degree of sustainability of our public transport, without those subsidies to build the connectivity require for a car-lite society, how can Singapore achieve the goals to reduce the reliance on cars and properly connect Singaporeans to the places they want to go in a reasonable and efficient manner?

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: We should also not forget that Singaporeans have underwritten through their tax dollars over the years, the necessary improvements in expansion to our public transportation system.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: Singapore should rightly expected that the public transportation system must serve the public good without the need for excessive profit-seeking behaviour after the improvements that Singaporeans had paid for and maintain that high level of performance.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: Can there be more buses servicing areas in (need?) that are not yet connected by our MRT?

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: Is the bus contracting model able to cater for sufficiently flexible deployment of bus services in growing estates as they look to be less short-term pains for public transport?

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: Maintaining the sustainability of our public transport system must not be viewed in isolation, line by line, but as a holistic policy objectives to ensure the society at large is well served.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
