sentences.text: And if the Government's position is that taxpayers and commuters must contribute more to achieve this, it should provide detailed figures and arguments for better public debate and understanding so that the public can decide where they wish to draw the line.

sections.label: Poster height complaint
sections.summary: ELD informed of a complaint about poster height and asked for it to be rectified.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
sentences.text: Yes, in terms of the poster height, ELD informed us of a complaint being made and asked us to rectify.

sections.label: Hougang complaints and PAP flags
sections.summary: Volunteers inspected complaints, found 12 of 13 similar to previous ones, and the PAP team at Hougang planted flags around coffeeshops.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
sentences.text: Our volunteers went to inspect the complaints directly and made the necessary rectification.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
sentences.text: And that was when they discovered that actually 12 of the 13 complaints made were actually similar to the previous ones.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
sentences.text: I also mentioned about the flags, planting of the flags.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
sentences.text: So, my point at the end of that section of my speech is really this – that the PAP team at Hougang has planted flags all over, around coffeeshops, a lot of flags around the coffeeshops.

sections.label: ELD complaint handling even-handed
sections.summary: ELD was even-handed in handling the complaints.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
sentences.text: Yes, to answer the question, yes, ELD was even-handed in handling the complaints.

sections.label: ELD even-handedness and incumbency
sections.summary: A view that ELD was not even-handed in GE2020 is raised, and the basis for suggesting PAP would unfairly use incumbency is questioned.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
sentences.text: It is my hon friend's view that ELD has not been even-handed in its dealings during GE2020; and what is the basis of suggesting that the PAP would use the power of incumbency against opponents in an unfair way?

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
sentences.text: I am not suggesting the PAP is using the power of incumbency to do those things.

sections.label: Social compact, EP policy, climate
sections.summary: Three items are listed: rethinking the social compact with private estate residents, strengthening the Singaporean Core via EP policy, and co-creating climate change policies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
sentences.text: One, rethinking our social compact with our private estate residents; two, strengthen our Singaporean Core in the private sector through fine-tuning our Employment Pass (EP) policy; and three, co-creating our Climate Change policies with Singaporeans.

sections.label: Reverse mortgage options for seniors
sections.summary: Not all seniors, especially Pioneer Generation, are financially savvy, so the Government must work with banking and insurance sectors on reverse mortgage options for private estates.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
sentences.text: But not all seniors, especially our Pioneer Generation seniors, are financially savvy to navigate the tricky global economic waters.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
sentences.text: Therefore, I believe the Government must actively work with the banking and insurance sectors to create reverse mortgage options for the private estates.

sections.label: Means testing alternatives to annual value
sections.summary: Instead of annual value of houses, means testing can use non-housing assets, income, and per capital housing equity of occupants.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
sentences.text: Instead of using annual value of houses as a key determinant of means testing, we can look at a combination of non-housing assets, income, and most importantly, per capital housing equity of the occupants.

sections.label: Private estate liveability and Singapore Core
sections.summary: Calls for MND-MOT task force on senior liveability in private estates, more shelters, bigger MSO budget, and notes Government moves on Singapore Core.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
sentences.text: As such, I hope that MND and MOT can work together to form a task force to come up with a masterplan for liveability and accessibility for the seniors and frail living within the private estates.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
sentences.text: We can also consider building more rain shelters and sheltered linkways to serve private estate residents in some selected areas.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
sentences.text: We can also beef up the budget allocated to MSO for private estate upgrading projects, so that decent-sized projects can be implemented outside the EUP when the situation calls for it.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
sentences.text: The Government has made some excellent moves to preserve and build on the Singapore Core in our private sector.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
sentences.text: This includes JSS, strengthening the Fair Consideration Framework or FCF, creating 100,000 jobs and training opportunities, and the recent increase in EP and S Pass salary thresholds.

sections.label: Declaring EP holders' country of origin
sections.summary: Proposes mandating large companies with over 25% EP holders to declare EP holders' country of origin across four annual remuneration bands.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
sentences.text: One way is to mandate all companies with more than 200 staff and with more than 25% EP holders to declare the country of origin of their EP holders along four annual renumeration bands: one, from $60,000 to $120,000 a year; two, from $120,000 to $250,000; from $250,000 to $500,000; and beyond $500,000.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
sentences.text: After all, if the EP holders are dominated by one particular country, despite our very diverse expatriate workforce, how can Singaporeans be persuaded that there is diversity in these companies’ hiring and renumeration policy, and how can Singaporeans trust that they have a genuine intention to build up a Singapore Core?

sections.label: Opening up climate change policymaking
sections.summary: Proposes Government open up its climate change workings so citizens can co-create policy, starting by levelling up environmental groups and youths.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
sentences.text: If you want to go far, go together.” And the longest term challenge that Singaporeans must face together is climate change.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
sentences.text: Therefore, I propose that our Government open up the hoods of the Government workings on Climate Change to Singaporeans, so that our citizens have the information and incentive to co-create policy, including making difficult policy trade-offs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
sentences.text: As a start, we can level up our environmental groups and our youths with the latest policy research and technology innovation through high-powered forums.

sections.label: Publicising emission tracking and carbon taxation
sections.summary: Suggests publicising, besides a white paper on emission tracking, the mechanism for regulating emissions and how carbon taxation is arrived at.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
sentences.text: The Government can also publicise, apart from a white paper spelling out the details of our emission tracking framework, the mechanism for regulating emissions including administrative measures and on how we arrive at carbon taxation.

sections.label: Cleaner energy and industrial emissions
sections.summary: States Government is shifting energy imports from natural gas to cleaner sources like solar and green hydrogen, and examining carbon sequestration and mineralisation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
sentences.text: Our Government is actively pursuing changing our energy imports for power generation away from natural gas and towards cleaner sources of energy, not just solar energy, but also green hydrogen.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
sentences.text: We are also examining how to reduce and transform industrial emissions through carbon sequestration, and through mineralisation of carbon so as to transform emissions into sand or ammonia.

sections.label: Independent environmental impact assessment body
sections.summary: Proposes an independent environmental impact assessment and audit outfit, possibly with the UN climate secretariat or a think-tank like McKinsey Global Institute.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
sentences.text: In fact, I further believe that Singapore should set up an independent environmental impact assessment and audit outfit, perhaps in collaboration with the UN Secretariat for Climate Change, or with a think-tank with deep expertise such as the McKinsey Global Institute.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
sentences.text: Having an independent body to evaluate the impact will allow us to make the trade-offs so that we can decide how to best meet emission targets while preserving economic opportunities and quality of life.

sections.label: AV trials and driver livelihoods
sections.summary: AV technology is being trialled locally, with large-scale trials soon in Punggol, Tengah and Jurong Innovation District, raising questions about bus drivers and vocational licence holders.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: Locally, AV technology is already being trialled in areas with complex traffic conditions and we will soon see large-scale trials in Punggol, Tengah and the Jurong Innovation District.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: What will happen to the livelihoods of more than 10,000 bus drivers?

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: What about the 100,000 Singaporeans who hold a Taxi or Private Hire Car vocational licence, many of whom rely on driving today as their source of income?

sections.label: DBS AI training partnership
sections.summary: DBS partnered with Amazon Web Services to equip 3,000 employees with basic knowledge in artificial intelligence and machine learning.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: DBS, for example, has partnered with Amazon Web Services to equip 3,000 employees with basic knowledge in artificial intelligence and machine learning.

sections.label: Compulsory Computer Science suggestion
sections.summary: Data literacy and coding are important skills for the young, and Computer Science should be made a compulsory Secondary school subject.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: Data literacy and coding will be important skills that our young will need to be familiar with.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: We should make Computer Science a compulsory subject in Secondary schools.

sections.label: Work stress and mental health support
sections.summary: A NUS study found work-from-home workers had higher stress than frontline workers, prompting calls to expand WICA occupational diseases, expedite the Tripartite Advisory and consider Right to Disconnect legislation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: A recent study by the National University of Singapore found that those who work from home faced higher levels of stress than our frontline workers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: I hope that the Government could expand the list of Occupational Diseases under the Work Injury Compensation Act (WICA), to include mental health illnesses related to work stress.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: I also hope that the Tripartite Advisory on Mental Health can be expedited, so that those who are currently struggling with mental health issues related to work can get the necessary support that they need.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: With more working from home, is it also time that we consider a "Right to Disconnect" legislation, which was pioneered in France, where employees can negotiate with their employers on answering work calls and emails outside of office hours?

sections.label: Freelancers lack WSH benefits
sections.summary: Freelancers do not enjoy the same WSH statutory benefits as employees, such as WICA coverage, medical group insurance and medical leave.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: Freelancers do not enjoy the same WSH statutory benefits as employees, such as coverage under WICA, medical group insurance and medical leave.

sections.label: Blame culture and risk aversion
sections.summary: A rising culture of blame, finger pointing and moral panic has led to increased risk aversion among public servants, forming the basis for two suggestions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: This is the bedrock and the simple philosophy behind two suggestions I would like to make for this new term.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: There is a rising culture of blame, finger pointing and moral panic in our society.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: As a result, there is a corresponding increase in risk aversion among our public servants.

sections.label: Sheltered home eligibility criteria
sections.summary: A subsidised sheltered home requires the senior to live alone without family or care-giver.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: One of the eligibility criteria for a subsidised sheltered home is that the senior is living alone and does not have any family or care-giver.

sections.label: Reduced hours and pay
sections.summary: After discussing with her supervisor and employer, she worked four hours a day and her pay dropped to about $1,200 monthly.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: So, after discussing with her supervisor and employer, they arranged her to work for four hours a day instead of working full-time.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: And so, her pay dropped to about $1,200 per month.

sections.label: Discretion for civil servants
sections.summary: The speaker asks the Civil Service to give civil servants and Statutory Board officers more authority to exercise discretion.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: It is an honourable purpose and I ask for the Civil Service to join us in one very specific way.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: I ask for civil servants and officers in Statutory Boards to be given more authority to exercise discretion.

sections.label: Volunteers assessing hard cases
sections.summary: Politicians must take criticism, but agencies and officers exercising discretion might rely on volunteers and social workers to assess hard cases.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: Politicians signed up for this and we must be tough enough to take whatever criticism whenever we are called to account.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: But for agencies and officers, if they are to exercise greater discretion, it might perhaps be useful to have and rely on groups of volunteers and social workers who visit and assess hard cases, so that those who fall through the cracks will receive the help they need in an expeditious manner.

sections.label: Fewer rules, more discretion
sections.summary: The speaker argues for fewer rules and more discretion and kindness.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: What I am arguing for is the reverse of rules – fewer rules, more discretion and kindness.

sections.label: Bursaries and foundation donations
sections.summary: Orange Aid gives over $1 million in bursary awards, Bright Horizons Fund about $1.75 million, and Fairprice Foundation over $6 million.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: For this year, Orange Aid will be giving out bursary awards amounting to over $1 million.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: Moving to education, our NTUC First Campus’ Bright Horizons Fund, they give out about $1.75 million this year, 50% higher than last year and, in the process, this will help some 4,700 children from the lower income households.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: For NTUC Fairprice Foundation, we will be increasing our donations this year to the tune of over $6 million.

sections.label: Tightening foreign worker controls
sections.summary: The passage states that controls over foreigners working in Singapore have to be tightened and welcomes higher qualifying salaries for EPs and S Passes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Hence, the controls over the number of foreigners working in Singapore have to be tightened.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: I welcome the higher qualifying salaries for EPs and S Passes.

sections.label: Insurance for older workers
sections.summary: The passage states employers struggle to get insurance cover for workers above 60, hopes MOM will find a solution, and requests a $1,000 monthly Wage Income Supplement for lower income workers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: One of the challenges facing employers is their difficulty in getting insurance cover for their older workers, especially those aged above 60 years old.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: With longer lifespans and a non-replacement birth rate, this is a problem and could be one of the factors driving some employers to retrench older workers, even if they are good at their jobs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: I hope that MOM will look into this and work out a feasible and sustainable solution between employers and insurance companies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: I would also like to request that MOM consider the grant of a $1,000 Wage Income Supplement each month for the lower income workers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: A boost in their take-home pay will make a significant impact and improve their families’ lives.

sections.label: Chance at own BTO flat
sections.summary: The passage states that every Singaporean should have a chance to get their own BTO flat if they desire.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Let each and every Singaporean have a chance to get their own BTO flat if they so desire.

sections.label: Thrift and bigger HDB flats
sections.summary: The passage states that thriftiness should be supported and suggests HDB build more bigger flats, which are popular among young families.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: In today's environment with less job security and more market uncertainty, their desire to be more thrifty is commendable and should be supported.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: I would also like to suggest that HDB build more bigger flats, which are increasingly popular among our young families.

sections.label: Free childcare under seven
sections.summary: The passage states the Government should consider free childcare for all children under seven before Primary school to encourage couples to have more children given the declining fertility rate.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: The Government should also consider providing free childcare for all children under age of seven, before they enter Primary school.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Providing free, reliable and good quality childcare services is necessary to encourage couples to have more children, in view of our declining fertility rate.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: We are in the midst of a crisis but life must go on – supporting procreation, making it easier to have and raise children in Singapore.

sections.label: EP and S Pass holder numbers
sections.summary: The passage states that as of December 2019 there were 193,700 Employment Pass holders and 200,000 S Pass holders according to MOM statistics.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast)
sentences.text: When I checked the MOM's statistics, I noted that there were 193,700 Employment Pass or E Pass holders and 200,000 S Pass holders as of December 2019.

sections.label: Unemployment rate and jobs priority
sections.summary: Unemployment hit a record 3.9% in the last quarter, and the President said securing jobs for Singaporeans is the top national priority.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast)
sentences.text: Unemployment rate hits a record high of 3.9% in the last quarter, the highest in 10 years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast)
sentences.text: When Singaporeans lose their jobs and foreigners are still holding on to PMET jobs, many will be unhappy.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast)
sentences.text: Thus, it was timely, important and pertinent that the President spoke about securing jobs for Singaporeans, and this is the top national priority.

sections.label: Australia abolishes 457 visa
sections.summary: Australia abolished a 457 visa in March 2018 to improve social cohesion, a visa used by skilled migrants including executives.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast)
sentences.text: In Australia, the government had tried to improve "social cohesion" by abolishing a 457 visa in March 2018, which was often used by skilled migrants to work in Australia, including middle and top-management level executives like CEOs and CIOs.

sections.label: Visa suspensions in US and Australia
sections.summary: A South China Morning Post headline said Australia's 457 visa ban hurts the economy, and Trump suspended foreign worker visas in June 2020.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast)
sentences.text: On this, a South China Morning Post article stated in its headline, "The Australians first policy that ban 457 visa scheme for skilled migrants will only hurt the economy." Most recently in June 2020, US President Donald Trump suspended foreign worker visas, including the H-1B visa used by the tech industry to hire highly skilled workers.

sections.label: National Human Resource Committee proposal
sections.summary: The suggestion is to set up a National Human Resource Committee working through Industry Transformation Maps developed for 23 industries.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast)
sentences.text: My suggestion is to set up a National Human Resource Committee, working through the Industry Transformation Maps or ITMs which have been developed in great detail for 23 industries.

sections.label: MOM blacklists employers for discrimination
sections.summary: MOM blacklisted 47 employers in early August for possible discriminatory hiring, mostly in financial and professional services.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast)
sentences.text: We do not want a situation where MOM starts to place employers on the watch list for possible discriminatory hiring practices after discovering that they have many Employment Pass and S Pass holders, outnumbering local PMEs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast)
sentences.text: I am referring to the news in early August where 47 employers were blacklisted by MOM and majority were from the financial and professional services sectors.

sections.label: Companies flouting Fair Consideration Framework
sections.summary: More than 1,200 companies flout the Fair Consideration Framework and may have bad discriminatory hiring practices.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast)
sentences.text: Neither can we remain status quo where we allow more than 1,200 companies to flout the Fair Consideration Framework (FCF), because they might have bad discriminatory hiring practices.

sections.label: Immigrants supplement labour force
sections.summary: If the birth rate cannot be raised in the long run, immigrants or foreign workers will still be needed to supplement the labour force.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast)
sentences.text: If we cannot increase the birth rate in the long run, we will still need immigrants or foreign workers to supplement our labour force.

sections.label: Committee guidance on Singaporean Core
sections.summary: The Committee may guide companies, encourage sharing of best practices and give guidelines so foreign companies build a Singaporean Core.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast)
sentences.text: On discovery of such things, the Committee may issue proper guidance to the companies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast)
sentences.text: However, we should not simply copy other countries by legislating how many local employees a company must have.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast)
sentences.text: If a company finds out that the number of its foreign employees are disproportionately higher than the sector average, it will feel some pressure indirectly and might make the adjustment accordingly.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast)
sentences.text: Thirdly, the Committee may also encourage major companies to share best practices to build a Singaporean Core and learn from one another.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast)
sentences.text: Based on these best practices, the Committee can give some guidelines so that foreign companies that have set up operations in Singapore can quickly build up a Singaporean Core.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast)
sentences.text: At the same time, these foreign companies have also benefited from Singapore’s eco-system, Singapore’s strategic locations and Singapore’s business-friendly infrastructure.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast)
sentences.text: Thus, they also have the obligation to grow the Singaporean Core in their workforce and their management team in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast)
sentences.text: The National HR Committee, working closely with the National Jobs Council, can help to accelerate that and I hope MOM can consider the proposal positively.

sections.label: Government loans for SMEs
sections.summary: The Government has provided SMEs with loans including the SME Working Capital Loan, Productivity Solutions Grants, Loan Insurance Scheme, Enterprise Financing Scheme and Enterprise Development Grant.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: This year, the Government has provided a number of useful loans to our SMEs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: These include SME Working Captial Loan, Productivty Solutions Grants, Loan Insurance Scheme, the Enterprise Financing Scheme or the Enterprise Development Grant.

sections.label: 2019 poll on young entrepreneurs
sections.summary: A 2019 poll of 56,000 people aged 15 to 35 in six countries found only 17% wanted to work for themselves.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Yet, a poll in 2019 showed that young people in Singapore are far less keen on being entrepreneurs than their peers across the region.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: The poll questioned 56,000 people aged 15 to 35 from Indonesia, Malaysia, the Philippines, Singapore, Thailand and Vietnam.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: It found that just 17% of those polled said they wanted to work for themselves in the future.

sections.label: SkillsFuture and start-up grant
sections.summary: It asks whether youths under 25 could use SkillsFuture for entrepreneurship, and notes first-time entrepreneurs can get a $50,000 start-up capital grant.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Could we build a pipeline by allowing youths under the age of 25 to use SkillsFuture to learn more about entrepreneurship?

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: I am glad that first-time entrepreneurs will be able to access a higher start-up capital grant of $50,000 to help them launch their business ideas.

sections.label: Citizen unemployment rate 2020
sections.summary: The overall unemployment rate of Singaporean Citizens rose to more than 3% in 2020.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Our overall unemployment rate of the Singaporean Citizens has risen to more than 3% in 2020.

sections.label: Blue-collar and sandwiched households
sections.summary: Bottom blue-collar households struggle with basic needs, while the sandwiched class has fewer discretionary savings and is more vulnerable to unemployment and illness.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: The bottom rung of the blue-collar households has difficulty making basic ends meet, while the sandwiched class have fewer discretionary savings and therefore may be more vulnerable to ad hoc occurrences of unemployment and illnesses.

sections.label: KidSTART, NEHR and SSO data sharing
sections.summary: More budget can scale up KidSTART, and the Government is urged to let NEHR and SSO records be shared with SSOs and schools.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: More budget can be set aside to scale up the KidSTART programme.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Despite the KidSTART programme's success, it remains very costly to sustain.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: I also urge the Government to allow medical records stored in the National Electronic Health Record (NEHR) be shared with the Social Service Offices (SSOs) in a secured manner after been authorised by the client so that the deserving cases can be helped expediently.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: In the same vein, SSOs' records should also be shared with schools so that the Financial Assistance Scheme and the School Pocket Money fund which are administered by MOE does not need to be applied separately.

sections.label: Mental health awareness and employment
sections.summary: Mental health awareness should start young to reduce stigmatisation, and the Government is proposed to incentivise employers to recruit mental health patients.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: We must have an awareness of mental health and aim to reduce stigmatisation at a very young age so that mental health patients will have more confidence in themselves and have fewer challenges navigating their life in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: I propose for the Government to incentivise employers to recruit mental health patients so that they also have the financial means to take care of themselves.

sections.label: Singapore COVID-19 containment spending
sections.summary: Singapore's Government has acted decisively to contain the virus and is injecting close to $100 billion to contain COVID-19's impact.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Education and Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
sentences.text: In Singapore, the Government has acted decisively to contain the spread of the virus and is injecting close to $100 billion to contain the impact of COVID-19.

sections.label: Resident unemployment rate rise
sections.summary: Due to COVID-19's impact on businesses, the resident unemployment rate rose from 3.3% in March to 3.9% in June, based on preliminary estimates.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Education and Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
sentences.text: Due to the impact of COVID-19 on businesses, our resident unemployment rate rose from 3.3% in March to 3.9% in June this year, based on preliminary estimates.

sections.label: Citizen population age and workforce
sections.summary: In 2019 about 63% of citizens were aged 20 to 64, projected to drop to around 56% in ten years, with the local workforce peaking in the next 10 years.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Education and Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
sentences.text: In 2019, around 63% of our citizen population were between 20 and 64 years old.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Education and Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
sentences.text: Ten years from now, this is projected to drop to around 56%.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Education and Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
sentences.text: With our low birth rate, our local workforce will peak in the next 10 years.

sections.label: Retrenchment: retain Singaporeans over foreigners
sections.summary: In a jobs crisis, employers are urged to favour and retain Singaporean jobseekers over foreigners, aided by government incentives.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Education and Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
sentences.text: In the current crisis where there are not enough jobs for locals, we need to work with employers so that Singaporean jobseekers will be viewed favourably when applying for jobs, especially given the Government incentives such as Jobs Support Scheme, Jobs Growth Incentive, SkillsFuture Enterprise Credit and career conversion programmes.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Education and Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
sentences.text: In circumstances where retrenchment is unavoidable and employers have to choose between foreigners and Singaporeans, I urge employers to lean towards keeping the Singaporean.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Education and Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
sentences.text: In short, if employers must retrench, retain the Singaporean over foreigner.

sections.label: National Jobs Council opportunities
sections.summary: The National Jobs Council is creating close to 100,000 jobs and training opportunities, with 25,000 jobseekers placed as at July.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Education and Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
sentences.text: The National Jobs Council is creating close to 100,000 jobs and training opportunities.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Education and Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
sentences.text: As at July, we have helped place 25,000 jobseekers into new opportunities.

sections.label: Work-Study programmes with Institutes of Higher Learning
sections.summary: Employers can partner with Institutes of Higher Learning on Work-Study programmes modelled after Germany's apprenticeship track.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Education and Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
sentences.text: For employers who are concerned about finding Singaporean workers with relevant skills to fill your business requirements, you can consider partnering with our Institutes of Higher Learning to offer Work-Study programmes and provide structured on-the-job training for potential hires.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Education and Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
sentences.text: These programmes are modelled after the vocational training and apprenticeship track in Germany, where about a third of upper- and post-Secondary students pursue an apprenticeship programme.

sections.label: Singaporean Core and competitiveness
sections.summary: The Government will ensure fair job opportunities and skills for Singaporeans, and Singapore was again ranked the world's most competitive economy.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Education and Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
sentences.text: The Government will do our best to ensure fair opportunities for Singaporeans to get jobs and to support Singaporeans in acquiring skills.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Education and Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
sentences.text: We will spare no effort to strengthen the Singaporean Core and walk the journey with every Singaporean.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Education and Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
sentences.text: Because our people are our only asset and every Singaporean counts.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Today, I would like to talk about a necessary pre-requisite – Singapore must continue to remain competitive.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: This year, Singapore was again ranked the world’s most competitive economy in the annual IMD World Competitiveness ranking.

sections.label: Forgetting Curve experiment result
sections.summary: The Forgetting Curve shows learners forget 75% of what they learnt within six days and 90% within the first month without applying it.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: The result of his experiments was the Forgetting Curve, which shows that learners will forget 75% of what they learnt within six days, 90% within the first month, if they do not apply what they have learnt.

sections.label: Google Career Certificates programme
sections.summary: Google launched six-month Career Certificates, which it considers equivalent to a four-year degree for related roles, costing US$49 monthly.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Last month, Google launched its new Google Career Certificates programme, a collection of six-month long courses designed to help participants get qualifications in high-paying, high-growth job fields without attending university.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Google said, I quote, “We will consider our new career certificates as the equivalent of a four-year Degree for related roles”.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: For example, the IT support certificate costs US$49 a month, or US$300 for six months.

sections.label: SGUnited Traineeships Programme vacancies
sections.summary: Since June 1, over 16,500 vacancies were approved and 1,000 trainees placed in the SGUnited Traineeships Programme.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Since the SGUnited Traineeships Programme started on June 1, more than 16,500 vacancies have been approved and 1,000 trainees placed on the programme.

sections.label: Training stipend for mid-career workers
sections.summary: A $1,200 monthly training stipend is described as a difficult sell for mid-career workers with children and ageing parents.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: With a training stipend of $1,200 a month, for the mid-career worker with children and ageing parents, it is quite a difficult sell. "We are paying you to learn", they are told.

sections.label: Jobseekers facing employment difficulties
sections.summary: The passage describes a retrenched PMET, a banker, a Malay accounts clerk and a graduate facing various job-search difficulties.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: The 50-something PMET who was retrenched when his company was acquired and has gone for countless interviews, only to be told he is “overqualified” for the roles; the 40-something banker who was first put on no-pay leave and then let go because he was told there was no business need, only to see a foreigner take his place two months later while he himself is unable to get back into an industry that is supposed to be still growing; the 30-something Malay accounts clerk who goes through countless job advertisements and interviews only to find that many of the jobs are for Mandarin speakers only, as if computers and ledgers can only speak Chinese; the 20-something graduate, a few years out of school, who goes for interviews for jobs that ask for experience, only to be offered a salary that he believes can only be called a low-ball offer, lower than what a fresh graduate should be making.

sections.label: Fair employment in legal framework
sections.summary: The passage says more can be done to ingrain fair employment in the legal and regulatory framework with TAFEP intervening.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: We have seen that efforts are being made with the recent interventions already highlighted by many of our colleagues today.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: But perhaps we can do more to ensure fair employment is ingrained in the legal and regulatory framework and strongly enforced with TAFEP and other relevant agencies stepping in to intervene on behalf of Singaporeans of all walks of life.

sections.label: Government addressing discrimination and prejudices
sections.summary: The Government has committed to address discrimination and prejudices through enforcement, education and dialogue.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: The Government has committed to address discrimination and prejudices through enforcement, education and dialogue.

sections.label: Business leaders renewing economy together
sections.summary: Business leaders are urged to work with Government, unions and employees on labour market issues and answer the President's call.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: As business leaders, this is our chance to lead a renewal of the economy through working together with the Government, unions and our employees on thorny issues of labour market practices, costs, regulation and discrimination.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: It is time for us to ask ourselves how the organisations we lead can be better corporate statesmen and women, and proactively contribute to addressing critical societal issues in order to strengthen our social contract with society in order to earn the social licence to operate.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Today, in this House, we must answer the President’s call for the Government, Singaporeans and, I will add, companies, to work together, learn faster and to create a better and stronger Singapore on the other side of this crisis.

sections.label: Programme beneficiaries increase
sections.summary: The number of beneficiaries under this programme increased from 30 to 90 people.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: The number of beneficiaries under this programme had increased from 30 to 90 people.

sections.label: Programme continues after Circuit Breaker
sections.summary: Some people still face financial difficulties and the programme will carry on as long as possible.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: While the Circuit Breaker period has ended, some people still face financial difficulties and we plan to carry on with this programme for as long as we can.

sections.label: President Halimah on changed situations
sections.summary: President Halimah Yacob noted the global and domestic situations have changed and there would be no going back to the status quo.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: In her Address, President Halimah Yacob noted that the global and domestic situations have changed and there would be no going back to the status quo.

sections.label: Free vegetable seed packets
sections.summary: NParks increased free vegetable seed packets from 150,000 to 400,000 after an overwhelming response.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: When NParks offered free packets of vegetable seeds, the response was so overwhelming that they had to increase the number of packets from 150,000 to 400,000.

sections.label: Donations from January to May 2020
sections.summary: From January to May 2020 Singaporeans gave about $90 million, roughly equal to all 2019 donations.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: From January to May 2020, Singaporeans gave about $90 million to the Community Chest, Community Foundation of Singapore’s Sayang Sayang Foundation and through Giving.sg.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: The amount received over this period is about equal to the overall donations received by the Community Chest and through the Giving.sg portal for the whole of 2019.

sections.label: MaskForce and Project Belanja donations
sections.summary: MaskForce raised 870,000 mask kits and Project Belanja raised over $2 million for migrant workers.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: Migrant Workers Centre, the Centre for Domestic Employees, the Textiles and Fashion Federation and many donors came together under project “MaskForce” to raise 870,000 mask kits for migrant workers and domestic helpers.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: Project Belanja, organised by several groups, including migrant worker advocacy group It’s Raining Raincoats, the Restaurant Association of Singapore and Blossom World Society, raised over $2 million to deliver more than 460,000 meals to migrant workers, of which more than $1.3 million was contributed by local bank DBS.

sections.label: Digital Ambassadors and hawker e-payment
sections.summary: IMDA set up the Singapore Digital Office and Digital Ambassadors who reached over 16,000 stallholders, with 5,400 signing up for SGQR e-payment.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: For this reason, IMDA established the Singapore Digital Office to make a nationwide push for digitalisation.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: We have recruited Digital Ambassadors who have reached out to over 16,000 stallholders from 112 hawker centres/markets and coffeeshops.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: Five thousand four hundred 5,400 stallholders have already signed up for SGQR e-payment.

sections.label: Helping heartland enterprises go digital
sections.summary: The passage calls for redoubled efforts to help heartland enterprises go digital, citing Pick! parcel lockers, SDO and Digital Ambassadors.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: Such is the daily life of some of our already digitally savvy seniors.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: We can and should redouble our efforts to help heartland enterprises go digital, so that more of the heartland shopping experience can be replicated online or in a mobile-friendly way.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: With the on-going implementation of Pick!, the nationwide parcel locker network, we can also improve on last-mile delivery and collection for e-commerce.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: Add to that the efforts of SDO and our Digital Ambassadors, I believe even more seniors can enjoy the convenience and comfort of being digitally savvy.

sections.label: Digital inclusion in post-COVID-19 society
sections.summary: The speaker hopes care for the vulnerable and helping all go digital will bring inclusivity and preparedness for future challenges like Disease X.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: I hope our care and concern for the vulnerable will bring about a cohesive and heartwarming post-COVID-19 society.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: I also hope that by helping all to go digital, we can bring about more inclusivity, greater advancement, convenience and security in the post-COVID-19 society.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: Such a society would be better prepared for future challenges, including Disease X which Prime Minister Lee mentioned in his speech.

sections.label: Audible pedestrian signals at junctions
sections.summary: Most junctions with traffic lights lack audible pedestrian signals, and where present the chirping sound is turned off at 9 pm or 10 pm.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: For example, most junctions with traffic lights still do not have audible pedestrian signals or APS and for those that do have them, the chirping sound is turned off at 9 pm or 10 pm to avoid disturbing nearby residents.

sections.label: Schemes and anti-discrimination for PWDs
sections.summary: Schemes like the Enabling Employment Credit and Assistive Technology Fund need complementing with public education and anti-discrimination legislation for PWDs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The Government has done well to provide schemes like the Enabling Employment Credit and the Assistive Technology Fund.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: This needs to be complemented with better public education for both employers and the general public in order to clear misconceptions about PWDs in the workplace.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: We also need to ensure that employers do not discriminate on the basis of disability by introducing anti-discrimination legislation.

sections.label: Documents required for public assistance
sections.summary: Applying for public assistance requires applicants to submit at least 10 documents to prove their neediness.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The application for public assistance, for example, requires applicants to submit at least 10 documents to prove their neediness.

sections.label: Centralised disability records system
sections.summary: A centralised system tracking each person's disability could let agencies assess eligibility for disability benefits, with all Government services digital by 2023.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: For PWDs, the Government could create a centralised system that keeps track of each individual's disability, which can be tapped into by various agencies to assess if they are qualified for disability benefits.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: I am glad to learn from the Minister-in-charge of the Smart Nation initiative in his Addendum to the President's Address that all Government services will be digital from end-to-end by 2023.

sections.label: MediSave700 for chronic conditions
sections.summary: MediSave700 lets patients with multiple conditions draw up to $700 yearly from MediSave, up from $500, but some still pay cash.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In the long run, missed or delayed treatments will cost both the patients and the healthcare system more if their conditions worsen and they need to be hospitalised.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: I welcome the introduction of the MediSave700 scheme, which allows patients with multiple conditions to draw up to $700 a year from their MediSave accounts.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: This is up from $500 a year currently.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Patients whose condition is not one of the 20 chronic conditions specified under the Chronic Disease Management Programme (CDMP) or whose treatment costs exceed $700 a year still have to fork out cash for their treatment.

sections.label: Migrant worker job payments
sections.summary: NGOs report migrant workers often pay up to $10,000 for jobs in Singapore and up to $4,000 to agents to renew contracts.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: NGOs have reported that migrant workers often pay as much as $10,000 to secure jobs in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: When their contracts end, some are asked to make cash payments of up to $4,000 to third-party agents to renew their contracts or find subsequent jobs.

sections.label: Delivery rider parking grace period
sections.summary: A delivery rider earning about $6 per delivery faces fines and unclamping charges, prompting a call for 15-minute parking grace.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: Rahman revealed to me that he works up to nine hours a day, six days a week to provide for his family.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: He also shared with me that delivery riders like him typically earn about $6 per delivery, and that he would sometimes lose part of his income due to summons while rushing to complete deliveries and meeting customers’ expectations.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: Because of the nature of their work and the tight deadlines imposed on them, they are often at risk of incurring such penalties – around $70 for fines imposed by LTA enforcement officers and about $300 for unclamping charges imposed by the Managements of shopping malls.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: In this regard, I am seeking the community’s support and the Government’s backing in implementing transitional parking of about 15 minutes grace period for food delivery riders, and also hope that all commercial malls in Singapore can provide designated food delivery pick up points.

sections.label: Carpooling rights for taxi operators
sections.summary: Agreeing transport is part of sustainable development, the speaker suggests MOT explore opening carpooling rights to taxi operators.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: On a national level, I agree with MOT that “transport is part of sustainable development of Singapore.” Apart from looking into improving and expanding the infrastructure of the public transport system, I would also like to suggest that MOT explore opening up carpooling rights to taxi operators so as to maximise the usage capacity of each vehicle.

sections.label: Overhead bridges without lifts
sections.summary: Elderly Woodgrove residents told the speaker that overhead bridges without lifts are useless to them.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: (In Mandarin):   	Mr Speaker, many elderly residents in Woodgrove have told me that overhead bridges without lifts are useless to them.

sections.label: PSLE bands and streaming
sections.summary: The speaker agrees with E W Barker's words on education and applauds MOE's decisions on wider PSLE scoring bands and phasing out Streaming.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: The late E W Barker once said and I quote, “Education should always seek to find and nurture the best in every student, inspiring him to contribute confidently and fully in the area of his own capabilities, rather than made to feel useless and ashamed for not having made it to the top of the school.” I wholeheartedly agree with his words, and I therefore applaud MOE’s decisions that the PSLE will soon have wider scoring bands and Streaming will eventually be phased out.

sections.label: Boosting parents' school confidence
sections.summary: The speaker urges MOE to boost parents' confidence in accessible schools, suggesting a framework akin to Enterprise Singapore's Business Excellence certification.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: In this regard, I humbly urge the MOE to introduce measures to break this trend and think of ways to boost parents’ confidence regarding sending their children to other, more accessible schools.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: One suggestion that MOE can consider is to introduce a framework for all schools in Singapore to adopt and work towards, akin to the Business Excellence certification set forth by Enterprise Singapore to recognise schools that have attained a commendable level of performance to achieve world-class standards of excellence.

sections.label: Lifelong learning law courses
sections.summary: The speaker suggests MOE and MinLaw collaborate on courses for seniors on consumer rights and estate planning, citing $82 million lost to scams.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: In relation to the courses to introduce for lifelong learning, I am suggesting for the MOE and MinLaw to collaborate and introduce courses targeting our seniors to increase their awareness and knowledge on certain aspects of the law, such as consumer rights and the importance of estate planning.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: I was appalled to learn recently that the top 10 most common scams active during the first half of 2020 had stolen an estimated $82 million in that period of time, with e-commerce scams being one of the most commonly reported.

sections.label: Integrating new arrivals
sections.summary: The speaker says Singapore continues to welcome and integrate new arrivals, noting many new citizens and PRs are spouses and family members of Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: At the same time, we continue to welcome and integrate new arrivals who identify with Singapore and our way of life.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: As Minister Josephine Teo had said in her speech, many of our new citizens and PRs are the spouses and family members of Singaporeans.

sections.label: Parliament's oath of allegiance
sections.summary: The speaker recounts a naturalised citizen's greeting and notes that, 55 years on, Members remain unanimous in their oath to preserve, protect and defend the Constitution.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: One day, I met a Caucasian resident who had married a Singaporean and later became a naturalised citizen.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: He approached me, and instead of saying, "Hi", he greeted me with a uniquely Singaporean "Ho seh boh?" Mr Speaker, it has been almost 55 years since the First Parliament session took place.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: Many of the Members who were sworn in at the Old Parliament House are no longer with us today, or have decided to serve in other roles, making way for the younger generations to contribute in Parliament and elevate the country to the next level.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: But what has not changed in all these years, is the unanimity in the conviction of the members, past or present, who have taken the oath of allegiance – to preserve, protect and defend the Constitution of Singapore.

sections.label: Conscience and migrant worker welfare
sections.summary: The speaker cites E W Barker's words on conscience and reassures the House that multiple mechanisms ensure migrant workers' welfare is taken care of.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: The late EW Barker once shared and I quote, "No Member will stray from the straight and narrow path if he always let his conscience be his guide." I will bear these words in mind as I assume the voice of Woodgrove constituents in Parliament and as a PAP backbencher Member of Parliament, speaking out on what is best for Singapore and Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Manpower and Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: I want to reassure the House that with regard to the point that the hon Member made about the exploitation of migrant workers and so on, we have in place multiple mechanisms to ensure that their welfare is being taken care of.

sections.label: Regulation of employment agencies
sections.summary: Singapore-based employment agencies face stringent regulation under the Act, while agencies in migrants' home countries are outside Singapore's jurisdiction.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Manpower and Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: The ones that are based in Singapore – they are subject to very stringent regulation by our Act to make sure that there is a fair benchmark in terms of the payment of the commissions to them for bringing them here.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Manpower and Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: I understand from the High Commissions that there is a separate set of employment agencies that operate outside of Singapore, that is in the home countries of these migrants coming across.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Manpower and Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: This group of employment agencies, we have no jurisdiction over them.

sections.label: Transferring employers near contract end
sections.summary: Workers have been allowed to transfer employers toward the end of their contract during their employment here.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Manpower and Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: The other thing is, we have separately also, through the course of their employment here, allowed for them to transfer employers toward the end of their contract.

sections.label: Ministry planning end-to-end ecosystem
sections.summary: The Ministry is thinking about building an end-to-end eco-system for a more sustainable system moving forward.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Manpower and Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: On top of that, our Ministry, we are now thinking about how to come up with an end-to-end eco-system built because we think that we need to have a more sustainable system, moving forward.

sections.label: Balancing openness and inclusiveness
sections.summary: This depends crucially on how two fundamental tenets, staying open and being inclusive, are balanced.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
sentences.text: In particular, I believe it depends crucially on how we balance two fundamental tenets – staying open and being inclusive.

sections.label: Matching openness with equitable distribution
sections.summary: Efforts to embrace openness must be matched by equal or greater effort for equitable distribution of benefits and access to opportunities to preserve fairness.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
sentences.text: Our efforts to embrace openness must be matched by an equal, if not greater effort, to achieve an equitable distribution of the benefits and the access to opportunities, to preserve a sense of fairness.

sections.label: Trust as foundation for balance
sections.summary: Sustaining the balance between staying open and being inclusive is challenging, especially amid economic uncertainty, so the foundation must be trust.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
sentences.text: Sustaining the dynamic economic and social balance between staying open and being inclusive is challenging in the best of times, what more at a time of economic uncertainty like the present?

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
sentences.text: So, to do so, the foundation must be trust.

sections.label: Open inclusive economy alignment
sections.summary: The speaker says words and actions must align, and Singapore has built an open, inclusive economy welcoming competitive enterprises and talent.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
sentences.text: What we say, but also what we actively advocate in this House and ultimately what we do, must all be aligned – because they are all keenly watched.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
sentences.text: We have painstakingly built an open and inclusive economy – that is able to create opportunities for Singaporeans by welcoming competitive enterprises and talent.

sections.label: Leong Mun Wai DBS CEO remark
sections.summary: The speaker was troubled by NCMP Leong Mun Wai lamenting that Singapore lacks a homegrown CEO for DBS.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
sentences.text: In contrast, I was troubled when Non-Constituency Member of Parliament Leong Mun Wai lamented that we do not have a homegrown CEO for DBS.

sections.label: FTAs attract foreign companies
sections.summary: 25 FTAs give companies preferential access to economies over 85% of global GDP and helped attract over 750 foreign companies.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
sentences.text: Our network of 25 FTAs provides our companies preferential access to economies that together, represent more than 85% of global GDP.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
sentences.text: They also have rules that protect our companies' investments.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
sentences.text: This combination of opportunity and stability, among other things has helped attract over 750 foreign companies to establish their regional headquarters in Singapore with nearly 30,000 employees.

sections.label: Infocomm sector growth and jobs
sections.summary: From 2011 to 2018 the infocomm sector grew 7.1% yearly, creating an estimated 22,000 jobs with median gross salary about $6,000.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
sentences.text: From 2011 to 2018, our infocomm sector registered a 7.1% average annual growth rate in nominal value added to our economy.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
sentences.text: An estimated 22,000 jobs were created in the last three years alone with a median gross salary of about $6,000.

sections.label: Google Skills Ignition SG programme
sections.summary: Google collaborated on Skills Ignition SG, which will train up to 3,000 Singaporeans for digital marketing and cloud technology roles.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
sentences.text: Google has collaborated with us on the programme Skills Ignition SG, which will train up to 3,000 Singaporeans for roles in growth areas like digital marketing and cloud technology.

sections.label: Digital economy jobs and skills
sections.summary: The digital economy offers more than 18,000 jobs and skills opportunities under the SGUnited Jobs and Skills Package.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
sentences.text: Indeed, the digital economy is a bright spot, offering more than 18,000 jobs and skills opportunities under the SGUnited Jobs and Skills Package.

sections.label: ICT graduates and tech job placements
sections.summary: AUs trained about 1,000 local ICT graduates yearly, now about 2,800 undergraduates, and TeSA placed about 6,600 Singaporeans in tech jobs.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
sentences.text: In the last three years, our Autonomous Universities (AUs) trained about 1,000 local ICT graduates annually.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
sentences.text: This has almost trebled and today, the undergraduates' enrollment collectively, is about 2,800.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
sentences.text: The Tech Skills Accelerator or TeSA progamme has successfully placed about 6,600 Singaporeans in tech jobs to date.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
sentences.text: Looking ahead, IMDA is working to place and train an additional 5,500 Singaporeans in good tech jobs over the next two to three years in functions like digital marketing, software engineering, cybersecurity and data analytics, including 2,500 mid-career professionals aged 40 and above.

sections.label: Low demand for live broadcasts
sections.summary: Demand for live broadcasts, even of major speeches, is generally low, at only 10% of free-to-air television news.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
sentences.text: Demand for such live broadcasts, even of major speeches, is generally low – only 10% of that of free-to-air television news, for example.

sections.label: Live streaming of Parliamentary proceedings
sections.summary: The Government agrees in principle to live streaming Parliamentary proceedings, and the Ministry will study technical and implementation details.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
sentences.text: Nevertheless, we also note the global and technological trends which have made online streaming commonplace and seen legislatures live streaming their proceedings in many countries.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
sentences.text: The Government therefore agrees in principle to the live streaming of Parliamentary proceedings.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
sentences.text: My Ministry will study the technical and implementation details.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
sentences.text: Our aim, as always, will be to achieve transparency, accountability and accessibility while preserving the integrity and dignity of Parliamentary proceedings.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Since the issue has been brought up every now and then, my colleagues and I have reflected on the Government's reasons for not proceeding with live broadcasts.

sections.label: Dignity of Parliamentary proceedings
sections.summary: The speaker says all in the House are committed to preserving the dignity and integrity of Parliamentary proceedings, but other countries' experience is not optimistic.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: So, I just wanted to make that point and hope it provides some assurance for the Minister in his deliberations on this matter.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: And I think we all accept that all of us in this House are committed to ensuring that the dignity and integrity of Parliamentary proceedings is preserved, notwithstanding how it is conveyed to a larger audience.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: However, I think it is important to also bear in mind the experience of other countries does not give us a lot of reason to be optimistic, in terms of the tone and nature of debates in Parliament and the impact such streaming or broadcasting will have.

sections.label: PSP on population and foreigners
sections.summary: PSP wants population growth slowed, a cap on foreigners at least for the immediate future, and ensured skills transfer.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: PSP would like to see this population growth being slowed down, would to see a cap on the foreigners, at least for the immediate future, and to ensure there is skills transfer.

sections.label: Evolution of manpower policy
sections.summary: Reviewing and evolving policy predates the Fourteenth and Thirteenth Parliaments and is an ongoing, evolutionary effort responding to economic and population needs.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: The process of reviewing and evolving our policy predates the Fourteenth Parliament, predates the Thirteenth Parliament.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: It is, in fact, an on-going venture and if you look at any one of our policies – and the foreign worker policy, the manpower policy is no exception to this – it is an evolutionary effort because it has to respond to the economic environment, the population's needs and concerns; and we have to then adapt and move along.

sections.label: Safeguarding Singaporeans' interests, FX trading
sections.summary: He says failing to safeguard Singaporeans' interests may lead to ridicule, and recalls tracing Singapore's start as an FX trading centre from the 1960s.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
sentences.text: In fact, if we failed to do certain things to safeguard the interests of Singaporeans, I am afraid we may be laughed at.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: I think I have to reiterate some of the things that I have said on Tuesday, when I explained and traced back – and I went into some detail – how from the 1960s, Singapore started as a foreign exchange or FX trading centre.

sections.label: Foreign expertise and local talent grooming
sections.summary: The process began 40 to 50 years ago by bringing in foreign expertise and grooming local talent, with many locals rising to senior positions.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: That whole process started 40 to 50 years ago.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: That process started when we brought in foreign expertise and then put in a lot of effort to groom local talent.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: Grow our own timber, learn from the foreign expertise and from there, many of our own rose up to take senior positions.

sections.label: No quota for Singaporean CEO
sections.summary: This has been done for decades, but no stage was reached of setting a quota requiring a Singaporean-born CEO to declare success.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: That is what we have been doing for decades.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: But we have never reached a stage where we say the only way to achieve this – set the quota.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: It must be a Singaporean CEO and born here, before we declare it a success.

sections.label: Investment concerns: local connections, talent
sections.summary: In private equity and venture capital investment, they are more concerned whether a company has local connections and enough local talents, including the CEO.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
sentences.text: When we do our investments, we actually look more at – of course, now, we are talking about private equity investment, venture capital investment.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
sentences.text: We are more concerned whether the company is – when we want to invest in a particular market – we are more concerned whether the company really has the local connections and so by implication, whether they have enough local talents, including the CEO on the company.

sections.label: Inaccurate memory and Grace Fu letter
sections.summary: He says his memory and attribution were inaccurate, and cites a 15 May 2020 letter from former Leader of the House Grace Fu's press secretary on live broadcasts.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
sentences.text: My memory on the matter was inaccurate and that attribution to him was also inaccurate.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
sentences.text: I refer to a letter sent by the press secretary of the former Leader of the House, Minister Grace Fu, and this is dated 15 May 2020.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
sentences.text: This is what was said in that letter to the press: "Live broadcast of Parliament risks turning the House into a form of theatre and do not add to the transparency," the spokesman for the Leader of the House Grace Fu said on Friday, 15 May.

sections.label: Incorrect attribution recorded, Sitting suspended
sections.summary: He puts his incorrect attribution on record, suspends the Sitting and will take the Chair at 4.00 pm.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
sentences.text: And to put on record, my incorrect attribution.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: I suspend the Sitting and will take the Chair at 4.00 pm.

sections.label: Singapore as nation by design
sections.summary: Singapore's racial harmony, economic growth and international standing result from deliberation, and the speaker sees an opportunity to become a nation by design through empowered people.

sentences.speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
sentences.text: The Singapore we have today is a nation by design.

sentences.speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
sentences.text: At the SUTD Ministerial Forum in 2018, our Prime Minister Lee noted that nothing we have in Singapore is by chance.

sentences.speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
sentences.text: Our racial harmony, economic growth, international standing are the products of deep deliberation of issues, leading to options that were proto-typed, tested and delivered.

sentences.speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
sentences.text: Without using the term, our founding fathers employed design thinking approaches to overcome the many impossibilities to be the Singapore of today.

sentences.speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
sentences.text: I believe we now have the opportunity to become a nation by design, not just through the collective efforts of our leaders, but also by the collective efforts of a people empowered to live a life by design.

sections.label: Space for vocational interests
